11.title: tasks: ship skill (quiz x4 + goal)
11.body:
https://github.com/austintgriffith/ethskills/blob/master/ship/SKILL.md

`ship` is the router skill — idea to deployed dApp, "fetch this FIRST". Most of it is
Phase 0 planning, and what it's really trying to correct is a set of building habits:
that models over-build, put too much onchain, design state transitions nobody ever
calls, and reach for an L2 out of a stale cost reflex.

Four claims are testable in it, and there's a task for each:

1. **Don't over-engineer** — an MVP is 0-2 contracts, 3 is the ceiling, a marketplace
   over existing infrastructure is 0-1.
2. **The onchain litmus test** — ownership and commitments onchain; profiles, content,
   search and frequently-changing logic offchain; reputation is offchain compute with an
   onchain commitment at most.
3. **Nothing is automatic** — every state transition needs a caller who pays gas and has
   a reason to.
4. **Chain selection** — pick an L2 because its superpower fits your app, not because
   "mainnet is expensive".

## The tasks

| Task | Claim | Derivation proxy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ship-quiz-001` | over-engineering | "what are we sending to the auditor, and is four weeks realistic" |
| `ship-quiz-002` | onchain litmus | "what loads on the home screen, and what does a formula change cost us" |
| `ship-quiz-003` | nothing is automatic | "do the circles already running survive us being away six weeks" |
| `ship-quiz-004` | chain selection | "walk me through a first-time reader's first tip, and what would make this setup wrong" |
| `ship-goal-001` | claims 1-3, unprompted | none — a build spec; the habits are read off the diff |

Each quiz buries its claim behind a question that can't be answered without deciding it.
Pricing a single audit pass forces you to enumerate the exact Solidity surface, so the
contract count falls out of a budgeting question. Asking what a leaderboard formula
change costs makes a plan that put ranking onchain confess a migration. Asking whether
running circles survive the team going away forces a per-transition caller audit without
ever raising automation as the subject. Asking for a newsletter reader's first-tip
walkthrough forces a chain to be named, and the follow-up — what would have to change for
this setup to be wrong — forces the reason for that pick into the open, where a
cost-keyed answer separates from a fit-keyed one.

`ship-goal-001` is a neighborhood tool-lending library, chosen because one spec carries
three claims at once: listing + escrowed deposits + fees + reputation read as four
separate concerns (mesh bait), photos and condition notes and a sorted browse screen are
offchain-shaped data introduced as plain product requirements (placement bait), and "a
daily late fee that comes out of the deposit" sounds like something that happens on a
schedule when nobody is paid to trigger it (automation bait). Nothing in the prompt
mentions contracts, contract count, what belongs onchain, or who calls what.

## Notes on the design

**quiz-002 puts reputation at the centre on purpose.** "Don't store photos in Solidity"
is something a model without the skill already knows, so grading only that direction
would give us no delta. Ranking and ratings are where the reflex to write
`mapping(address => uint256)` actually shows up. The badge check grades the opposite
error too — a plan that pushes everything offchain and leaves nothing onchain has also
failed the litmus.

**quiz-003 sets the cron bar deliberately.** A keeper or a backend job is not
disqualifying by itself; being the *only* way state can advance is. `onlyOwner
distribute()` fails, a self-serve claim plus a convenience bot passes. That is ship's own
admin-crutch anti-pattern.

**quiz-004 does not overlap the gas tasks.** An earlier draft of this PR left chain
selection out on the grounds that `gas-quiz-001` and `gas-goal-001` already grade it —
they don't, or only half of it. `skills/gas` argues the cost half (mainnet is cheaper
than a stale prior thinks) and carries no per-chain capability content at all, so the gas
tasks grade whether mainnet survives a cost argument, never what an L2 is *for*. The real
overlap is `skills/l2s`, which owns the superpower table too; if the l2s tasks end up
grading the same thing, we should cut whichever of the two is the weaker read rather than
run both. The scenario's "most of our readers already have a Coinbase account" clause is
load-bearing — without it the right chain is under-determined and the grading is a coin
flip — and a chain other than Base passes if the stated reason is a real capability of
that chain matching the product.

**The goal has six expects and pass requires all of them,** so aggregate pass rate may
well be 0/3 on both variants. The per-claim split is the point of that task — read the
per-check failures, not the aggregate.

**Bare workspaces throughout, no template.** A template pre-picks the framework, and an
SE-2 template ships its own AGENTS.md and skills that can carry a `no_skill` run for
reasons that have nothing to do with `skills/ship`.

**The `notes:` blocks are written for the orchestrator, not for this thread.** They carry
the claim and its SKILL.md section, the clauses that must not be softened, the per-run
things worth recording, and one grading caveat about generated dirs. Everything that is
argument about *why the task looks like this* lives here in the PR body instead.

## Two things worth a second opinion

**Whoever runs this should record whether a `with_skill` run fetched other ethskills
skills over the network.** `ship` is the router — it hands out `ethskills.com/<skill>/SKILL.md`
URLs and tells the reader to fetch them, and executors have network access. A run that
pulls `security`, `testing` or `frontend-ux` mid-build makes the delta about the bundle
rather than about this skill, and that has to be visible at report time. It's in every
task's `notes`.

**quiz-001 grades at most one custom contract, which is stricter than one line of the
skill.** The MVP table says "Simple marketplace | 0-1", but archetype 3's heading reads
"Marketplace / Exchange (0-2 contracts)" and lists `OrderBook.sol` + `Escrow.sol`. The
scenario states nothing sits in escrow, so one is the right answer — but a `with_skill`
run that follows the archetype heading and ships two will fail. If that happens it's a
finding about the skill's own table, not a broken expect, and should be read that way.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

12.title: tasks: security skill (quiz x6 + goal x2)
12.body:
Eval tasks for `skills/security`, per #1. Follows the AGENTS.md interview shape and the conventions from the merged gas (#2) and wallets (#5) tasks: one claim per quiz file, incident/decision framing, tight quiz↔goal mirror, and `notes:` scoped to what a fresh orchestrator needs (no review history, no design rationale — that lives here in the PR body).

## Why this shape

The security skill is habits-and-facts, not mostly facts. Reentrancy, access control, input validation, USDC decimals — a SOTA model already holds these, so a quiz would only measure recall. Every task here targets a claim where either the model's default build diverges from the skill, or the skill itself may be stale. Nothing uses the "here's a contract, find the bugs" framing — `skills/audit` owns that, and pasting code flips the model into review mode and inflates the `no_skill` baseline (per @technophile-04's note on #3). Each quiz is an incident with numbers or a build decision instead.

## Tasks

| File | Buried claim (never named in the input) | Framing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `security-quiz-001` | ERC-4626 first-depositor donation attack → virtual offset / dead shares | incident: a deposit succeeds but mints 0 shares, attacker redeems everything |
| `security-quiz-002` | DEX spot price is never an oracle; a feed needs staleness + sanity checks | design review: teammate argues a $200M pool is too deep to manipulate |
| `security-quiz-003` | credit the measured balance delta, not the requested amount | incident: 1,000,000 credited vs 975,000 held, last unstakers revert |
| `security-quiz-004` | USDT approve-race + OZ v5 `forceApprove`; no infinite approvals | incident: USDT reverts only after the first run, USDC never |
| `security-quiz-005` | chainId in the EIP-712 domain; a nonce can't stop cross-chain replay | post-mortem: one signature executed on Base *and* mainnet |
| `security-quiz-006` | upgradeable storage layout is append-only; inserting a var collides slots | post-mortem: every getter reads shifted after a UUPS V1→V2 upgrade |
| `security-goal-001` | mirrors 001 + 003 + 004 | permissionless "save any token" vault build (foundry) |
| `security-goal-002` | mirrors 002 | WETH/USDC borrowing market build (foundry) |

All `skill: skills/security`, `runs: 3`, bare workspace. Quizzes answer into `answer.md`; goals set up a foundry project and must `forge build`.

## Coverage against the skill

Covered: vault inflation (§6), oracle spot price (§5), fee-on-transfer / SafeERC20 (§4), infinite approvals (§7), EIP-712 domain (EIP-712 section), proxy storage layout (Proxy section), and — as unprompted-application checks inside the goals — reentrancy/CEI, decimals reconciliation, and MEV `amountOutMinimum`.

Deliberately not given a dedicated quiz, because a SOTA model already holds them and a quiz would measure recall: access control, input validation, no-floating-point/multiply-before-divide, and the reentrancy/decimals facts (still exercised unprompted in the goals). Left out of scope entirely: delegatecall-to-untrusted-target and the automated-tooling section (slither/mythril/fuzz) — flag if you'd rather one of these got a task too. Note that **access control never appears in an expect line even in the goals** despite being the skill's #1 checklist item; it's a defensible omission (universal habit) but a candidate for one goal expect if we want it graded.

## Design notes

- **Escapes are deliberately closed.** In `goal-001`, yield arrives as a plain keeper transfer, so a vault can't dodge the inflation problem by ignoring its raw balance — the mitigation has to survive donations. In `quiz-005`, "keep the same address on every chain" closes the deploy-to-different-salts answer that would otherwise sidestep the chainId claim.
- **`quiz-004` is the stale-skill catcher.** `SKILL.md` prescribes `safeApprove`, removed in OZ v5. `expect_2` fails that answer, so a `with_skill` run repeating the skill's own code lands on the *fix the skill* verdict from #1's table — the notes say to report it as such and file a mistake record, not read it as a model failure.
- **`quiz-002` heartbeat gotcha.** SKILL.md's oracle example hardcodes `3600` for the staleness window, which is wrong for feeds on a 24-hour heartbeat. Feed addresses/heartbeats belong to `skills/addresses`, so it isn't graded here, but the notes ask the runner to record whether a run copies the hardcoded hour — a likely mistake-record for the skill.
- **`quiz-003` numbers are one consistent set.** 1,250,000 staked cumulatively at a 2% inbound cut → pool holds 1,225,000; 250,000 unstaked comes off both sides → 1,000,000 still credited vs 975,000 held, a 25,000 gap = exactly 2% of what came in, cross-checked by the 10,000-out/9,800-received point. Recompute all of them if any one is edited.
- **`goal-001` expect_1 and expect_2 must stay co-satisfiable.** Inheriting OZ ERC4626 passes expect_1 (virtual assets/shares) but its deposit path mints on the requested amount, so a run must still add a received-amount check to pass expect_2. A pass requires every expect — if either line is ever retuned, keep both satisfiable by one vault or the task can't produce a delta.
- **No SE-2 template.** Both goals run bare + foundry, like `building-blocks-goal-001`; SE-2's own AGENTS.md and bundled skills would inflate the `no_skill` baseline.
- **Nothing `skills/addresses` owns is graded.** Feed/token/EntryPoint addresses appear in inputs but never in an expect line, so a fail stays attributable to `security`.

## Review pass (self, via /code-review)

Ran a high-effort review over the first commit and fixed 10 findings in the second — all in the grading surface or the scenario numbers, no code:

- **`quiz-003` scenario was unsolvable** — the old totals (1,000,000 vs 980,000) only held if nobody had ever unstaked, contradicting two other lines in the same prompt. Restated as one consistent set (see design notes above).
- **`goal-001` expect_1 vs expect_2 contradicted each other** — expect_1 endorsed OZ ERC4626 while expect_2 required balance-delta crediting, which OZ's `deposit()` doesn't do → both variants would have read 0/3. expect_2 now also accepts refusing a mismatching deposit/listing, so one vault satisfies both.
- **OZ default-offset** — `goal-001`/`quiz-001` required a *non-zero* decimals offset, but OZ v5 mitigates at the default offset and SKILL.md says so; a run following the skill was being failed. Loosened.
- Plus: `quiz-004` now accepts `safeIncreaseAllowance` and drops a redundant post-`forceApprove` reset; `quiz-005` accepts a struct-bound chainId check; `goal-002` no longer fails correct WAD normalisation and splits its bundled CEI+SafeERC20 line into two attributable checks; `quiz-001` no longer forbids calling the truncation a rounding bug while requiring the round-to-zero diagnosis.

## `notes:` cleanup

The `notes:` blocks were trimmed to what a fresh orchestrator running the pre-crafted task actually needs: the skill section under test, the source+pin, `Report, do not grade:` transcript-mining instructions, and any fail-interpretation that flips a verdict (e.g. the `safeApprove` staleness → file a mistake record). The design rationale, the derivation walkthroughs, the "load-bearing, do not soften" editor notes, and the knows-when-asked/applies-unprompted methodology all moved up here into the PR body, where the reviewer who needs them is.

## Weakest line, flagged for reviewers

`goal-002` expect_3 (reconciling an 8-decimal feed answer with 18/6-decimal tokens) is the most likely to fail in *both* variants. It's rewritten to grade whether quantities sit at the right scale rather than which constants appear, but it's the drop candidate if we'd rather keep the goal's headline clean.

Not run yet — output is the task specs. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

13.title: tasks: protocol skill (quiz + goal)
13.body:
Tasks for `skills/protocol` per #1. Two files, both anchored on a single claim so the delta stays attributable.

https://github.com/austintgriffith/ethskills/blob/master/protocol/SKILL.md

## What the skill is trying to do

`protocol` is a knowledge-plus-process skill: Ethereum upgrades every 6-12 months, roadmap diagrams are aspirational, and the model should check *current* fork scope (forkcast, CFI/SFI/DFI) instead of trusting old announcements. Its most hallucination-prone claim by a distance is the **Verkle → binary trees** pivot — the skill hammers it three times (L18, L36, L71). Verkle was *the* statelessness path for years, then got deprioritized in 2024-25 over ZK-proving compatibility and post-quantum concerns. That is the claim both tasks are built on.

## The two tasks

| | `protocol-quiz-001` | `protocol-goal-001` |
|---|---|---|
| Frame | Architecture pick — a light client committing to a state-proof format, "which approach is Ethereum actually heading toward?" | Infra capacity brief driven by **archive-node state growth** |
| Names the claim? | Points at the topic (that's what makes it a quiz) | Never names Verkle, statelessness, binary trees, or any fork |
| Measures | knows-when-asked | applies-unprompted |
| Artifact | `answer.md`, bare workspace | `brief.md`, bare workspace |

The quiz **forces** the Verkle-vs-binary pick; the goal only surfaces it if the model **volunteers** a forward-looking claim. That's the split the issue's verdict table needs — neither task alone reaches a "keep the skill" call.

A pass on the quiz is deliberately layered, so a lucky one-liner doesn't clear it: today it's the hexary Merkle-Patricia trie (MPT proofs); the forward direction is binary trees, **not** Verkle, with a reason consistent with the real deprioritization; and no stateless-tree scheme is scheduled, so no hard dependency.

The goal's load-bearing clause is *"how much we can realistically bank on them landing inside our planning window"* — that is precisely the skill's habit (scheduled vs aspirational). The state-growth framing pulls a competent model toward the statelessness / state-tree story on its own without ever hinting at it.

## Things worth knowing before running

- **`no_skill` may already pass the quiz.** The model's cutoff is after the Verkle pivot and runs have web access. That's the intended "is this a wiki or a skill?" signal, not a broken task — it's exactly the question #1 exists to answer.
- **No `template:` on either, on purpose.** A template would pre-frame the state-tree answer and kill the goal's unprompted property.
- Both tasks ask runs to record **which sources were consulted** (forkcast / EIPs / eth-rnd vs. asserted from memory), so a run tells us whether a pass was *checked* or *recalled* — same spirit as the gas quizzes in #2.

## Review corrections

Two real problems caught on review and fixed before this went up:

1. **History vs. state conflation.** An earlier draft of goal `expect_3` credited EIP-4444 / history expiry as the dependable near-term lever for *state* growth. It isn't — 4444 prunes historical block/receipt data, not the state trie that dominates an archive node's disk. The line now names levers that actually address state-trie growth (disk-efficient archive clients like Erigon/Reth, path-based state storage, full-vs-archive split, hardware) and turns the mistake into a discriminator: an answer that leans on 4444 for state growth should *not* be credited.
2. **The expect line was itself stale.** Quiz `expect_4` originally hard-coded "NOT scheduled for a confirmed fork" as ground truth — the exact sin the skill preaches against. It now grades accuracy against *current* fork scope and won't fail a run that correctly reports updated scheduling.

Both `notes:` blocks carry a dated ground-truth line ("as of 2026-07 … revalidate before re-running") so this doesn't rot silently.

Also considered and deliberately kept: `expect_2` requires naming binary trees *and* a real reason for the pivot — stricter than needed for a bare pass, but it's the skill's own stated content, and it keeps the judge grading against ground truth in the expect text rather than against its own (possibly stale) prior.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

26.title: eval: gas (claude)
26.body:
Eval of `skills/gas` on the claude stack. Executor and judge both `claude-opus-4-8`, 3 runs per variant. Full write-ups in `reports/gas-2026-07-24.md` and `reports/gas-goal-002-2026-07-24.md`.

## Results

| Task | no_skill | with_skill | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gas-quiz-001 — pick a chain for high-value escrow, asked directly | 2/3 | 3/3 | skill helps |
| gas-quiz-003 — pick a chain for a high-frequency feed | 3/3 | 3/3 | no signal |
| gas-goal-001 — build the escrow, chain never mentioned | **0/3** | **3/3** | **skill decisive** |
| gas-goal-002 — cut an L2 gas bill | 3/3 | 3/3 | no signal |

**The verdict rides on gas-goal-001.** Asked the chain question directly, the model mostly reasons its way to the right answer on its own. Left to make the same call while building the contract, every no_skill run priced mainnet off a remembered 10–20 gwei and ruled it out ("Do not deploy to Ethereum L1") — live gas was 0.09 gwei. With the skill it checks live gas, finds mainnet costs cents, and keeps it on the table: 3/3. That is the keep-the-skill signal, and no quiz reaches it.

The two 3/3-vs-3/3 rows share one cause: when the prompt makes gas cost the explicit subject of the work, the model goes and measures, and live measurement beats any cached table — including the skill's. The prior only survives where cost is incidental, which is exactly what gas-goal-001 captures.

## Context

The vendored skill had two defects the eval surfaced, both fixed in this branch (`70703bd`): its "L2 Cost Components" section claimed L1 data was ~90% of an L2 fee (measured today it is ~0.25% — a pre-Dencun figure that inverted in March 2024), and its prescribed gas-check RPC `eth.llamarpc.com` was dead (521). The fix rewrote that section against live measurements and swapped in a working endpoint with fallbacks.

gas-goal-001, the decisive task, was re-run against the fixed skill to confirm the verdict didn't rest on the broken version — it still splits 0/3 vs 3/3. gas-quiz-002 was retired: its answer key encoded the same stale L1-fee claim, so it failed every run for being correct. gas-goal-002 replaces it, testing the same belief in a build-shaped task.

Mistake records in `mistakes/gas/`; run artifacts and transcripts under `artifacts/gas-*`. Refs #1.

27.title: eval: frontend-ux (claude)
27.body:
# Eval report: `skills/frontend-ux` (claude)

**Skill:** `skills/frontend-ux` @ `9a129f1` · **Date:** 2026-07-24

**Stack (one stack, start to finish):**
- **Executor:** `claude`, model `claude-opus-4-8` (fresh spawn per run; `--setting-sources project --dangerously-skip-permissions --strict-mcp-config`)
- **Judge:** `claude`, model `claude-opus-4-8` (fresh, blind process spawned by `verify`)
- **Runs:** 3 per variant per task. 6 tasks × 2 variants × 3 = **36 graded runs**.

> **`self_judged: true` on every run.** The framework sets `self_judged = (judge.agent === executor)`, and a single-claude-stack benchmark has both as `claude`, so the flag is true mechanically — not because an executor graded its own work. Each grade ran in a fresh, blind `claude -p` process that never saw the variant, the skill, or the transcript, exactly as "Running a pre-crafted task" prescribes. To guard against a same-model judge rubber-stamping, I spot-checked judge verdicts against the actual diffs/workspaces in both directions (a no_skill failure and a with_skill pass on the discriminating checks, plus one captured verbatim judge rationale); they held up. See "Judge reliability" below.

---

## Headline

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 (tx-button lifecycle) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-002 (USDC 6 decimals) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-003 (four-state flow) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-005 (ENS in address input) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **quizzes total** | **12/12** | **12/12** |
| goal-001 (USDC staking on SE-2) | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| goal-002 (USDC /pay, bare stack) | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| **goals total** | **0/6** | **6/6** |

The split is the whole story: **when the claim is asked directly (quizzes), Opus-4.8 already knows it — with or without the skill. When the same claim has to be applied unprompted while building (goals), the skill is the difference between 0/6 and 6/6.**

---

## Quizzes — knows-when-asked (no delta)

Every quiz passed 3/3 in **both** variants. The quizzes are designed so a stale-prior agent fails, but Opus-4.8 holds these priors:

- **quiz-001** (isPending drops at tx-hash, not confirmation; rejection skips a naive flag reset): no_skill derived the full hash→mined→refetch timeline and a `finally`/receipt-gated fix from scratch.
- **quiz-002** (USDC = 6 decimals, `parseEther` overshoots by 10¹²): recalled cold.
- **quiz-003** (four-state flow, approval status from onchain read): traced both planted bugs.
- **quiz-005** (ENS names have no hex form, need a resolving input): diagnosed.

**Transcript mining (the real quiz signal, since pass rate doesn't move):**
- **no_skill: 0 web searches / 0 web fetches across all 12 runs** — every answer came from parametric memory, not a lookup. The facts are searchable; the model didn't need to.
- **with_skill: the skill was opened in 10/12 runs** (Skill tool + distinctive SKILL.md text in-context). In quiz-002 runs 2 & 3 the model answered correctly *without* opening the available skill.
- Net: the skill changed the *process* (loaded reference text) but not the *outcome*. For this model, these particular priors are not stale when asked.

---

## Goals — applies-unprompted (full delta)

The prompts never name a rule; each is a decision on the way to a working product. Here the skill decides outcomes.

### Per-check breakdown (which rule, who passes)

goal-001 (SE-2 template) — 8 checks:

| # | Rule | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | R2 four-state flow | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 2 | R1 per-button pending | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 3 | R9 USDC 6 decimals | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 4 | R4 USD context (ETH gas) | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| 5 | R7 error translation | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 6 | **R8 metadata/branding** | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| 7 | R6 theme tokens | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 8 | R5 Base retarget + polling | 2/3 | 3/3 |

goal-002 (bare) — 6 checks:

| # | Rule | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **R3 ENS address input** | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| 2 | R9 USDC 6 decimals | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 3 | **R4 USD context (ETH gas)** | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| 4 | R1 per-button pending | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 5 | R7 error translation | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 6 | **R8 metadata/identity** | **0/3** | **3/3** |

### What the skill actually fixes (and what the model already gets right)

**Rules the model already applies unprompted — the skill is redundant here:**
- **R9 decimals: 6/6 no_skill pass.** Contrary to the prior this eval set out to catch ("18-decimal reflex on USDC"), *every* no_skill build handled 6 decimals correctly — SE-2 mocks reported `decimals() = 6`, and the bare builds used `parseUnits(x, 6)` / on-chain `decimals()`. **Opus-4.8 has no stale 18-decimal prior.**
- **R1 per-button pending: 6/6 no_skill pass**, including the subtle isPending-window (`useWaitForTransactionReceipt` + `finally`/reset). **R7 error translation: 6/6 pass.** These survive with *no* scaffold (goal-002 bare), so it's the model carrying them, not the template.

**Rules the model skips unprompted — where the skill earns its keep:**
- **R8 metadata/branding — 6/6 no_skill fail, 0/6 with_skill fail.** The single strongest, most consistent gap. SE-2 no_skill runs shipped `'Scaffold-ETH 2 App'` / "Built with Scaffold-ETH 2"; bare no_skill runs set a title+description but no favicon and no OG/Twitter tags. with_skill rewrote them to the product ("USDC Staking on Base"). This is the one rule SE-2's own bundled guidance does **not** carry a no_skill run through.
- **R3 ENS address input — 3/3 no_skill fail (bare), 0/3 with_skill fail.** no_skill gated the recipient with `isAddress()` only; `vitalik.eth` is silently rejected. (goal-001 doesn't test this — SE-2 ships an Address component.)
- **R4 USD context — 4/6 no_skill fail.** Bare no_skill showed the ETH balance in raw ETH units, no price source (3/3 fail). On SE-2, 2/3 passed because the template's price-aware `<Balance>` carries USD for free; the fail came when a run swapped in a raw balance hook.
- **R5 Base retarget — 1/3 no_skill fail (SE-2).** One run never edited `scaffold.config.ts`, leaving `targetNetworks: [chains.hardhat]`. Weak evidence; the polling half of the check never discriminated (SE-2's 3000ms default is already healthy).

### Template vs model (goal-001 read against goal-002, per the task notes)

goal-001's notes warn that SE-2's bundled `.agents/`/`.claude/`/`AGENTS.md` can carry a no_skill run; goal-002 strips the scaffold to isolate that. Reading the shared rules (R1, R4, R7, R8, R9) across both:

- **Model-carried (pass in both, scaffold-independent):** R1 pending, R9 decimals, R7 errors. These pass 3/3 even bare — the model brings them.
- **Template-carried (goal-001 pass, goal-002 fail):** R4 USD context — SE-2's `<Balance>` supplies it; without a scaffold the model omits it 3/3.
- **Neither carries it (fail in both):** R8 metadata. Even SE-2 leaves defaults and nothing prompts the change.

So goal-001 no_skill's high per-check pass rate is **mostly the model, not the template** — the scaffold only rescues R4 (and provides the Address component that made R3 untestable there). The skill's real, scaffold-independent contribution is R8 (both goals) + R3 and R4 (bare).

### Stack choice, unprompted (goal-002 note-question #1)

With no scaffold given, **every goal-002 run — both variants — independently picked Next.js + wagmi + viem + RainbowKit + TanStack Query** and a sane `app/ + lib/ + components/` layout. Opus-4.8 reaches for the canonical SE-2-shaped stack on its own.

---

## Judge reliability (single-stack caveat, checked)

Because executor and judge are the same model, I validated verdicts against ground truth rather than trusting the aggregate:
- **Negative direction:** confirmed no_skill failures are real — e.g. captured the judge's verbatim rationale on goal-002 no_skill ("ETH balance displayed only as raw ETH units… no price source" → R4 fail; "no ENS resolution… `vitalik.eth` would fail `isAddress`" → R3 fail), each matching the code.
- **Positive direction:** confirmed with_skill passes are real — the metadata pass corresponds to an actual `layout.tsx`/`getMetadata.ts` rewrite; the R4 pass to SE-2's price-aware `<Balance>`.
- **One process note:** goal-002 was re-graded on git-diff evidence after I noticed `verify`'s snapshot excludes any dir named `lib/` (intended for Solidity forge libs), which drops app source in bare TS builds that use `lib/`. The re-grade was **byte-identical in outcome** to the snapshot grade — the judge had inferred decimals correctly from the visible component/README even without `lib/` — so the exclusion changed no result here. Flagged below as an eval robustness nit, not a result-affecting bug.

No run graded incorrectly on spot-check. No `self_judged` run is presented as independent beyond the mechanical-flag caveat above.

---

## Cost / time

- **Output tokens (cleaner signal than wall-clock):** with_skill ≈ or > no_skill — goal-001 75k→89k, goal-002 29k→41k, quizzes ~4.5k→4.5k. The skill does *more* work (reads reference text, adds the missing ENS/USD/metadata), so it does not reduce tokens.
- **Wall-clock/turns are not cleanly measured here** — no_skill goals ran under concurrency-2 contention (with API backoff) while some with_skill re-runs ran sequentially, so the apparent goal-001 time gap (18.5 vs 3.4 min) is a scheduling artifact, not a skill effect. Not claimed.

## Run integrity notes

- **5 infra recoveries, none affecting the reported numbers.** 4 executor runs died on transient "connection closed mid-response" API errors under concurrency-2 on the heavy goal builds (goal-001 with_skill ×1, goal-002 with_skill ×3) — discarded and **re-executed sequentially** to valid completion. 1 judge call hit the framework's 120s timeout under load (goal-001 no_skill/2) and was **re-graded** at low load (verify leaves a run ungraded on judge error, so this is a clean completion, not an overwrite). Final: 3 valid graded runs per variant per task.
- Grading and setup used the framework scripts throughout. goal-001 used git-diff evidence via a pristine-template baseline + `git reset --mixed` (the prompt says "committed code is the deliverable," so executors that `git commit` would otherwise yield an empty `git diff`); goal-002 was re-graded on git-diff evidence (see above).

---

## The required table

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Did the skill improve pass rate? | **Goals yes, decisively: `6/6 vs 0/6`. Quizzes no: `12/12 vs 12/12`.** |
| Did it reduce time/tokens? | No. Output tokens ≈ or higher with_skill (it does more work). Wall-clock not cleanly measurable (concurrency-confounded). |
| Did it create negative deltas? | None observed. No with_skill run regressed a check that no_skill passed. |
| What mistakes repeated without the skill? | `metadata-left-as-template-default` (6/6), `address-input-no-ens-resolution` (3/3), `eth-balance-no-usd-context` (4/6), `target-network-not-retargeted` (1/3) |
| What mistakes remained with the skill? | None — all four dropped to 0 with_skill. |
| What should change in the skill? | See below — mostly it's well-targeted; trim/re-weight the rules the model already applies. |
| What should change in the eval? | See below — split expect_8; the `lib/` snapshot nit; consider a bare-scaffold quiz mirror for R8. |

### What should change in the skill

- **It works — the delta is real and clean.** The rules that move outcomes are R8 (metadata), R3 (address/ENS), R4 (USD context) — the product-completeness/polish rules the model skips unprompted. Keep these prominent.
- **Down-weight what the model already does.** R9 (decimals), R1 (pending, incl. the isPending window), R7 (errors) passed 6/6 no_skill unprompted. For Opus-4.8 these are settled knowledge; they add length without changing behavior. Consider compressing them to a one-line checklist and spending the space on R3/R4/R8 with concrete before/after snippets.
- **R8 is the headline win — make it the lead.** It's the only rule neither the model nor the SE-2 scaffold carries. A short "ship checklist" (tab title, favicon, OG/Twitter title+description+image) would be the highest-leverage addition.

### What should change in the eval

- **Split goal-001 expect_8.** It bundles Base-retarget (R5) with polling health; polling never discriminated (SE-2's 3000ms default is healthy), so the check only ever tests the retarget. Separate them so a pass/fail is unambiguous.
- **`verify` snapshot excludes `lib/`.** `GENERATED_DIRS` includes `lib` (for forge), which also drops app source in bare TS builds under `lib/` or `src/lib/`. It changed no result here (judge inferred from visible code), but it's a latent evidence gap for bare TS goals. Scope the exclusion to forge workspaces, or prefer git-diff evidence for bare builds.
- **R8 has no quiz mirror.** It's the strongest applied gap but is only measured by the goals (asked directly it's pure retrieval). That's the right call, but it means R8's signal rests entirely on 6 goal runs — worth keeping in mind if goal coverage shrinks.
- **The eval is the right artifact.** The quiz/goal split cleanly separated "knows" from "applies," which is exactly what surfaced that this skill's value for a strong model is unprompted product-polish, not correctness knowledge.


---

28.title: tasks: indexing skill (quiz x3 + goal)
28.body:
Eval tasks for `skills/indexing` per #1. Three quizzes (one stale/hallucination-prone claim each, derivation not retrieval) and one goal (the same claims applied unprompted, graded off the diff). All bare workspaces, no templates on purpose — a template pre-frames the answer. `runs: 3` per variant. Skill vendored at `191dcc1`.

## Tasks

| File | Claim tested | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `indexing-quiz-001` | You can't cheaply scan history via `eth_getLogs` — provider caps force thousands of paginated calls; use an indexer | Price a contractor's `fromBlock: 0 → latest` scan: derive the request count, what breaks first, the fix |
| `indexing-quiz-002` | The Graph's real go-live path — the skill's most stale-prone section | Hand a dead runbook step (`--hosted-service`, sunset Jun 2024) and ask for the current Studio → publish → API-key path + a real cost figure |
| `indexing-quiz-003` | The **opposite** error — current state doesn't need an indexer | Reject an over-engineered "subgraph to track balances" plan; force the one-batched-call answer (Multicall3 or a provider balances API) |
| `indexing-goal-001` | All of the above, unprompted | "Streak" check-in app: a full-history feed + streaks + month leaderboard force the index-over-events decision; the diff is graded for event-first contract design and no onchain rankings |

quiz-001 and the goal pair as knows-when-asked vs applies-unprompted; quiz-003 grades the reflex-index error so the set isn't one-directional.

## Ground truth checked (2026-07)

- **The Graph hosted service** fully sunset **12 Jun 2024** — endpoints gone. Current path: deploy to Subgraph Studio (test) → publish to the decentralized network (prod) → query via a Studio API key. Free tier ~100K queries/mo, then ~\$2 per 100K. Signal/curation GRT is part of publishing; per-query billing is fiat/credits, **not** GRT-per-query. This is the most time-sensitive task in the set — the notes flag every number as revalidate-before-run.
- **`eth_getLogs` caps**: block-span limits commonly ~2K blocks and/or a ~10K matched-log response cap. Mainnet ~block 25.5M (grows ~7.2K/day, so bump the height in quiz-001's input on re-run).
- **Multicall3** `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11`, same address on Base and 50+ chains.

## On the `notes:` blocks

Kept them to what a fresh orchestrator needs — the claim under test, task shape, ground truth to revalidate, per-run recording, vendoring line — and out of them the PR-body context (review history, reviewer names, report references) that a blind notes reader would only see as noise.

| --- | --- | --- |

## Story

- **The skill works on its designed use.** goal-001 (reviewer pass over a finished SE-2 dApp): **0/3 → 3/3**, a full 18/18 sweep in every run; all 3 with_skill runs invoked the `Skill` tool. It flips exactly the 8 checklist-only claims the base model never catches (connect-button, externalContracts, Address/contract-addr, `--radius-field`, branding ×2, deep-link, Phantom).

- Skill: add a concrete **fix recipe** to the externalContracts section; reconcile the **~2s** deep-link delay with the model's well-reasoned sub-second prior.

30.title: tasks: addresses skill (quiz x5 + goal)
30.body:
Eval tasks for `skills/addresses` per #1.

The pure "what's the address of X" case is the most web-retrievable content in the repo, so every task targets an **opinionated steering claim** where a stale-prior model reflexively defaults *wrong* and wouldn't think to look. Each `input` buries the target — no address, DEX, or claim is named; the expectation has to surface on the way.

## Tasks

| Task | Claim (SKILL.md) | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `quiz-001` | Don't reflex-default to Uniswap on L2 — Aerodrome dominates Base (L353) | Base best-execution routing decision |
| `quiz-002` | Uniswap v4 addresses differ per chain, unlike v3 (L106) | "reuse the mainnet addresses" plan to reject |
| `quiz-003` | A vanity/CREATE2 address on one chain ≠ deployed at that address on another (L462) | verify-before-wiring-funds plant |
| `quiz-004` | V1 VELO is deprecated; V2 is the live token on Optimism (L388) | zero-balance dashboard diagnosis |
| `quiz-005` | Aave V3's Pool is shared on Arbitrum/Optimism but different on Base (L190); native vs bridged USDC (L539) | multi-chain supply config |
| `goal-001` | Native USDC + non-reflex venue + verify discipline, unprompted (L539/L353) | viem Base swap build, mirrors quiz-001 |

The **knows-when-asked vs applies-unprompted split** rides on two pairs: quiz-001 ↔ goal-001 (Base venue) and quiz-005 expect_3 ↔ goal-001 expect_2 (native USDC). Where the stale prior is a once-true belief (v3 CREATE2, vanity address, V1 VELO) it's planted as "the plan on the table" or as working config, so a wrong answer is a real failure rather than a defensible alternative.

## Grading notes

- **Ground truth lives in the `expect:` lines.** The judge runs blind and offline — its prompt is the task input, the evidence and the expect lines, with no notes and no network (`lib/judge.ts`) — so every address it grades against is written into the rubric rather than left to its own memory.
- **quiz-003 rests on a fact the skill gets wrong.** Morpho Blue **is** deployed on Arbitrum, at `0x6c247b1F…`, **not** the `0xBBBB…` vanity address the teammate wants to reuse — so the plan is wrong either way, and expect_4 grades the deployment status. That is where a **negative delta** should show up: a `with_skill` run that trusts L462 ("not on Arbitrum" as of Feb 2026) fails where a verifying run passes.
- **Aggregator answers pass, but not for free.** The skill recommends aggregators for best execution (L151), so 1inch passes quiz-001 and goal-001 — only with Base-liquidity reasoning attached, otherwise a run that has never heard of Aerodrome passes the pair the verdict rides on. Contracts that are the same address on every chain via CREATE2 (1inch v6, Permit2) never count as "reused mainnet addresses".
- **Two expect lines pin live deployments** — Morpho on Arbitrum in quiz-003, the current VELO token in quiz-004. Re-verify both against the protocols' address lists before running; each task's `notes` says so.

## What is deliberately not tested

Roughly 80% of the file is a lookup table — Lido, Rocket Pool, Safe, EntryPoint, Chainlink feeds, CCIP, Across, EigenLayer, Yearn, Pendle, GMX, Curve, Balancer, Seaport, ENS, ERC-8004, major tokens. Per #1's methodology those rows are retrieval, not derivation, and get no tasks. That is itself a finding for the migration question: six opinionated claims worth grading, out of 547 lines of address table.

The ve(3,3) fee split (LPs earn emissions, veAERO voters earn the trading fees) is also not tested here — the merged `building-blocks-quiz-002` already grades that claim verbatim, and `skills/building-blocks` carries the same text (L16, L169-173) before delegating addresses to this skill. `quiz-004` covers the L373-388 Velodrome material instead, which nothing else touches.

Task specs only — no runs yet, matching #2/#3.

31.title: eval: frontend-playbook (claude)
31.body:
## What this is

Benchmark of `skills/frontend-playbook` on the **claude** stack: the same task run with the skill and without it, 3 fresh executor runs per variant, graded blind. Full write-up in `reports/frontend-playbook-2026-07-24.md`.

**Stack (one stack, start to finish):**
- **Executor:** `claude`, model `claude-opus-4-8` (fresh spawn per run)
- **Judge:** `claude`, model `claude-opus-4-8` (fresh, blind process spawned by `verify`)
- **Node:** v25.9.0 on every run (load-bearing — Node 25's built-in localStorage is what makes quiz-004 / goal-001 expect_10 fire)
- **Runs:** 8 tasks × 2 variants × 3 = **48 graded runs**

## Headline

| Task | Claim under test | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 | fork, not chain | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-002 | fork Base → target chains.foundry (31337) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-003 | trailingSlash / IPFS routing | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-004 | Node 25 built-in localStorage prerender crash | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-005 | anvil per-tx mining freezes block.timestamp | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| quiz-006 | unchanged CID proves a stale build shipped | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **quizzes** | | **14/18** | **18/18** |
| goal-001 | tip jar on SE-2 template (10 checks) | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| goal-002 | scaffold decision from empty (create-eth) | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| **goals** | | **0/6** | **6/6** |

**The split is the story:** when a claim is asked directly (quizzes), Opus-4.8 mostly already holds it — four of six quizzes are 3/3 in both variants with zero web lookups. When the same class of decision has to be applied *unprompted* while building (goals), the skill is the difference between 0/6 and 6/6.

Where the skill actually moves outcomes:
- **Scaffold choice (goal-002, 0/3 → 3/3):** every no_skill run hand-rolled `forge init` + a manual Next.js app (`/frontend` + `/contracts`); every with_skill run used `npx create-eth@latest` → the SE-2 monorepo. The skill's headline "never scaffold manually" prior, and structurally its only coverage.
- **IPFS deploy discipline (goal-001 checks 6–9):** no_skill applies the fork-mode setup perfectly (checks 1–5 all 3/3) but drops the clean rebuild, CID-as-proof, non-home route verification, and production OG metadata.
- **Node 25 prerender (quiz-004, goal-001 check 10):** no_skill gets the mechanism and refutes the instrumentation.ts fix, but stops at app-code guards / Node-24 pin instead of a process-level polyfill that reaches build workers.
- **Frozen timestamp one-off (quiz-005, 0/3 → 3/3):** no_skill diagnoses the mining model and gives the permanent `--block-time` fix, but reaches for `evm_mine` instead of `anvil_setIntervalMining` for the live-demo one-off.

## What's in this PR (55 files)

- `reports/frontend-playbook-2026-07-24.md` — full report with per-check breakdowns, transcript mining, and judge-reliability spot-checks
- `mistakes/frontend-playbook/` — **6 mistake records** (scaffold-manual-not-create-eth, frozen-timestamp-wrong-oneoff-fix, node25-localstorage-fix-wrong-layer, deploy-no-clean-rebuild-no-cid-proof, deploy-verify-home-route-only, og-metadata-not-prod-url)
- 48 `result.yaml` — one per run (per-run evidence `output/` stays local per repo convention / `.gitignore`)

## Notes for the reviewer

- **All runs `self_judged: true`** — mechanical, because a single-claude stack has `judge.agent === executor`. Each grade still ran in a fresh, blind `claude -p` process that never saw the variant, skill, or transcript. I spot-checked the discriminating verdicts against the actual outputs in both directions; they held (see report).
- **Mid-run spend/rate limit** hit the account partway through the goals. Runs that failed with a `429` never produced a grade — I deleted those run dirs (no partial data kept) and re-ran them fresh after the limit cleared, running goal-002 serially to stay under the cap. Every number is from a clean, fully-graded run.
- **Eval-sharpening note (not a blocker):** quiz-005 expect_3 is strict — no_skill answers were mechanically sound (correct diagnosis + valid permanent fix + a working manual one-off) and failed only for not naming `anvil_setIntervalMining`. Real delta, but the expect could split "any working one-off" from "the interval-mining one-off." Detailed in the report's final table.

32.title: eval: protocol (claude)
32.body:
12 runs — 3 per variant across both protocol tasks. Executor and judge both `claude` / `claude-opus-5`, one stack start to finish. Content-only: no trigger line prepended.

`self_judged: true` on all 12 — one stack means the judge is the same model as the executor. Each judge still ran blind (evidence only: output files, no skill, no variant, no transcript).

## Results

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 (state-proof target: binary trees, not Verkle) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| goal-001 (archive capacity brief, claim unprompted) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **Total** | **6/6** | **6/6** |

Every expect passed in every run. No failures, so `mistakes/protocol/` is empty — that absence is the finding, not an omission.

## The headline is a null result, and it is about the eval

Both tasks target a roadmap picture that froze before the 2024-25 Verkle deprioritization. `claude-opus-5` no longer holds that prior, and the quiz/goal split designed to separate knows-when-asked from applies-unprompted collapsed because the baseline passes both.

What `no_skill` did with no skill in the workspace, on all six runs: named EIP-7864 binary trees as the forward direction, gave a correct reason (ZK-proving compat / post-quantum), grounded the present in the hexary MPT, and declined to bank on an unscheduled migration. One run went further than the expects require — "Verkle is the design the protocol is moving *away* from — its core EIPs are Stagnant."

goal-001 was the task expected to carry the evidence: its prompt never says Verkle, statelessness, binary trees, or any fork name. All three `no_skill` briefs raised the state-tree path unprompted **and** handled it correctly — scheduled vs aspirational separated, explicit warning against banking an 18-24 month plan on it, and levers that actually address state-trie growth (Erigon/Reth, path-based storage, full-vs-archive split). `expect_4` (don't mistake EIP-4444 history expiry for a state fix) passed 6/6, including a run that discussed history expiry ten times while correctly scoping it to historical chain data.

## Mining the notes asked for

Both task notes ask which sources each run used and whether Verkle surfaced. Mentions in the graded output file:

| Task | Variant | forkcast | SFI/CFI | eips.ethereum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 | no_skill | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 4 / 4 / 4 |
| quiz-001 | with_skill | **3 / 3 / 6** | **7 / 10 / 5** | 3 / 3 / 3 |
| goal-001 | no_skill | 0 / 1 / 0 | 1 / 1 / 4 | 7 / 3 / 7 |
| goal-001 | with_skill | **0 / 9 / 5** | **20 / 26 / 20** | 6 / 0 / 0 |

The skill is invisible in the pass column and unmistakable in the method. Baseline runs reason from the EIPs repo and EthMagicians; skill runs go to forkcast first, as "How to Actually Check" prescribes, and answer in SFI/CFI status-against-a-named-fork terms rather than prose hedging. Verkle surfaced in every run of both variants and was framed as the abandoned design every time — never recommended, never presented as the direction.

Cost: **+32% wall-clock on quiz-001, +43% on goal-001** (start-to-start, grading included). Live source-checking the model would not otherwise do. No correctness regression — zero `with_skill` expect failures.

**Trigger rate is not reported here, and cannot be from these runs.** `claude -p` emits only the final message, so the saved transcripts contain no tool calls. The forkcast/SFI signature above implies the skill was read in at least 5 of 6 `with_skill` runs, but that is inference from output text, not the direct `Skill`-tool evidence other evals in this repo report. Capturing `--output-format stream-json` in the executor spawn would fix this repo-wide.

## Ground truth revalidated before the first run

Both notes carry dated ground truth ("as of 2026-07") and require revalidation, since quiz `expect_4` and goal `expect_2` grade against **current** fork scope. Checked 2026-07-25, before any run:

- **Glamsterdam** (meta [EIP-7773](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7773)) — ePBS 7732, BALs 7928, 8037 state-creation costs. No state-tree migration.
- **Hegotá** ([EIP-8081 meta thread](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8081-hegota-network-upgrade-meta-thread/26876)) — CL headliner FOCIL (7805) + AA minor set. No state-tree migration.
- **[EIP-7864](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7864)** (unified binary tree) — still `Draft`, no fork assignment.

No confirmed fork schedules a binary-tree/stateless migration. The notes' assumption held unchanged, and the expects were graded against exactly that scope.

## Recommendations

**Skill:** one concrete edit. The Fork Process table (`SKILL.md:119-125`) ends at Glamsterdam "~Q3-Q4 2026 (in progress)" and never mentions Hegotá, which now exists with FOCIL as its CL headliner — a dated list rotting inside a skill whose entire thesis is anti-staleness. Refresh it, or replace the fork rows with a forkcast pointer so there is nothing to rot. Nothing in the run data forces any other change; "What You Probably Got Wrong" is simply no longer wrong for this model tier.

**Eval:** the expects grade the *conclusion*, so parametric recall satisfies them and these tasks no longer discriminate on `claude-opus-5`. In order of value: (1) grade the **habit** — fail a scheduling claim asserted without a live check, which is the one thing that actually separated the variants here; (2) re-target the claim past the model's knowledge cutoff (e.g. current Hegotá non-headliner scope, decided within the last ~2 months) so memory cannot cover it; (3) failing both, retire these two for this model tier and keep them as regression checks for smaller or older models.

Full write-up in `reports/protocol-2026-07-25.md`.

## Run hygiene

All 12 runs completed normally — no 429s, no empty transcripts, no deleted-and-retried runs. Executed sequentially at concurrency 1. Every workspace was deleted after grading; `setup`'s leak guard passed on all 12. `run.diff` is absent by design: both tasks use bare workspaces, so `verify` takes the snapshot path rather than the diff path. `output/` (the answers and briefs) is gitignored repo-wide, as in every prior eval PR — the source-mining table above is drawn from those files on disk.

One record-keeping note for reviewers: `skill_version` reads `9a129f1`, this repo's HEAD, not the upstream pin `191dcc1`. `getSkillVersion` returns the SHA of whichever repo contains the skill dir, so a vendored-in-repo skill always records the eval repo's commit. Cosmetic, but it makes `skill_version` non-comparable across evals run at different repo HEADs.

33.title: eval: wallets (claude/opus-5)
33.body:
42 runs — 3 per variant across all 7 wallets tasks. Executor and judge both `claude` / `claude-opus-5`, one stack start to finish. Content-only: **21/21** `with_skill` runs invoked the `Skill` tool on their own, no trigger line.

`self_judged: true` on all 42 — one stack means the judge is the same model as the executor. Each judge still ran blind (evidence only: output files + diff, no skill, no variant, no transcript).

## Results

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 (7702 batching from an EOA) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-002 (multisig > lone hardware wallet) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-003 (EntryPoint version mismatch) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-004 (Safe CREATE2 determinism) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-005 (7702 delegation persists) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-006 (agent custody topology) | **0/3** | **1/3** |
| goal-001 (same batching, unprompted) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **Total** | **18/21** | **19/21** |

## The headline is a null result, and it is about the eval

The stale prior these tasks were built on is one `claude-opus-5` no longer holds — and it is not compensating with search. Across 42 runs, **2** used WebSearch and 4 verified something on-chain. Everything else came from parametric knowledge, in both variants: 7702 live since Pectra, `0x5FF...` as EntryPoint v0.6, Safe addresses as CREATE2-deterministic, delegations persisting until cleared.

Mining the specs asked for, all of it negative:
- **quiz-003** — 0/6 searched. All six gave the deposit-namespace reasoning; none topped up the v0.6 deposit; none called v0.7 "the current EntryPoint" despite SKILL.md naming only v0.7. The mistake record the notes hold open for that case is **not** filed.
- **quiz-004** — 0/6 searched; one `no_skill` run forked Base with anvil and verified the CREATE2 address through the real factory. None pinned v1.3.0 as the fix; none stored per-chain addresses.
- **quiz-005** — 0/6 searched. No run got persistence right while still calling the reverted tx a no-op.
- **goal-001** — the prior opus-4-8 benchmark's negative delta (the skill's own 7702 hedges talking runs off 7702) **did not reproduce**: 3/3 both variants, every `with_skill` run shipped 7702.

## quiz-006 is the only signal, and it is not staleness

All six runs reject threshold 1, with better reasoning than the task anticipated (a stolen agent key at threshold 1 can `swapOwner` the human out or `enableModule` a backdoor, so the "backup owner" property evaporates precisely when needed). They fail on the shape of the fix: **expect_4 fails 5/6**. Five runs design *around* the co-signing requirement — a Zodiac Roles Modifier giving the agent scoped co-signer-free execution, or a deliberately-threshold-1 bounded float — and never state the latency cost. The one passing run writes the section expect_4 asks for, so the check is doing real work.

SKILL.md never mentions modules, Guards, or the Roles Modifier; one `with_skill` run demoted the skill's canonical 2-of-3 to "a stopgap while you set up the Roles Modifier". Filed as `mistakes/wallets/wallets-agent-keeps-unilateral-execution.yaml` with both readings left open — skill gap, or over-pinned expect lines. Six runs don't settle it.

## Recommendations

**Skill:** add Safe modules / Guards / the Roles Modifier to "Safe for AI Agents" and say when scoped module execution is an acceptable substitute for a co-signer. "What You Probably Got Wrong" is no longer wrong for this model tier. SKILL.md L12 names only EntryPoint v0.7 (v0.8/v0.9 are deployed) — stale but harmless here.

**Eval:** five tasks should be retired for this model tier or rebuilt on genuinely contested claims. quiz-006's expect_2/expect_4 need a deliberate call: test the skill's topology, or test the security property ("a stolen agent key cannot move more than X without a human") — as written they fail designs arguably stronger than the skill's own.

Full write-up in `reports/wallets-2026-07-25.md`.

## Run hygiene

One executor escaped its workspace: an `npm install viem` resolved to the repo-root `package.json` (the nearest one up the tree) and modified it. Reverted; not part of this branch. Worth a guard in `setup` — a workspace `package.json` would keep installs local.

## Orchestrator-owned fabrication check

Every command and pasted output line in all 6 goal `FINDINGS.md` cross-checked against `transcript.md`: **0 fabricated output lines.** Command *text* drifted from verbatim in 3 runs (tidied per-file reconstructions that still reproduce) — filed as a mistake record, not a fabrication.

## Verdict

The eval is the wrong artifact for this model, not the skill. Concrete fixes are in the report's last row: an inspection-resistant bug, grading method on at least one expect line, and dropping quizzes 002/003/005 that the notes already predicted would double-pass.

35.title: eval: standards (claude)
35.body:
Benchmark of `skills/standards` on one stack, start to finish.

**Stack:** executor `claude -p --model claude-opus-5` (fresh per run, pointed only at `TASK.md`); judge `claude-opus-5`, blind, fresh process per run. Content-only variant, **no trigger line prepended**. 3 tasks × 2 variants × 3 runs = **18 runs, all graded**.

## Results

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| standards-quiz-001 (ERC-8004 + x402 + EIP-3009) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| standards-quiz-002 (EIP-7702 in-place EOA upgrade) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| standards-goal-001 (build the service, 10 expect lines) | 2/3 | 3/3 |

17/18 runs, 131/132 expect lines.

## The read

**The stale prior this eval targets is not stale for `claude-opus-5`.** The specs predicted `0/3` on both goal variants as plausible; instead every `no_skill` run reached ERC-8004, x402, EIP-3009 and EIP-7702 unprompted, with the right addresses, the `350000` encoding, and correct 7702 persistence semantics. Two of three `no_skill` goal runs used **zero web calls**. One quiz run verified 7702 liveness by scanning mainnet for type-4 transactions with `cast` — spending $3.36 to establish what the skill states in one line.

**What the skill does buy is cost:** $1.85 → $0.69 per run (−63%), 421s → 170s (−60%), 40 web calls → 0. Skill triggered 9/9 without prompting.

**One check discriminates, out of 22.** `goal-001` expect_10 — the ERC-8004 `.well-known/agent-registration.json` domain binding. All 3 `with_skill` runs serve it with `agentId`/`agentRegistry`/`owner`; `no_skill` runs substitute an A2A `agent-card.json` with a `registrations[]` back-pointer, which proves the card claims an identity but not that the domain controls it. Filed as `standards-missing-domain-binding`.

## Disclosed in the report

- **A judge false pass on that same line.** Two `no_skill` runs omitted the binding file identically; the judge failed one and passed the other. Recorded as graded (append-only, and I can't grade blind), but the substantive `no_skill` score on expect_10 is 1/3, not 2/3. The benchmark's entire signal rested on one line judged once.
- **Judge blindness broken on 4 runs.** The quiz phrasing "showing how you got each value" leads `with_skill` runs to cite the skill — one prints `.claude/skills/standards/SKILL.md` — inside the evidence the judge reads.
- **Two operational faults**, neither affecting a graded result: 4 goal runs killed by a 10-minute harness cap (discarded, not graded, relaunched with new run ids); and an executor's `npm install` from a bare workspace walked up and rewrote the **eval repo's own** `package.json`/`yarn.lock` (restored from git).
- `self_judged: true` on all 18 — one stack per AGENTS.md, codex not installed here.

Full analysis, transcript mining, and the eval-fix list: `reports/standards-2026-07-27.md`.

36.title: tasks: noir skill (quiz x3 + goal)
36.body:
Tasks for `skills/noir` per #1. Four files: three quizzes on separate stale claims, one goal that buries the hardest of them in an unprompted build.

https://github.com/austintgriffith/ethskills/blob/master/noir/SKILL.md

## What the skill is trying to do

`noir` is a toolchain-plus-architecture skill, and it's unusually exposed to rot: the Noir stack moved fast enough that half its content is corrections to commands and import paths that *used to be right*. Three claims carry the weight — `nargo prove` / `nargo verify` were removed (nargo compiles and executes, everything else is `bb`), Poseidon left the stdlib and is now an external dependency, and — the only silent one — a commitment-nullifier app is not private if the same wallet commits and later acts, because `msg.sender` is public regardless of how good the circuit is.

The first two fail loudly. The third ships.

## The four tasks

| | `noir-quiz-001` | `noir-quiz-002` | `noir-quiz-003` | `noir-goal-001` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frame | CI build script for an existing circuit | Sealed-bid auction range proof | Privacy review of a shipped mixer | Anonymous DAO voting, built from nothing |
| Claim | 1 — toolchain | 2 — Poseidon (+3, 4) | 5 — linkability | 5 — linkability, unprompted |
| Names it? | Never says bb or Barretenberg | Never says Poseidon or hash cost | Asks for a reality check, names no flaw | Names no wallet, relayer, or nullifier |
| Measures | knows-when-asked | knows-when-asked | knows-when-asked | applies-unprompted |
| Artifact | `build.sh` | `Nargo.toml` + `src/main.nr` | `privacy-review.md` | circuits + contracts + deploy + node script + `NOTES.md` |

quiz-003 and goal-001 are the pair that matters. Same claim, different domains on purpose (withdrawals vs voting) so they share no surface text — the quiz asks, the goal waits to see if it surfaces unasked.

## How the checks are shaped

Each task grades one claim plus riders, split so a failure says *which* thing the run got wrong rather than collapsing into one verdict.

- **quiz-001** splits lazy from stale: e1 grades the smoke test's presence (omitting it would dodge the only place the dead nargo commands can surface), e2 the `nargo prove` / `nargo verify` prohibition itself. `expect_5` is the strictest: a run can get 1-4 right from current docs and still silently break onchain verification by dropping the EVM oracle-hash setting from the VK feeding the Solidity verifier. It accepts both spellings — legacy `--oracle_hash keccak` and current `--verifier_target evm`.
- **quiz-002** splits the hash question in two. `expect_2` grades the hash *family* — algebraic vs bit-oriented, the ~30k-gate mistake the "mid-range phones" clause makes derivable — while `expect_1` grades which algebraic hash and via which import path, the actual stale claim. `expect_4` accepts both commitment-binding shapes (assert against a public input, or return as a public output for the contract to compare) and requires the range bounds to be public or constant — prover-supplied bounds grade nothing. The `compiler_version` check moved to report-only: `nargo new` never writes the line, so an expect would pass for free on both variants and the judge has no N/A to record.
- **quiz-003** measures the bait separately from the diagnosis. The fresh recipient address is deliberate — the leak is who *submits* the withdraw transaction, not where funds land — and `expect_2` tracks how often a review is bought off by it. "An auditor already verified the cryptography" walls off circuit-security boilerplate so the transaction-graph hole is the only real finding left.
- **goal-001** keeps all seven expects pointed at the build's decisions: e1 requires a named *production* gas path (an anvil prefunded account passes only as a stated stand-in — otherwise a local dev account trivially satisfies "fresh wallet"), e6 grades the serialization boundary (public-input order across circuit / script / contract — "most zk app failures happen here"), e7 the tree mirror and note persistence, the forgetting-failure SKILL.md predicts by name. The circuit-currency floor (post-colon pub, external Poseidon) moved to report-only — it re-graded quiz-002 territory and was the one check not about a decision this scenario surfaces. `expect_4` covers the NoirJS stack *and* EVM-targeted serialization (`{ keccak: true }` or the newer `{ verifierTarget: "evm" }`), the mismatch that actually breaks verification onchain.

## Claim coverage

| SKILL.md claim | Graded |
|---|---|
| 1. `nargo prove`/`verify` removed | quiz-001, all five expects |
| 2. Poseidon external, not SHA256 | quiz-002 e1/e2; goal report-only |
| 3. post-colon `pub` | quiz-002 e3; goal report-only |
| 4. `compiler_version` rejects beta | report-only on quiz-002 — an expect both variants pass for free grades nothing |
| 5. `msg.sender` linkability | quiz-003 all, goal e1/e5 |
| 6. verifier pragma / `evm_version` / 24KB | **deliberately not graded** |

Beyond the numbered claims: NoirJS stack + EVM-targeted serialization (goal e4), external-nullifier scoping (goal e2), verify-then-mutate and no `MockVerifier` in the deploy path (goal e3), the serialization boundary across layers (goal e6), tree mirror + note persistence (goal e7), salt on a small-domain commitment (quiz-002 e4).

**On claim 6.** Both its failure modes are loud — a compile error and a deploy error — so a run reads the error and fixes it rather than shipping the bug, and a fresh `forge init` already defaults to a recent `evm_version`, so an expect bolted onto the goal would pass for the wrong reason. Testing it honestly needs its own quiz seeded from a `template:` foundry project pinned to an older solc. Recorded as a decision in goal-001's notes so it doesn't read as an oversight later.

## Things worth knowing before running

- **Pre-flight the toolchain.** goal-001 is the only task in the repo needing a prover. Install nargo then `bbup` (it picks the matching bb) once per machine, before the first run — a `template:` can't carry it, nargo and bb are global binaries. Authored against nargo 1.0.0-beta.3, bb 0.82.2, forge 1.4.4-stable, node v22.18.0 — but the nargo floor is **beta.4**: stdlib Poseidon still resolves on beta.3, which contradicts the Poseidon expects. Recipe and check command are in goal-001's notes, along with a one-time HonkVerifier.sol size check against verify.ts's 256KB snapshot cap. `@aztec/bb.js` must match the bb CLI exactly or proof serialization diverges silently.
- **goal-001 is the heaviest task here.** The executor still runs `forge init` / `npm install` itself, so runs need network. A run that dies in setup is an env failure — re-run it, don't score it as a design miss.
- **Lead the reports with per-check counts.** quiz-002 has four conjunctive expects and the goal seven; aggregate `pass` will likely read 0/3 on both variants and tell you nothing. The per-check split is where the linkability delta shows up.
- **`with_skill` may burn turns on a dead end.** SKILL.md tells the agent to `claude mcp add noir-mcp` then `/reload-plugins`, neither of which survives the `-p --strict-mcp-config` spawn in AGENTS.md. That's a negative delta and a skill-edit candidate, not a wash — both quiz-001 and goal-001 ask runs to record it.
- **Poseidon2 is a known edge on quiz-002.** The skill takes a position against it, but the scenario is greenfield — no existing tree, contract, or frontend to match — so a run failing only on that should be reported as skill-conformance, not as a wrong answer.
- **No `template:` anywhere.** A scaffold would pre-pick the architecture on the goal, and on quiz-002 a seeded `Nargo.toml` would leak the poseidon dependency e1 exists to grade.

## Review round

Changes landed from review (thanks @technophile-04, @damianmarti):

- **From technophile-04's commits**: dead bbup installer URL → `next`; beta.4 recorded as the nargo floor for the Poseidon expects; quiz-002 e3 no longer grades the type (post-colon `pub` predates 1.0), e4 accepts both commitment-binding shapes and requires public/constant bounds, `compiler_version` moved to report-only; the generated-folders guard on goal-001's input; and the durable harness fix on main (`writeDiff` now excludes `GENERATED_DIRS`).
- **From damianmarti's review**: quiz-001 e1 split into presence vs prohibition; goal e1 closed the anvil-prefunded-account hole (production gas path must be named); goal gained the serialization-boundary and tree-mirror/note-persistence expects; the circuit-currency floor moved to report-only so all seven goal expects point at build decisions; notes trimmed toward orchestrator-actionable content (design rationale lives here instead).
- **Both flag-spelling deprecations absorbed**: quiz-001 e5 and goal e4 now accept `--verifier_target evm` / `{ verifierTarget: "evm" }` alongside the legacy keccak spellings, so a run following current docs doesn't read as failing.
- **Harness one-liner in this PR**: `target/` added to `GENERATED_DIRS` — nargo build artifacts were landing in the evidence as noise.
- **Known skill rot recorded in goal notes** (skill-edit candidates, not run errors): `u1` removed in beta.20 while the skill's examples still use it; zk-kit `binary_merkle_root` won't compile against current Noir; verifier Solidity floor is >=0.8.27, not the cited >=0.8.21.

Deferred to follow-ups, per damianmarti's ranking: a pattern-selection quiz (`noir-quiz-004` — simple private proof vs commitment-nullifier, the biggest coverage hole and cheapest to add), then WASM config, chain compat, and the testing boundaries.

Every `notes:` block carries a dated ground-truth line ("as of 2026-07 … revalidate before re-running") — the Noir toolchain moves fast enough that these expects will rot, and the pinned versions above are what they were validated against.

37.title: building-blocks-quiz-001: grade LP venue on Base evidence, not the rotted TVL claim
37.body:
Fixes two facts that have rotted inside `tasks/building-blocks-quiz-001.yaml`, found while reviewing #30 — the same two claims appear in `skills/addresses` and `skills/building-blocks`, so the fix is the same on both sides.

## What is wrong

| Claim in the task | State on 2026-07-27 |
|---|---|
| expect_1: Base-native DEX "rather than defaulting to Uniswap", no pass path for Uniswap | Uniswap's versions lead **Base TVL** (~$386M vs ~$308M); Aerodrome leads **volume** ~4x (Slipstream ~$344M/24h vs Uniswap v3 ~$89M). Dominance is metric-dependent, so a correct run can be graded wrong |
| notes: "Aero since the Nov 2025 merger" | Announced Nov 2025; VELO→AERO migration window opened 2026-05-12; unified launch slated July 2026 — not done |

Sources: DefiLlama `/overview/dexs/base` and `/protocols` (per-chain TVL), Dromos Labs' merger announcement and migration timeline.

## What changes

The steer is right and stays — reflex-defaulting to Uniswap on Base is still the failure this task exists to catch. Only the thing being graded moves: expect_1 now checks **how** the venue was chosen (pool depth, routed volume, or the emissions the position would actually earn) rather than which name appears. Aerodrome/Aero still passes; any other venue passes with that evidence attached; a bare "LP into Uniswap on Base" still fails. That also keeps the line from re-rotting the next time the TVL and volume leaders diverge.

Notes get the corrected merger timeline and say why the expect grades reasoning.

No runs exist for this task yet (`artifacts/` has none), so no recorded result is invalidated.

## Note on #30

The notes cross-reference `mistakes/addresses/addresses-base-dominance-metric.yaml` and `addresses-aero-merger-tense.yaml`, which land with #30. Those paths dangle until it merges — merge #30 first, or say the word and I'll drop the pointers.

38.title: tasks: orchestration skill (quiz x2 + goal)
38.body:
Eval tasks for `skills/orchestration`, per #1. Follows the AGENTS.md interview shape and the conventions from the merged sets: one claim per quiz, incident/decision framing, quiz↔goal mirror, `notes:` scoped to what a fresh orchestrator needs.

https://github.com/austintgriffith/ethskills/blob/master/orchestration/SKILL.md

## Why this shape

`orchestration` is a process skill — the three-phase build system, sequencing, validation gates — with one hard fact riding along: SE2's `yarn verify` needs no user-provisioned block explorer API key. That fact is the stale-prior magnet (models reflexively prescribe an Etherscan/Basescan key in `.env` + `foundry.toml` and treat verification as a pre-launch chore), so it anchors the quiz↔goal pair. The second quiz targets behavior, not facts: under schedule pressure, models endorse frontend workarounds for contract bugs — which bind nobody, since the contract is a public API.

## Tasks

| File | Buried claim (never named in the input) | Framing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orchestration-quiz-001` | verify immediately after deploy; no explorer API key needed (Phase 2, step 4) | unblock a ticket marked "blocked: waiting on API key from ops" — the pass must contradict the premise |
| `orchestration-quiz-002` | live contract bug → back to local: repro, fix, regression test, redeploy; never hack around bugs in production (Phase Transition Rules) | incident: fee decimals bug on mainnet, PM argues for a UI-only minimum to avoid a redeploy |
| `orchestration-goal-001` | reuses quiz-001's claim + Phase 2 as a distinct stage + go/no-go gates at three named transitions + conditional secrets hygiene | "we want real users on a public URL" — full launch runbook, phases/verification/keys never named |

All `skill: skills/orchestration`, `runs: 3`, bare workspace, answer into a file. quiz-001↔goal-001 is the knows-when-asked / applies-unprompted split from #1; quiz-002 deliberately has no goal twin — the scenario is already decision-shaped and an incident goal would read as a near-duplicate.

## Ground truth

The no-key claim is traced through the vendored `templates/se-2-foundry`, not asserted: `.env.example` ships a default `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY`, postinstall copies it to `.env`, and `yarn verify` → `make verify` → `VerifyAll.s.sol` → `forge verify-contract --chain <id>` with no key flag — Base rides the env var through Etherscan's multichain API even though `[etherscan]` only names polygonMumbai/sepolia. Both notes carry the dated revalidate-before-re-running caveat; the expect carve-out is "you don't have to obtain a key", not "no key exists anywhere", so mentioning the bundled default doesn't fail a run.

## Design notes

- **quiz-002 pre-registers a real skill gap.** SKILL.md's transition table has rows for Phase 3 bug → Phase 2 and Phase 2 contract bug → Phase 1, but no row for this scenario — a *contract* bug found in Phase 3. The graded answer is the two-hop composition. A `with_skill` run that applies the table literally and stops at "back to Phase 2" lands in #1's *fix the skill* lane: notes say to file a mistake record proposing the missing row, not read it as judge noise.
- **Deltas stay attributable.** goal-001 doesn't grade metadata/OG or IPFS-vs-Vercel — those belong to ship / frontend-playbook. Secrets hygiene IS graded (expect_6, conditional) after review established no other task in the suite covers "don't commit the key". burnerWalletMode stays ungraded for a different reason: both vendored templates already ship `localNetworksOnly`, so the skill's checklist item is a no-op on a fresh scaffold — a skill finding for the report, not a task gap. No `template:` on purpose: a repo would pull runs toward checklist fixes (qa-goal-002's lane) instead of sequencing.
- **quiz-002's bug is an overcharge on purpose** — no exploit angle, so security-incident reflexes (pause, war room) don't crowd out the graded decision. The phases are never named in the input; the expects grade the back-to-local discipline in substance, not the skill's vocabulary.
- **quiz-001 is expected to ceiling.** With network on, its first two expects are one web search away and the input hands the timing as a binary. Kept anyway for the embedded-blocker framing; goal-001 measures the same claim unprompted and carries the delta.
- Both quizzes ask runs to record which sources were consulted (SE2 docs/repo, web search, memory), so a pass tells us checked vs recalled.

## Review pass

Tightened before this went up: the default-key carve-out (an obtained key as prerequisite fails; noting the bundled default doesn't), dropped verify from quiz-002's expects so a failure there can't be confused with quiz-001's claim, swapped a weak compiler-settings rationale for a real one, made goal-001 say the repo isn't checked out. Post-review tweaks: a fork-mode forge test counts as local repro in quiz-002 (grade discipline, not tool choice), and quiz-001's notes report-don't-grade the `broadcast/run-latest.json` dependency (verify must run from the deploying checkout).

Applied from review (294dce0): bundled expects split so per-check failures stay readable — quiz-001 timing vs substantive-reason, quiz-002 hot-patch vs missing-regression-test, goal-001 one-hop-deploy vs never-tested-live-with-real-money; forge-verify-contract explanation carve-out on quiz-001 expect_2; secrets conditional added to goal-001; burner and secrets attributions in notes corrected; notes trimmed per inline comments, design reasoning moved here.
