39.title: tasks: audit skill (goal + quiz x3)
39.body:
Eval tasks for `skills/audit`, per #1. One goal + three quizzes, plus the fixture the goal audits.

## Why this skill needed a different shape

`skills/audit` carries no factual claims of its own. It is a routing table, a pointer to `austintgriffith/evm-audit-skills` (500+ checklist items behind raw URLs), and a five-phase methodology: recon → route → one parallel sub-agent per domain → synthesis → file issues. There is no stale claim to bury inside a derivation, so the thing worth measuring is **recall breadth over a real codebase** — does routing 6-8 checklists surface bugs a single-pass read misses — with quizzes only on the handful of claims where a default model is genuinely thin.

Worth stating plainly for whoever reads the results against #1's verdict table: the knowledge here lives upstream in an unvendored, unpinned repo, and the skill under test is the router in front of it. A `with_skill` win is partly a win for `evm-audit-skills` at whatever state it was in that day.

## audit-goal-001

`templates/audit-market-001` is a hand-authored foundry fixture: "ArbiLend", an overcollateralised USDC lending market whose README states it deploys to **Arbitrum One** and shortlists yield-bearing and rebasing collateral for the next listing round. The prompt asks for a security review before mainnet and names no vulnerability, contract area or domain. Ten planted bugs, one per expect line, plus an eleventh expect on severity:

| # | Where | Bug |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `LendingMarket.setOracle` | no owner check — swap in your own price source |
| 2 | `CollateralVault.withdraw` | transfer before state update and health check |
| 3 | `PriceOracle` | no L2 sequencer uptime feed |
| 4 | `PriceOracle.getPrice` | `latestAnswer()`, no freshness or negative-answer check |
| 5 | `LendingMarket.accrueInterest` | `block.number * 12` as a clock |
| 6 | `LendingMarket.healthFactor` | divide before multiply |
| 7 | `CollateralVault.deposit` | credits requested amount, not balance delta |
| 8 | `LendingMarket.borrowWithSig` | no nonce, no deadline, cached domain separator |
| 9 | `LendingMarket.upgradeTo` | unguarded; implementation never disabled |
| 10 | `LendingMarket.liquidateAll` | unbounded `borrowers` array |

**Read this one as a count, not a pass.** Ten hard findings means `pass: true` is out of reach for both variants by design, so the headline is findings-caught-out-of-10 per variant, read off the per-expect results. The notes say so, so a fresh orchestrator does not write it up as a null 0/3 vs 0/3. Bundling the bugs into 4-5 domain expects would have kept the aggregate meaningful, but it hides *which* bug was missed, and attributability is the whole point here.

Expect 11 is the severity check. The input already asks for a severity per finding and a ranking ("so I can hand the top of the list to the team on Monday"), and severity definitions are skill content — they live in the master index. Without expect 11 a report that rates all ten findings "Medium" scores a clean 10/10, so the check requires the two take-everything access-control breaks (unguarded `upgradeTo`, unguarded `setOracle`) to sit in the report's top band, and the ranking to follow the severities the report itself assigned. It grades only findings the run actually reported, so it never double-punishes a miss.

Expect 5 grades only that the `block.number * 12` clock is flagged and `block.timestamp` prescribed. The chain semantics — on Arbitrum `block.number` reports the **L1** block number, so `blocksElapsed * 12` is roughly right there by coincidence and the bug detonates on any chain whose `block.number` counts L2 blocks — are recorded but not graded, because quiz-002 grades that derivation directly and against a prompt built for it. Grading it in both places would collapse the knows-when-asked / applies-unprompted split into one measurement, and would fail a run that flags the clock but reasonably downgrades it to informational-portability on the one chain this fixture targets. A per-chain seconds-per-block constant offered as the fix still fails.

## The three quizzes

Sequencer uptime feed, `block.number` semantics across chains, EIP-712 replay — the same claims as goal expects 3, 5 and 8, so each pair reads as knows-when-asked vs applies-unprompted.

Every one closes off the reflex answer inside the prompt, so a pass needs the derivation rather than a matched pattern:

- **quiz-001** hands over a working staleness check and states the price was fresh and correct, so "check for stale prices" is already spent — the answer only reaches the sequencer feed by working out that the *users*, not the price, were the thing that went stale. The words sequencer, uptime and grace period never appear in the input.
- **quiz-002** states the wrong prior out loud ("Arbitrum makes 250ms blocks, this should be tens of times off") and then hands over figures that refuse it: both deployments charge the same 3,391 USDC, and both land a couple of tenths under the 3,397 the rate implies. The two figures are equal on purpose — reading the same L1 counter, they cannot diverge, so a gap would contradict the very mechanism the task grades, and a careful run would waste the answer explaining it. Keep them equal if anyone edits the scenario. The Base half then forces the same knowledge in the opposite direction, with arithmetic that cannot be bluffed.
- **quiz-003** rules out the compromised key, the relayer and the recovered address, and notes the signature is byte-identical — which also rules out malleability, the reflex answer for a signature incident, and that is what expect 4 exists to enforce. The "what else does this expose us to" clause is what pulls at the cached domain separator without naming it.

## Notes on the fixture

Deliberately dependency-free and test-free: no `lib/`, no imports outside `src/`, so `forge build` succeeds in a fresh workspace with nothing installed and there is no pinned install to rot. Verified through a real `yarn setup` run.

Three things the notes flag for whoever runs this:

- `forge build` prints lint warnings that point straight at the divide-before-multiply, the unchecked ERC-20 transfers and the unsafe `int256`→`uint256` cast. Both variants get those for free; runs should record whether they got there via lint or via review. I left the lints on rather than suppressing them, since a real auditor builds the project.
- The skill's last phase files GitHub issues with `gh issue create` for Medium+ findings. The prompt provides no repo and says the code is not hosted anywhere, so that phase self-skips. If a run tries to file issues anywhere, stop it — no eval run touches GitHub.
- The task input asks for `AUDIT-REPORT.md` to be the only file left behind, in both variants identically. This is load-bearing rather than tidiness: the skill has each sub-agent write `findings-<domain>.md` first, and `verify` snapshots the whole workspace except the skill install dirs into the judge's evidence — so those filenames would tell a judge that must stay blind exactly which variant it is grading, and could earn a pass for a finding the report itself never carries. If a run leaves them behind anyway, that run's grading was not blind and the report should say so.

## Coverage, and what this eval does not reach

Ten of the routing table's twenty rows get exercised: general, precision-math, erc20, defi-lending, oracles, chain-specific, proxies, signatures, access-control, dos. The other nine (amm, staking, 4626, 4337, bridges, governance, assembly, flashloans, erc721) never get routed to, because one fixture is one contract type. If routing breadth turns out to be the interesting variable, that is a second goal task with a differently-shaped fixture, not more expects on this one.

The issue-filing phase is unevaluable here by design, and the standard finding *format* is recorded rather than graded — grading it would reward ceremony over findings. Expect 11 grades severity because severity changes what a human does on Monday; format does not.

Expects 2, 4 and 7 restate claims `security-goal-001`/`-002` already grade from the writing side. That is deliberate — one skill teaches writing the code, this one finds it in code you did not write — but it is worth knowing when mistake records start colliding across the two skills.

The `notes:` blocks are written for a fresh orchestrator with no context on any of this — how to read the result, network and cost requirements, what to record but not grade, what invalidates a run's blindness. Everything that is background for reviewers lives here and in the commit messages instead.

40.title: eval: security (claude)
40.body:
48 runs on one stack: executor and judge both `claude` / `claude-opus-5`, 8 tasks × 2 variants × 3 runs, content-only (no trigger line). Report: `reports/security-2026-07-28.md`.

## Result

**48/48 runs pass. 210/210 expect lines pass. Every task 3/3 vs 3/3 — not one check discriminates.**

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 first-depositor donation | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-002 spot price is not an oracle | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-003 credit the balance delta | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-004 USDT approve race / OZ v5 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-005 chainId in the EIP-712 domain | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-006 append-only storage layout | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| goal-001 vault, 5 habits unprompted | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| goal-002 borrowing market, oracle unprompted | 3/3 | 3/3 |

The stale prior does not hold on opus-5. In 24 `no_skill` runs the three predicted defaults never appeared: zero naive `assets * totalSupply / balanceOf` vaults (5/6 goal-001 runs inherit OZ `ERC4626`, the sixth hand-rolls a virtual offset), zero `slot0`/`getReserves` reads across twelve goal runs, and balance-delta crediting written unprompted with fee-on-transfer never mentioned in the input. No web calls in any of the 48 runs — it is parametric knowledge, not retrieval.

## What the skill changed

Overhead: **+32% cost** ($1.01 → $1.33/run), +19% wall-clock, +20% output tokens. Ungraded deltas: ~51% more tests on goal runs, Slither recommended 6/6 `with_skill` vs 0/6 `no_skill`, MEV exposure raised 3/3 vs 0/3 on goal-002.

## Two defects in the skill, filed

Both found because runs corrected the skill in writing:

- `security-safeapprove-removed-in-oz-v5` — the SafeERC20 block prescribes `safeApprove`, removed in OZ Contracts v5, which quiz-004's repo is pinned to. 6/6 runs used `forceApprove` instead; one wrote a section titled *"One correction to the skill material"*.
- `security-hardcoded-3600-staleness` — the Chainlink example hardcodes a 1h staleness bound for every feed; USDC/USD's heartbeat is 24h, so it would revert continuously. One run: *"will make USDC/USD revert almost continuously and brick the market. Worth correcting in that skill too."*

Pattern: the prose is right, the copy-paste snippet is wrong, and this model overrides it. A weaker model would ship the snippet.

## Disclosures

- `self_judged: true` on all 48 runs (one stack per AGENTS.md; codex not installed here). Grading still ran blind in a fresh process per run.
- **Judge negative control:** a planted wrong answer to quiz-001 (blames a USDC fee, calls it user error, prescribes blocking transfers) failed 4/4 with specific reasons. The all-pass is not a rubber stamp.
- 5 `with_skill` runs named the skill inside judged evidence; three of those were footnotes declining the skill's closing feedback-URL instruction.
- 6 runs died at launch to a macOS-missing `timeout`; deleted un-graded and relaunched with new run ids, nothing overwritten.
- `forge install` created a root `.gitmodules`, staged six gitlinks, and left 288 MB in `.git/modules` — cleaned, nothing committed.

## Recommendation

The eval is the wrong artifact for this stack, not the skill. Eight saturated tasks cost 48 runs to establish zero resolving power. Details and concrete re-targeting suggestions in the report's verdict table.

41.title: tasks: concepts skill (quiz x2 + goal)
41.body:
https://github.com/austintgriffith/ethskills/blob/master/concepts/SKILL.md

Tasks for `skills/concepts`, per #1. Two quizzes and one goal.

`concepts` is mostly a mental-model skill rather than a facts skill, so the pick was about which of its claims can actually be graded off an artifact. What came out testable: onchain randomness, whether an incentive is *big enough*, and three of the four CROPS habits (admin key as a censorship vector, what a public ledger exposes, and contracts-are-verified standing in for a forkable stack).

### What each task targets

**`concepts-quiz-001` — "Randomness Is Hard" (5 expects).** A 5 ETH meetup raffle, entries close Friday 20:00, prize handed over that same evening. The prompt never says *random*, *VRF* or *commit-reveal* — it asks for the exact sequence from entries-close to payout, who sends each transaction and the window it has to land in. That can't be answered without picking a source. The same-evening constraint is load-bearing: it's what makes the 256-block blockhash window (~51 min at 12s blocks) and VRF callback latency bite instead of staying abstract. Expects 2 and 3 are per-path (commit-reveal vs external service) and each passes trivially when the run took the other one, so every design still faces the same three shared lines.

**`concepts-quiz-002` — "is the incentive sufficient?" (4 expects).** This is the third question SKILL.md attaches to every state transition, and the one I couldn't find covered anywhere else. The design handed to the executor already passes the first two questions — `harvest()` is permissionless and it pays its caller — so the only thing left to get wrong is the arithmetic: 1% of ~$0.88/day against 250k gas of mainnet cost.

Deliberately distinct from `ship-quiz-003`, which grades whether a design names a caller and a reason **at all**. This grades whether the reason is big enough to move a caller who's paying gas.

Worth flagging how the numbers landed: my first draft was a $250k vault with a 1% cut, and checking live gas killed it — at ~0.09 gwei and ETH ~$1,945, a daily harvest is comfortably profitable and there's no derivation left to test. Re-sized to launch scale ($8k of deposits), where the caller's fee is ~$0.009/day against ~$0.05 of gas: break-even ~5-6 days now, ~50 days at 0.9 gwei, months if gas returns to multi-gwei. A stale-prior model that reads gas as expensive reaches the same verdict, harder. The expect grades the break-even the run derives *from the prices it states*, not a fixed interval — the spread inside sub-1-gwei alone is a factor of ten, which is too much to freeze into a rubric.

**`concepts-goal-001` — the same claim, unprompted (7 expects).** Onchain billing for a small API service: pre-funded USDC balances, monthly plans, cancel any time, and the backend needs a per-request "is this address subscribed" check. The prompt never says automatic, keeper, cron, incentive, admin, privacy, open source or decentralization. "Charged monthly for as long as they keep the subscription" is the trap — there is nothing to run it. The per-request check is deliberate too: it leaves the read-time accrual design (no periodic transaction exists to pay for) available as the strongest answer without hinting at it.

Expects 2-4 grade *nothing is automatic* plus the hyperstructure test (can a customer still get their funds out with nobody operating the thing). Expects 5-7 grade the CROPS habits the skill says to surface rather than scaffold silently: censorship (5), privacy (6), and open source (7) — the last one leans on the fact that the subscription buys access to a weather API the provider runs, so public contracts are visibly not the whole stack. Bare workspace, no template, stack left to the executor — so we also record what it reaches for.

Read together: quiz-002 measures knows-when-asked, goal-001 measures applies-unprompted. The issue's "keep as skill" row is only reachable from that split.

### What these tasks don't cover

So the coverage claim is legible rather than implied:

- **CROPS "Security" — "audited" treated as proof of security.** Untested here. A derivation-shaped test of it lands on `skills/security` / `skills/audit` turf rather than this one, and this build has no natural hook for it. Flagging that #39's audit tasks don't cover it either, so it's currently a hole in the suite as a whole.
- **The "Teaching Your Human" section.** The pedagogy framing isn't gradable off an artifact. Its two hard technical claims already are, elsewhere: the approve pattern / infinite approvals in `security-quiz-004`, and never reading prices from a DEX pool in `security-quiz-002`.
- **The SpeedRun learning path.** Not gradable this way.
- **`onchain` vs `on-chain`.** See below.

### Notes on the `notes:` blocks

Following the point raised on #3 — the `notes:` reader is a fresh orchestrator that never saw this PR. So they carry only what's needed to run and grade: the claim and its SKILL.md section, which input clauses are load-bearing and must not be softened, the ground truth to re-check on run day, what to record per run, and the workspace shape. Scenario history, review back-and-forth and the reasoning above live here in the PR body instead.

Where a carve-out has to reach the **judge**, it's written into the expect line itself rather than the notes — the judge never sees notes.

### Three things for reviewers

**1. Vendored `skills/concepts` has drifted from live, and CROPS is being spun out into its own skill.** Live `ethskills.com/concepts/SKILL.md` now expands CROPS' O to "Open Source **and Free (as in Freedom)**", rewrites that bullet around licensing (a verified contract with no real license isn't open), reworks the second catch-yourself question, and adds a pointer to a new `crops/SKILL.md` — which exists (`https://ethskills.com/crops/SKILL.md` returns a full skill covering custody, admin keys, hosted infra, privacy, user exit and restrictive licenses). It isn't vendored here and isn't on #1's checklist. The vendored copy at `191dcc1` predates all of it.

Tasks are written against the vendored copy, since that's what actually gets installed into the workspace. Diffed the two: nothing outside the CROPS section changed, and expects 5-7 grade the censorship, privacy and whole-stack points, which survive both wordings. Two things a re-vendor would bring: a licensing claim nothing here tests, and a `with_skill` run that may fetch `crops/SKILL.md` over the network — which would make the delta about the bundle rather than this skill, the same problem `ship`'s notes flag. Worth deciding whether `crops` becomes a 20th vendored skill with its own tasks, in which case expects 5-7 arguably belong there.

**2. `onchain` vs `on-chain` is graded nowhere.** The skill makes the call explicitly, and a run's prose is the obvious place to check it. I left it out of the expects on purpose: a run passes only when *every* line passes, so a single hyphen would sink an otherwise-correct build and make the delta unreadable. All three tasks record it per run in `notes:` instead. Happy to promote it to an expect if you'd rather grade it.

**3. Two things in the tasks that exist for evidence-plumbing reasons, not eval reasons.**

- `goal-001`'s input carries the generated-dirs guardrail line that `ship-goal-001` already has. `scripts/verify.ts:21` drops `lib/ dist/ build/ out/` from the snapshot, and `:221` grades any workspace containing `.git` from `run.diff` — which `git add -N` + `git diff` leaves **empty** if the run committed its own work. Without the guardrail a Foundry or `create-eth` run could show the judge nothing and fail expect_1 for code sitting right there. The `notes:` tell the orchestrator to check the evidence before grading rather than grading the gap.
- `goal-001` expect_2 is scoped to the provider withdrawing revenue that accrued **without** that transaction. An earlier wording allowed "revenue it has already earned", which is itself an operator-only transaction — an `onlyOwner chargeAll()` could have been argued into the allowed list by a blind judge.

42.title: addresses: correct the Aero merger dates the run-day gate rests on
42.body:
Follow-up to the #37 review, which flagged that both Aero merger dates on this branch are wrong. Targets `tasks/addresses` so it lands inside #30.

## What is wrong

| Claim on this branch | State on 2026-07-28 |
|---|---|
| "the VELO->AERO migration window opened 2026-05-12" | No token migration has opened. The 12 May event was Aerodrome moving liquidity into new MEV-resistant pools. AERO, veAERO, VELO and veVELO all upgrade **at launch** |
| "the unified launch is slated for July 2026" | Dromos re-timed it on 16 Jul: codebase public **3 Aug**, audits through **21 Aug**, Sherlock contest **24 Aug - 11 Sep**, launch targeted **September 2026** |

Source: [aero.xyz — "Aero is on the Horizon"](https://aero.xyz/articles/aero-is-on-the-horizon/). "Slated July 2026" was already stale when #30 opened.

## Why it matters

`addresses-quiz-004`'s RUN-DAY GATE branches on whether AERO is live on Optimism at run time. Under the old dates that reads as a live coin flip mid-migration; under the real timeline branch (a) — V2 VELO still the live token, `0x9560e8...` — is the expected state, and (b) only trips if September gets pulled forward. Same gate, but a runner now knows which way to expect it to fall.

`mistakes/addresses/addresses-aero-merger-tense.yaml` carried the same two announcement-derived dates in its `symptom` and `expected_pattern` — the exact habit it faults SKILL.md L375 for — so it gets the same correction, plus a pointer to `skills/building-blocks` SKILL.md L16/L169, which state the merger complete in a second skill.

## Not changed

The V1/V2 VELO addresses, the expects, and the gate's two branches are untouched. V2 `0x9560e827aF36c94D2Ac33a39bCE1Fe78631088Db` re-verified live 2026-07-28.

43.title: eval: ship (codex-gpt-5.6-terra)
43.body:
30 runs on one stack: executor and judge both `codex` / `gpt-5.6-terra`, 5 tasks × 2 variants × 3 runs, content-only (no trigger line). Reports: `reports/ship-*-2026-07-30.md`.

## Result

**No clean overall win.** Three quizzes saturated at 3/3 vs 3/3; liveness regressed to 2/3 vs 3/3; the unprompted build improved to 1/3 vs 0/3. **105/120 expect lines passed.**

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 MVP contract count / audit scope | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-002 onchain litmus / reputation | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-003 six-weeks liveness | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| quiz-004 chain superpower | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| goal-001 Toolshed, six habits unprompted | 0/3 | 1/3 |

Goal per-check split matters: the skill changed raw data placement from 0/3 to 3/3 and offchain ranking from 0/3 to 2/3. It did not fix README transition documentation (1/3 to 2/3 failures) or a concrete deployment decision (2/3 failures in each variant).

## What the skill changed

`with_skill` consistently stopped putting tool/profile data onchain. It did not reliably stop computed reputation ranking onchain, make the deployment target explicit, or document every USDC-moving caller. Quiz-003 added one negative: a plan named a permissionless transition without an actual gas incentive.

Six mistake records filed: data/ranking placement, transition incentives, README caller audit, deployment decision, and executor timeout.

## Disclosures

- `self_judged: true` on all 30 records. Grading was executed after each run, but this harness classifies same-stack Codex executor/judge runs as self-judged.
- Ship routing caused additional ethskills retrieval in many with-skill runs; this is trigger-inclusive/bundle-contaminated, not content-only.
- All quiz-004 runs also browsed Base/Coinbase material; that task measures network-enabled product research as much as skill content.
- Five goal runs stopped making observable progress for over five minutes and were terminated, then blindly graded from their captured snapshots: 1/3 no-skill; 2/3 with-skill. This cutoff was an operator recovery decision, not part of the task spec.

## Recommendation

Keep goal-001: it is the only discriminating positive task. Rework quiz-001/002/004 because baseline saturation means they do not test the stated stale prior on this stack. Add a defined executor timeout before rerunning; separate content-only from routing-inclusive runs.

44.title: tasks: l2s skill (quiz x4 + goal)
44.body:
Tasks for `skills/l2s`, per #1. Four quizzes and a goal, one claim each, every claim buried behind a decision rather than asked directly.

| Task | Claim under test | How it surfaces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `l2s-quiz-001` (4 expects) | Celo is an OP Stack L2, not the L1 it was until 2025-03-26 | Runbook for a monthly CELO sweep to a mainnet treasury. An L1 prior reaches for a wrapped-asset bridge and quotes minutes; the L2 answer is initiate → prove → finalize across a multi-day window |
| `l2s-quiz-002` (3 expects) | Polygon zkEVM is discontinued | A support ticket (dashboard stuck, block number not moving, providers already swapped) plus a Q3 feature plan on a chain that stopped producing blocks |
| `l2s-quiz-003` (5 expects) | Base announced its Superchain / OP Stack exit, Feb 2026 | A Base↔OP Mainnet game token. A stale prior ships SuperchainERC20 native interop, which is neither mainnet-live nor a safe Base bet |
| `l2s-quiz-004` (5 expects) | Compute-heavy Rust belongs on Arbitrum, where Stylus runs it alongside the EVM | A DePIN team wants its existing 2k-line Rust scoring routine onchain and will not maintain a second implementation. No chain is named in the prompt |
| `l2s-goal-001` (5 expects) | Same claim as quiz-001, unprompted | Build `payout.ts` + `sweep.ts` + `NOTES.md` for Celo. Nothing in the prompt says bridge, L1, L2 or withdrawal |

All bare workspaces, `runs: 3`, all five load through `loadTaskSpec`.

`quiz-004` is the only task in the set that makes the model choose a chain — the half of the skill its own description calls "when to use which". The other four hand the chain over in the prompt, so without it the selection guide (14 rows) goes ungraded.

## Ground truth the expects rest on

Checked 2026-07-31. Several of these are counter-intuitive enough that an expect written without them fails correct answers, so they are worth reading before grading.

- **Polygon zkEVM is frozen, not unreachable.** `zkevm-rpc.com` still answers `eth_chainId`, `eth_getBalance` and `eth_call`; latest block is 33391890, timestamped 2026-07-03T15:55:44Z. Reads work, writes can never land. That is why quiz-002's symptom is a stalled block number rather than failing calls, and why its expect_1 disqualifies only *fixable*-cause answers — a run that probes the endpoint and reports reads working must not be marked down for it.
- **The zkEVM claims path covers wallet-held balances only.** Polygon's sunset post says outright that funds locked in DeFi protocols cannot be auto-migrated: the exit snapshot never covered contract-held balances, and the claims UI (open ~2026-07-13 to 2027-12-31) cannot return them. quiz-002 expect_3 grades only that the recovery is not treated as a routine exit — the split itself is absent from the skill, so it cannot be a `with_skill` win and is recorded rather than graded. "The vault's \$400k may be unrecoverable" is the correct answer, not a failing one.
- **Celo withdrawals are the standard OP Stack exit** — initiate on L2 (`L2ToL1MessagePasser`), prove on L1, finalize after the challenge period, "the same as on OP chains that use ETH as the native token" (specs.celo.org/bridge.html). Celo's own guide points at viem's `getTimeToProve`/`getTimeToFinalize` rather than pinning numbers, so quiz-001 and goal-001 grade the magnitude (days), not a figure. Fast Celo↔Ethereum routes are live, so a fast-bridge design is a legitimate pass — and so is declining one at $2M on trust grounds and rescheduling the close instead, which is what the skill's own >$100K bridging guidance points at.
- **Superchain interop is not live on Base or OP Mainnet**, and the docs describe it as in active development, rolled out iteratively. quiz-003 grades only "not live on those mainnets today" — what a run says about when it might land is not graded.
- **Base's exit was announced 2026-02-18**, migration to its own client and stack is rolling out, and Base remains an Ethereum L2 throughout. (The "~99% shared code" figure in an earlier draft has no primary source located and is now marked unverified in the record.) quiz-003 expect_4 fails the overcorrection as well as the stale prior.
- **Stylus launched with ArbOS 32** and is live on Arbitrum One, which runs ArbOS 51 today (`ArbSys.arbOSVersion()` returns 106): Rust/C/C++ compiled to WASM, deployed and then *activated* in a second onchain transaction, interop both ways with Solidity. The gas story is real for memory- and compute-heavy work, but the skill's "10-100x" conflates two metrics — RedStone's Nov 2025 benchmarks report 10-100x on *execution speed* and roughly 26-50% on *gas* — so quiz-004 grades the capability and the activation step, never a multiplier.

## Skill rot found while fact-checking

Eight records under `mistakes/l2s/`. Six are ungraded by design: where a claim appears in the skill only in its wrong form, an expect written against reality fails every `with_skill` run and measures the rot instead of the model. quiz-003 and the Celo bridging gap are the exceptions, and the difference is stated in the records — there the skill carries the fact correctly in one place and contradicts it in another, so a run can pass by reading the right line.

- `l2s-unichain-ordering-inverted` — the skill says Unichain orders "by time received, NOT gas price" and tells builders not to pay priority fees. It is the reverse: the TEE enforces priority-fee ordering ("the TEE orders transactions based purely on priority fees", Uniswap's own Rollup-Boost post). Same section also has 1s blocks with 250ms "on the roadmap"; Flashblocks confirm every 200ms today.
- `l2s-zksync-zksolc-required` — "must use zksolc, no EXTCODECOPY, 65K instruction limit". Era ships an EVM bytecode interpreter, so standard solc bytecode deploys through stock Foundry and Hardhat. Scoped wrong rather than false: native EraVM compilation is still the primary, cheaper path and still carries every one of those constraints, so the error is the blanket "must".
- `l2s-aero-merger-tense` — Aero is announced, not launched: aero.xyz still reads "Aero is on the horizon", contest 24 Aug–11 Sep, launch expected September. The l2s copy of a fact `mistakes/addresses/` already flagged as living here untracked; that back-reference is updated in this PR.
- `l2s-polygon-zkevm-tense` — "is being shut down" is now past tense. Sequencer stopped ~2026-07-01.
- `l2s-base-superchain-contradiction` — the departure is recorded in one line, but the selection table still answers multi-chain with "Base or Optimism — Superchain / OP Stack" and the 58.6% share counts Base.
- `l2s-celo-fee-abstraction-gap` — CIP-64 (pay gas in USDC/USDT/USDm) is absent, while the selection table routes mobile payments to Celo. A reader building exactly that app reaches for ERC-4337 it does not need.
- `l2s-celo-chain-params-stale` — the comparison row gives Celo 5s blocks and 7-day finality. Blocks are 1s (measured over 24,912 of them), and the challenge window is 3.5 days: Celo's mainnet dispute game `0xA35d2A7F365b42EcFCB7Db9240c3973Fc8e65139` is `gameType()` 42, an OP Succinct game rather than the standard fault-dispute timeline, and its `maxChallengeDuration()` returns 302400. Ungraded — both timing expects grade magnitude.
- `l2s-celo-bridging-gap` — **graded.** The bridging table has no Celo row, and `prove`, `finalize`, output roots and `L2ToL1MessagePasser` appear nowhere in the skill. quiz-001 expect_2 and goal-001 expect_4 require those mechanics, so both notes carry a verdict-flipping marker: a `with_skill` fail on that line alone is the gap, not the model.

## What this set does not grade

- **Cost claims** (the $0.001-0.003 figures, "mainnet is cheap too", "Base is ~50% cheaper") and the mainnet-first steer above the selection guide. The cost model is graded against `skills/gas` by `gas-quiz-001` through `gas-quiz-003` and `gas-goal-001`; duplicating it here would attribute the same delta to two skills.
- **`block.number` semantics**, including Arbitrum returning the L1 block number — graded by `audit-quiz-002` and `audit-goal-001`.
- **Dominant DEX per chain** — graded by `addresses-quiz-001`, `addresses-goal-001` and `building-blocks-quiz-001`, where both the Aerodrome and Aero names pass.
- The four rotted claims above.

## Review fixes (e989c56)

Applied from @technophile-04's review, whose factual calls I re-checked live and confirmed on all three counts (3.5-day challenge window, 1s Celo blocks, ArbOS 51):

- **Judge visibility.** quiz-002 expect_2 no longer grades chain liveness, which the notes file under record-don't-grade and an offline judge cannot check. quiz-003 expect_1 gains a pass path for answers that never raise SuperchainERC20 at all. quiz-004 expect_2's non-Arbitrum path now needs a named mechanism plus a checkable source instead of a blind factual verdict, and expect_3 splits deploy-and-activate from the Solidity call path.
- **Two inputs gained a neutral clause** so expects stop grading questions the prompt never asked: quiz-002 "tell me what all this means for the merchant money", and quiz-003 "say what you're assuming about Base and OP Mainnet that this design would break if it stopped holding". On the latter I kept expect_2 standalone rather than folding it into expect_1 — folding means a run that silently ships an OFT is never graded on the Base departure, which is the task's whole claim.
- **goal-001 expect_5** (the review numbers it expect_4) stated "roughly a week" with no live-override clause and would have failed a run that correctly checked and said 3.5 days. Both timing expects now grade magnitude with the override quiz-001 already carried.
- **quiz-003 gains a blocking run-day gate**, since three of its expects rest on in-flight states, modelled on `addresses-quiz-004`.

## Two things worth knowing before running

**`l2s-quiz-003` can fail `with_skill` on the skill's own contradiction.** If it does, the selection-table row is the likely cause, not the model — the notes say so and tell the orchestrator to check the transcript first. That outcome is what closes `l2s-base-superchain-contradiction`.

**`l2s-quiz-002` may ceiling at 3/3 on both variants** if the executor model already knows about the July 2026 shutdown, since network access makes it searchable. Cheap to run and decisive either way, but if it ceilings, the budget is better spent on `goal-001`.

`notes:` blocks are deliberately short — ground truth with its check date, the mirror task, run mechanics, record-don't-grade items — since their reader is a fresh orchestrator running the loop, not a reviewer.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

45.title: eval: tools (claude/opus-5)
45.body:
Thirty graded runs of `skills/tools` @ `ddce3b8` — five tasks, three runs per
variant, executor and judge both `claude` / `claude-opus-5` on one stack.
Report: `reports/tools-2026-08-02.md`.

## Headline

| Task | Claim | `no_skill` | `with_skill` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tools-quiz-001 | x402 SDKs (asked) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| tools-quiz-002 | Hardhat 3 Solidity fuzzing | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| tools-quiz-003 | Blockscout MCP for agent reads | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| tools-quiz-004 | Scaffold-ETH 2 / `create-eth@latest` | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| tools-goal-001 | x402 unprompted while building | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| | | **12/15** | **15/15** |

The stale prior this skill exists to correct is mostly gone on `claude-opus-5`.
Three of the four quizzes are saturated, and every x402 run in both variants
verified package names live against npm (9–20 `npm view`/`npm i` calls each)
rather than answering from memory. Nobody reached for `create-eth-app`.

## The one claim that carries

`tools-quiz-003` is the entire delta. All three `no_skill` runs recommend the
Etherscan API; none names an MCP server. The failures are narrow, not sloppy —
`expect_2`/`expect_3` pass 3/3, so the service named is real and concrete and
nobody proposes scraping or hand-decoding `eth_getLogs`.

**It is not a wiki candidate.** The task notes flagged this as the likeliest
"pure recall" verdict on the theory that a run could search its way there. Two
of the three `no_skill` runs *did* web-search first and still landed on
Etherscan. `tools-goal-001` then reproduces the identical split unprompted, in
the data path each run builds anyway — Etherscan/Alchemy 3/3 vs Blockscout 3/3.
Knows-when-asked and applies-unprompted both clear. → **keep as skill.**

The notes also predicted a `with_skill` split, since L22 lists reads as
"Blockscout MCP *or* Etherscan API", co-equal. It did not happen: 3/3 went
Blockscout, apparently on the unambiguous stack-table row at L85. Recommending
L22 be left alone — the predicted weakness is contradicted by the runs.

## The skill has a bug the runs caught for us

`SKILL.md` L53-62 ships a sample importing `x402Fetch` from `@x402/fetch` and
`createWallet` from `@x402/evm`. **Neither symbol exists** in the 2.x line that
L50, one paragraph above, correctly tells you to install. All three `with_skill`
quiz-001 runs installed the packages, read the actual exports, and contradicted
the skill in writing — one naming its own context: *"My in-house tools reference
gives the right package names but a wrong code sample."* L65's Go path is stale
the same way (`coinbase/x402/go` → the project moved to the x402 Foundation).

Filed as `tools-skill-x402-example-api-nonexistent` with `frequency: 0/6` — a
skill defect no executor reproduced. It was contained only because the model
verifies against npm, and quiz-001's input explicitly asks it to. Fix the sample
and the Go path, then re-evaluate; the install line is already correct, so it is
a self-contained edit.

## Mistake records

- `tools-etherscan-instead-of-blockscout-mcp` — 6/6 `no_skill`, 0/6 `with_skill`
- `tools-x402-v1-line-under-build-pressure` — 1/3 `no_skill`, 0/3 `with_skill`
- `tools-skill-x402-example-api-nonexistent` — skill defect, 0/6

The second is the interesting one. Asked directly, all 6 quiz-001 runs name the
v1/v2 split with publish dates. But building, one `no_skill` run shipped the
frozen v1 line (`x402@^1.2.0`, `x402-express`, `x402-fetch`, `express@^4`) — and
not from ignorance: the transcript shows it installed v2 first, saw
`@x402/core ^2.0.0` in the `@coinbase/x402@2.1.0` tree, correctly said *"a
different package family"*, then cleared the conflict by pinning **down**. That
is the case for keeping a goal task next to the quiz; the quiz alone scores
3/3 vs 3/3 and would have called this claim fully known.

## Eval gaps worth fixing before the next pass

- **`tools-goal-001` expect_3 accepts any "concrete, named package"**, so the run
  that shipped the frozen v1 line passed all three checks. The scoped `@x402/*`
  line is the version-sensitive claim and nothing currently grades it.
- **quiz-001, quiz-002 and quiz-004 are saturated** at 3/3 vs 3/3 and cost ~$14
  per full pass to re-confirm. Retire or re-sharpen rather than re-run as-is;
  quiz-001's value now lives in goal-001.
- **n=3 cannot separate 1/3 from 0/3.** The build-pressure regression is an
  existence proof, not a rate.

## Cost

The skill pays for itself where it replaces a search: quiz-002 126s→77s /
$0.55→$0.30, quiz-003 89s→46s / $1.55→$0.21, goal-001 805s→590s / $4.18→$3.09.
It costs more on quiz-004 (298s→327s, $1.01→$1.60), where the model already knew
the answer and the skill added material to read.

## Integrity notes

All 30 runs are `self_judged: true` — executor and judge are the same agent on
one stack, per "Running a pre-crafted task". The judge still ran blind in a
separate process with no access to the variant, the skill, or the transcript.
Read as same-family grading.

Four executor spawns were aborted before producing a gradeable artifact (two
killed by the orchestrating harness, one by a nested-classifier rejection of a
compound `npm i --prefix` command, one by a session usage limit). None were
graded, none have a run id, each was re-run under a fresh id. One judge call
failed transiently and was re-run against the same already-snapshotted run dir
without re-running the executor. Details in the report.

`.gitignore` gains `artifacts/**/transcript.jsonl` — the raw stream-json form of
the already-ignored `transcript.md`, captured so the notes' transcript-mining
questions (verified vs. remembered vs. read-from-skill) could be answered.

46.title: docs: match the committed-artifacts list to .gitignore
46.body:
Follow-up to #33. `cf69190` flipped `artifacts/**/transcript.md` from ignored to committed without touching the docs, so the two places that enumerate what lands in git are now wrong — in both directions, since the `output/` rule had drifted the other way earlier.

Verified against `git ls-files` on `main` rather than read off `.gitignore`:

| claim | `README.md:38-39` / `AGENTS.md:169` said | actually |
| --- | --- | --- |
| transcripts | gitignored | committed since `cf69190` |
| `output/` | committed | ignored (`artifacts/**/output/`), 0 tracked files |
| `templates/` | gitignored (README only) | committed, 1410 tracked files |

The `templates/` line is the one addition beyond the transcript fix that prompted this PR. It is not a judgement call: `templates/README.md` opens with "Committed snapshots of generated projects", `AGENTS.md:99` says "Every workspace seed … is committed under `templates/`", and `git check-ignore` matches nothing under the directory. Only the README layout box disagreed, and its parenthetical pointed at the wrong file for the regeneration recipe. Easy to drop if you'd rather keep this PR to the transcript change alone.

Docs only — no code, no `.gitignore` change.

47.title: fix: sharpen frontend UX guidance
47.body:
## Summary

Updates `skills/frontend-ux/SKILL.md` based on the findings from #27:

- replaces the ambiguous approval cooldown guidance with an explicit submit → receipt → allowance-refetch lifecycle
- adds a prominent pre-ship checklist around the behaviors that produced the strongest eval delta
- makes ENS recipient handling actionable, including resolution feedback and use of the resolved address
- scopes fiat context to decision points and requires a real, safely handled price source
- calls out target-chain configuration alongside RPC reliability
- makes social metadata guidance work before and after a production domain exists
- adds focused build and interaction verification steps
- removes the unrelated mandatory feedback action

## Why

PR #27 showed the strongest improvements in product identity, ENS-capable inputs, and ETH/USD context. It also exposed an ambiguity in Rule 1: clearing a local flag in `finally` only covers the hash-to-confirmation window if the guarded operation explicitly awaits the receipt and refreshes allowance. This change makes that lifecycle concrete and avoids presenting a fixed sleep as the correctness mechanism.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- documentation-only change

Related: #27, #1

48.title: fix: make QA guidance evidence-driven
48.body:
## Summary

Updates `skills/qa/SKILL.md` based on the findings from #29:

- adds explicit review and remediation modes so fix requests no longer conflict with “report only” instructions
- replaces fixed approval cooldowns with receipt confirmation and authoritative state refetch
- keeps the approve example on `useScaffoldWriteContract` and names `isMining` — not the passed-through wagmi `isPending` — as the confirmation-aware flag
- adds a concrete `externalContracts.ts` migration and validation recipe
- replaces brittle WalletConnect localStorage scraping, hardcoded schemes, and the universal 2-second delay with version-pinned supported metadata and device testing
- removes the stale claim that current SE-2 defaults `--radius-field` to `9999rem`
- makes Phantom, contract-address display, USD context, address components, polling, and RPC fallbacks conditional on product behavior rather than universal blockers
- requires evidence for findings and build/typecheck validation after remediation

## Why

PR #29 demonstrated strong value for the QA checklist in review mode (`0/3 → 3/3`), but also exposed three problems in the skill itself:

1. The skill prohibited fixes while the remediation goal required them.
2. The mobile-linking guidance encoded an unsupported universal timeout and depended on undocumented storage internals.
3. The DaisyUI radius section described a stale template default.

This change preserves the checklist discipline that produced the positive delta while making its instructions safer, current, and applicable to both review and remediation.

## Transaction-lifecycle section

The first pass at that section replaced the two-cooldown recipe with a raw wagmi `writeContractAsync` + `waitForTransactionReceipt(config, { hash })` example, fifteen lines below the rule declaring any raw `useWriteContract` outside scaffold internals a bug. `3b32935` puts the example back on `useScaffoldWriteContract`, which already awaits the receipt through `useTransactor`, leaving the local lock to cover only the authoritative refetch that follows. A trailing note keeps the non-SE2 case: await the receipt explicitly, because the write call alone resolves at the hash.

The same commit corrects the flag name the section depends on. `useScaffoldWriteContract` sets `isMining` before the write and holds it across `waitForTransactionReceipt`; the `isPending` it passes through from wagmi drops when the wallet returns the hash — precisely the gap this section exists to close.

## Scope

Skill-only. The eval-side changes this makes necessary — `qa-quiz-004`'s expects now grading against the new mobile-linking guidance, the goal-001 expects that assume unconditional Phantom/contract-address/deep-link failures, and the `191dcc1` provenance notes across `tasks/qa-*.yaml` — are written up in https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/pull/29#issuecomment-5221932929 and belong with that PR's records.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- checked against `templates/`: `templates/se-2/…/globals.css` ships `--radius-field: 0rem` (confirming the stale default), `externalContracts.ts` uses `satisfies GenericContractsDeclaration` (confirming the migration recipe), and `useScaffoldWriteContract.ts` / `useTransactor.tsx` confirm the `isMining` lifecycle
- documentation-only change

Related: #29, #1

55.title: fix: ground the gas skill in measured numbers, cut what runs ignore
55.body:
Follow-up to the gas eval in #26, applying the two skill recommendations that PR's own report left open, plus the numbers that re-measurement contradicts.

**Based on `eval/gas-claude`, not `main`** — it builds on the L2 Cost Components fix in `70703bd`, so basing on main would revert it. GitHub will retarget this to main when #26 merges. Two files: `skills/gas/SKILL.md` and a new mistake record.

## Why these edits, in the framing of #1

The gas eval landed on **keep as skill**: quiz passes in both variants, `gas-goal-001` goes 0/3 → 3/3. Per the verdict table in #1 that means the value is *the trigger* — the model knows this when asked and fails to think of it mid-build, and a wiki page can't fix that.

The per-section triage in `reports/gas-2026-07-24.md` says the same thing from the other side. Across 24 runs:

- **used:** the when-to-use rule, "why gas dropped", the fee-settings block, the freshness stamp
- **ignored:** both cost tables, the real-world examples, the gas trackers — every run queried live instead
- **caused harm:** the L2 blob example and the dead RPC (both fixed in #26)

So the cached numbers are the part that behaves like a wiki, and they're the part that rotted and got copied wrong. This PR keeps the trigger and the rule and stops shipping a stale almanac underneath them.

## Removed

| Section | Why |
| --- | --- |
| "Mainnet vs L2 Costs" table | Never cited in 24 runs, and after #26's rewrite it contradicted the same file: `$0.002` for a Base swap against the L2 section's `$0.00126`, `$0.001` for a Base ERC-20 transfer against a measured `$0.00052`. |
| "Real-World Cost Examples" | Never cited, and internally inconsistent with the table above it — 10k swaps/day at \$150 implies \$0.015/swap against the table's \$0.036; 10k NFT mints at \$150 implies \$0.015 against \$0.030; "deploy an ERC-20 ~\$0.50" against \$0.240. |
| "Live Gas Trackers" | Triaged "ignored, and redundant": a `no_skill` run fetched a gas tracker unprompted, so the pointer adds nothing over default behaviour. |
| Feedback footer | Report recommendation 5. Refused in 11 of 18 `with_skill` transcripts, costing a paragraph of the closing turn each time. Now backed by `mistakes/gas/gas-feedback-footer-refused.yaml`, which also records that it is **not** a universal convention — it appears in 4 of 19 vendored skills (`ship`, `addresses`, `security`, `frontend-ux`) — and that the fix belongs upstream rather than in each vendored copy. |

## What the numbers are now

Everything measured in **one pass on 2026-08-07** so the whole file shares a window: 9,203 mainnet receipts across 40 blocks spanning ~8 hours, 4,908 Base receipts, ETH \$1,910 from the Chainlink ETH/USD feed.

| Claim | Was (vendored skill) | Now | Provenance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ERC-20 transfer gas | ~65,000 | **45,148** (p25 41,273 / p75 57,424) | n=2,930 |
| ERC-20 approve gas | ~46,000 | **48,549** | n=220 |
| Swap gas | ~180,000 | **183,377** (p25 132k / p75 371k) | n=473 |
| Base fee | 0.1-0.5 gwei | **0.081 gwei** p50, 0.036-0.163 across the window | 40 blocks |
| What a median tx pays | base fee only | **0.151 gwei** all-in, **1.3x** its block's base fee | 9,203 txs |
| Mainnet ERC-20 transfer cost | \$0.013 | **\$0.015** p50 (mean \$0.076, p90 \$0.18) | n=2,930 |
| L2 vs mainnet | "5-10x cheaper" | **~30x** — \$0.00052 on Base vs \$0.015 on mainnet, p50 against p50 | same operation, both chains, same window |
| L1 data share on Base | ~90% (pre-#26) | **0.18%** p50, 0.29% p90 | n=234 |
| Overstatement factor | "100-600x" | **~130x** — a remembered 20 gwei against a 0.151 gwei median | derived from the above |
| Spike-detection snippet | read `feeData.maxFeePerGas` as the base fee | reads `block.baseFeePerGas` | ethers returns ~2x base + tip, so the `> 5 gwei` warning fired at ~2.5 gwei |

## The correction this PR went through

The first commit (`56ccf34`) claimed **"the tip is now most of the bill"** — median tx pays 0.45 gwei all-in, ~3x base — and a **200x** mainnet/L2 gap off a \$0.109 mainnet transfer. Review re-measured both and neither reproduced. They were means reported as medians:

| Statistic | p50 | mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tx price / its block's base fee | **1.3x** | 8.6x |
| priority fee | **0.024 gwei** | 0.49 gwei (p90: 2 gwei) |
| ERC-20 transfer cost | **\$0.015** | \$0.076 (p90: \$0.18) |

The distribution is heavily right-skewed by MEV and arbitrage traffic that an ordinary transfer never competes with, so mean and median differ by 5-8x and the choice of statistic swamps the choice of day. Corroboration from the two endpoints the skill itself prescribes: `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas` returns **0.00001 gwei**, and `cast gas-price` exceeds `cast base-fee` by that same sliver — a model following the skill's own instruction to read the tip would have found the prose contradicting the RPC by three orders of magnitude.

Worse, `56ccf34` left three costs for one operation on one day sitting in one file — \$0.013 base-fee-only, \$0.040 worked example, \$0.109 like-for-like, 8x apart — which is the same defect it removed the old tables for having.

Fixed by making the statistic part of every number rather than by picking better constants. The header bullet now teaches the skew instead of a level; the worked example shows p50 and mean side by side and says which to quote; the gas-used table carries `n` and p25-p75 on every sampled row; and the L2 comparison is p50 against p50.

## Structural change

Dollar columns are gone. In their place:

```
cost_usd = gas_used × gas_price_gwei × 1e-9 × eth_usd
```

plus a gas-used table where every row carries its sample size and spread. Gas used is the durable half — it is a property of the code — but it is not a constant either: an ERC-20 transfer spans 41,273 to 57,424 gas depending on warm slots and whether the recipient already held a balance, so the table gives a range rather than a point. Price is volatile and belongs in an RPC call. This also matches what #1 asks of the quiz tasks — derivation over retrieval. A model that reads this file can no longer answer a cost question by looking up a cell.

Other changes from the same review:

- The fee-settings snippet sets `maxPriorityFeePerGas` as well as `maxFeePerGas` (the report triage names that pair as the clearest skill-attributable delta, 3/3 `with_skill` vs 0/3 controls, so dropping half of it would have cost the thing that was working), guards a null block, and explains that a near-zero suggested tip is real at ~47% full blocks — headroom belongs in `maxFeePerGas`, which you only pay up to, not in the tip, which you pay in full.
- The L1-data and base-fee-floor claims are scoped to OP stack; zk rollups price data differently, so zkSync and Scroll need their own measurement rather than inheriting Base's.

## Unchanged on purpose

- The `description:` frontmatter. It fired on its own in 12/12 `with_skill` runs; don't touch a trigger that works.
- "When to Use Mainnet vs L2", the section the whole benchmark turns on, is kept verbatim — with one paragraph **added** ("what is not a reason to avoid mainnet: cost"). That is the exact failure `gas-goal-001` catches, so flagging it: `with_skill` was already 3/3, so it can't inflate the arm, but it does mean the task loses some power to detect a regression from future skill edits. A re-run should treat this as a new `skill_version` rather than comparing against the `079045f` numbers.

## Not in this PR

The eval-side problems from the same review are separate, since they change grading rather than the skill:

- `gas-quiz-001` expect_3 and `gas-quiz-003` expect_3 hardcode "sub-1-gwei" as an answer key — the same class of bug that retired `gas-quiz-002`. A run during a spike fails for being right. They should key on provenance (did the run fetch it?) rather than magnitude.
- `gas-goal-001` expect_4 gives the judge two thresholds ("single-digit-gwei range (roughly 1-2 gwei)") and passed 12/12, so it has never discriminated. expect_1 also passed 12/12. The 3/3 vs 0/3 verdict rests entirely on expect_3.
- `gas-goal-002` needs the no-signal marker its own report asks for, or it gets re-run.
- `.gitmodules` is committed at the root of #26, pointing into a gitignored workspace.

Happy to open those as a second PR.

Refs #1. Follow-up to #26.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

56.title: fix: sharpen frontend playbook guidance
56.body:
## Summary

Updates `skills/frontend-playbook/SKILL.md` based on the benchmark findings in #31:

- scopes fork mode to integration work that needs copied protocol/token state
- keeps clean-chain development valid for isolated contracts and unit tests
- scopes `create-eth` to SE-2-compatible projects and respects explicitly requested stacks
- requires selecting and recording a tested generator version instead of relying on `latest`
- distinguishes continuous interval mining from valid manual debugging controls
- corrects the Node 25 Web Storage explanation and documents all process-level remedies accepted by the eval
- qualifies what an unchanged CID proves and adds evidence-based build/upload diagnosis

## Why

It also exposes places where the existing text is more absolute than the evidence supports: scaffold selection is context-dependent, manual mining remains useful for debugging, Node supports multiple worker-safe Web Storage remedies, and an unchanged CID proves identical uploaded bytes rather than a unique root cause.

## Validation

- skill-creator `quick_validate.py`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

## Merge order and provenance

This PR is draft and should follow #31, whose mistake records provide the evidence for these edits. It proposes the next vendored revision in this eval repository and should be synchronized upstream before being treated as byte-identical to the live ethskills.com skill.

57.title: fix: reduce gas skill to live measurement workflow
57.body:
## Summary

Alternative follow-up to the gas eval in #26 and to the broader reduction proposed in #55. This takes the minimal-skill direction from [Technophile-04’s issue #1 comment](https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/issues/1#issuecomment-5237465043) to its procedural endpoint.

The skill is reduced from roughly **1,083 words / 149 lines** on the eval branch—and **1,415 words / 157 lines** in #55—to **438 words / 49 lines**. It reached 308/38 before review; the four pointers restored in `633a8c9` account for the difference.

It keeps one behavior and the pointers needed to carry it out:

> Measure current fees before quoting cost or excluding a chain.

How reliably the skill actually induces that is the thing this PR has revised downward — see Results.

## Results

Benchmarked 2026-08-28 at `skills/gas` `017d9dc`, **regraded 2026-08-31** against a rubric that
requires a measurement (see "What changed since the last review"). Executor codex
`gpt-5.6-terra`, judge claude `claude-opus-5`, so **no run is self-judged**. 3 runs per variant
per task.

| Task | `no_skill` | `with_skill` | as first reported |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `gas-goal-001` | 0/3 | **0/3** | *3/3* |
| `gas-goal-002` | 0/3 | **3/3** | 3/3 |
| `gas-quiz-001` | 0/3 | **3/3** | 3/3 |
| `gas-quiz-003` | 1/3 | **3/3** | 3/3 |
| **total** | **1/12** | **9/12** | *12/12* |

**`gas-goal-001` shows no delta.** An earlier version of this PR called it the cleanest signal
in the set; that was an artifact of a rubric with no line requiring a reading, under which a
run that measured nothing scored 4/4. Two did. Of the six skilled runs, one both measured and
converted correctly; two measured nothing at all after reading `SKILL.md`; three measured and
lost the unit — including the only run that passes the corrected rubric, which read 52,042,833
wei, wrote "approximately 52 gwei", and converted Base's 6,000,000 wei to 0.006 gwei correctly
in the same paragraph.

**`gas-goal-002` is the cell this PR stands on:** 3/3 vs 0/3, held through a rubric fix that
made its `expect_5` strictly harder.

The control failures are the behavior the skill targets, not diffuse noise:

- **`gas-quiz-001`** — controls quoted `$5.48` per ERC-20 transfer, a `20 gwei` stress case yielding `$16.10`, and a hardcoded `ETH = $3,500`, while the chain was at 0.045 gwei and ETH at $2,512.
- **`gas-quiz-003`** — two controls quoted mainnet at `$12.35` and `$12.75` per action at 0.06 gwei.
- **`gas-goal-001`** — all three controls chose Base and named cost as the reason without measuring anything. But so did two skilled runs, which is why this task no longer discriminates.

Full write-up in `reports/gas-minimal-2026-08-31.md`. `reports/gas-minimal-2026-08-28.md` is kept, annotated, and superseded.

## What changed since the last review

Rebuilt after [rin-st's review](https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/pull/57#pullrequestreview-5051786597), which was right on every item.

1. **`output/` is committed** for all 39 codex runs (1.1M). None of it shipped before, so no reader could re-check the judge on the material the judge saw.
2. **`yarn verify --regrade` now exists.** It did not — `verify` refused any graded `result.yaml` and built evidence from a workspace it then deleted, so the only answer to an edited expect line was a fresh executor run. That is what made editing a task's `input` look cheaper than editing its `expect`. Every grade now also carries an `expect_sha`.
3. **`gas-goal-001` gained a measurement requirement** and had `expect_3` rewritten from a strict subset of `expect_2` into a unit-consistency check. **`gas-goal-002`'s `expect_5`** now requires the fee breakdown before checking it adds up, instead of rewarding its omission. All 18 runs with committed evidence were regraded — no executor.
4. **Four pointers restored to the skill**: named fallback RPCs (the reduction had regressed a mistake record still marked `fixed`), the L1 data-fee term in the formula, `cast gas-price` vs `cast base-fee`, and named ETH/USD sources. All re-tested live 2026-08-31. 49 lines / 438 words, from 149 originally.
5. **A harness failure is retracted** rather than counted as a model failure, via a new `retracted:` field.
6. Two new mistake records; the four existing ones re-pointed at paragraphs that still exist.

## Honest limits

- **`gas-goal-001` is not trustworthy and needs rebuilding, not patching.** Its corrected rubric depends on a reporting habit the task never asks for: the judge sees `output/`, never the transcript, so the unit-consistency line only bites where a run happens to print the raw reading beside the converted one.
- **Its new expect lines were written after reading the runs they grade**, over two passes. The requirements trace to the skill's own text and to the review, but the order is what it is; both passes are recorded in the task notes.
- **The four skill corrections are unvalidated.** No run set has measured them. Same footing as the wei clause, which is present and did not prevent the error — it recurred in 3 of 6 skilled `gas-goal-001` runs.
- `gas-quiz-001` and `gas-quiz-003` were not regraded (their expect lines did not move), so they carry no `expect_sha`.
- Three runs per cell separates 0/3 from 3/3 reliably; it does not resolve 1/3 from 2/3.
- One executor model, one judge model.

## Token cost

Higher with the skill on build tasks (`gas-goal-001` 40.5k vs 26.9k; `gas-goal-002` 54.2k vs 38.8k), **lower** on direct questions (`gas-quiz-001` 21.4k vs 36.3k; `gas-quiz-003` 24.9k vs 53.3k) — the skill short-circuits research the control does from scratch. That localizes the overhead to build tasks and weakens the case for the proportionality guardrail floated in the 2026-08-10 report.

## Removed to the future wiki

- dated base-fee, tip, ETH-price, block-fullness, and rollup figures
- sampled gas-used tables and percentile discussion
- worked dollar examples
- “Why Gas Dropped 95%+” history
- Dencun/Fusaka narrative
- cached mainnet/L2 cost ratios
- freshness snapshots and fixed spike thresholds
- long fee-setting implementation examples

#26 shows that the trigger and measurement instruction — not cached knowledge — cause the improvement, though `gas-goal-001` no longer contributes to that case. #55 says “Every number below rots” and then retains over 100 lines of dated numbers; this PR removes that contradiction.

## Why not remove the skill entirely?

Weaker than this PR first argued, but still a case.

Gas differs from wallets: the wallets eval found no reliable delta, and this one finds **9/12 vs 1/12**. The three tasks that discriminate all do so for the same reason — the control quotes a remembered gas or ETH price, or rules a chain out without checking, and the skilled run does not.

What no longer holds is the sharper version, that the skill reliably induces live measurement *while building*. `gas-goal-001` is the build task that tests exactly that, and it shows **0/3 vs 0/3**. Two of its six skilled runs read `SKILL.md` and then measured nothing at all; three more measured and lost the unit. Triggering the skill and having it read is demonstrably not sufficient on that task.

So the honest claim is narrower: the skill reliably fixes the answer to a **direct cost question** (`gas-quiz-001` 3/3 vs 0/3, `gas-quiz-003` 3/3 vs 1/3) and to a **build task that names cost as the deliverable** (`gas-goal-002` 3/3 vs 0/3), and does not reliably change behavior on a build task where the cost decision is incidental to shipping a contract. That still justifies a small behavioral nudge over a wiki-only migration. It does not justify calling the measurement instruction dependable, and `gas-goal-001` needs rebuilding before anyone claims otherwise.

Related: #1, #26, #55, #91.

58.title: skills: minimal frontend-ux (alternative to #47)
58.body:
## Summary

Cuts `skills/frontend-ux` from 1100 to 355 words (7.6KB → 2.3KB, roughly 1900 → 590 tokens) — issue #1 step 4, "minimal and thoughtful, remove the why stuff, just have the nudge".

One file, nothing else. **The task specs are deliberately untouched**: this PR exists to answer one question — is the cut safe — and that answer comes from re-running `with_skill`. Change the grading surface in the same PR and a moved result can't be attributed to either cause. The expects stay exactly as #27 measured them.

Alternative to #47 for `SKILL.md` — that PR sharpens the existing structure, this one removes most of it. They conflict on the file, which is the point: it forces an explicit choice rather than letting two versions stack silently. #47's task-yaml fixes are independent of skill size and stand on their own merits either way; if #47 is closed in favour of this, its `quiz-001` `expect_4` clarification is worth picking up separately from `1b5eb8f`.

Draft until #27 lands — the mistake records this rests on are there.

## What the cut is based on

Per-check pass rates read from the raw `result.yaml` files in #27 (3 runs per variant, both goals):

| Rule | no_skill | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R8 metadata / identity | **0/6** | skill carries it entirely |
| R3 ENS address input | **0/3** | skill carries it entirely |
| R4 fiat context | **2/6** | skill carries most of it |
| R5 target chain | 2/3 | weak but real |
| R1 pending, R2 four-state, R6 theme, R7 errors, R9 decimals | **6/6, 3/3 — all pass** | model already carries these |

The cleanest evidence for "nudge, not knowledge" is R3: quiz-005 passes **3/3 without the skill** (the model knows an ENS name has no hex form when asked) while goal-002 fails **0/3 without it** (it doesn't apply that unprompted). Knowledge present, application missing. Same shape for R4.

That makes the parts of the skill that explain *how* — the wagmi approve snippet, the `formatUnits` block, the try/catch — pure context cost: all four quizzes went 12/12 in both variants, so the model derives that code cold.

## What changed

**Kept, with the specificity that makes them actionable** — the four rules that moved outcomes. Concreteness is the nudge: "`isAddress()` silently rejects `vitalik.eth`" changes behavior where "support ENS resolution" did not.

**Compressed to one line each** — R1, R2, R6, R7, R9. Compressed rather than deleted on purpose: the evidence is one stack (claude/opus-4.8), and #27's review caveat 4 says not to generalize the down-weight until another stack confirms it. Five lines is cheap insurance for codex/gpt-5.5.

**Dropped** — the "What You Probably Got Wrong" preamble, all code snippets, both duplicate checklists (the top-of-file checklist and the bottom-of-file verification list restated the rules between them), R5's QPS diagnostics prose, R7's five-step implementation list. The last two are wiki candidates rather than deletions.

**Dropped with no evidence either way, flagging it explicitly:** Rule 3's second half about *displaying* addresses (explorer link, copy-to-clipboard, truncation, blockie). No expect grades it, so nothing supports keeping it — but nothing condemns it either. This is a real content loss, not compression, and it should be a conscious call rather than something that slips through.

## How to test

Coverage first — every graded expect still has a home in the shorter text:

- goal-001 expects 1-8 → four-state bullet, pending bullet, decimals bullet, **Fiat context**, errors bullet, **Product identity**, theme bullet, **Target chain**
- goal-002 expects 1-6 → **Address inputs**, decimals bullet, **Fiat context**, pending bullet, errors bullet, **Product identity**
- quiz-002 → decimals bullet · quiz-003 → four-state bullet · quiz-005 → **Address inputs**
- quiz-001 `expect_4` reads "disabled from click through onchain confirmation and the allowance refetch (submitting flag cleared in `finally` plus a post-confirmation hold)". The first bullet satisfies the main clause — receipt and refetch awaited inside the guarded block, released in `finally`. The parenthetical hold is a mechanism a receipt-awaiting implementation doesn't need, and empirically this judge doesn't require it: quiz-001 passed 3/3 in **both** variants under this wording, on answers that derived `useWaitForTransactionReceipt` + `finally` with no separate hold. Worth clarifying for future stacks — but as #47 does it, not here.

Then the actual test, which is issue #1 step 5 — a fresh benchmark of both goals against this revision, landed on this branch (artifacts + report) before it leaves draft: 3 × `no_skill` + 3 × `with_skill` per goal, one stack start to finish (claude / opus-5, fresh blind judge on the same model), reported separately from #27. `no_skill` re-runs too — comparing fresh `with_skill` against #27's July baseline would blend stacks and judges, which AGENTS.md forbids ("never blend them in one table"). Quizzes are skipped as non-discriminating: 12/12 in both variants in #27, and their claims are covered by the mapping above.

Twelve runs total. Any expect that drops from #27's 6/6 marks where the compression went too far — that is the signal this PR exists to produce.

Also verified locally: `git diff --check` clean, frontmatter parses, `setup-workspace.ts` only copies the directory and records the repo sha, so nothing structural depends on the removed sections.

## Worth a reviewer's attention

- The `description:` frontmatter is now the whole trigger surface. If it is too narrow the skill never loads and the eval measures nothing, so it names all four things by name.
- `frontend-ux` is a skill the evidence **keeps** (goals went 0/6 → 6/6), unlike gas. It just does not need 1100 words to do it.
- It overlaps `frontend-playbook` (362 lines) — a candidate for the combining pass in step 7, not now.

59.title: skills: minimal protocol status guidance

## Summary

Reduces skills/protocol/SKILL.md from 1,931 to 212 words and narrows it to the one behavior PR #32 showed the skill changes: checking live protocol sources and classifying commitment against a named fork.

The shorter skill:

- requires live verification instead of roadmap or parametric-memory claims

Those added context but produced no correctness uplift in #32: both variants passed 6/6, while with_skill added 32-43% wall-clock cost. The static fork table was also already becoming stale inside an anti-staleness skill.

## Basis

This follows issue #1 step 4 and the minimal-skill direction in issue comment 5237465043: preserve the behavioral nudge, move explanatory knowledge out of the skill, and rerun the same evaluation afterward.

62.title: eval: addresses (claude)
62.body:
Benchmark of `skills/addresses` per #1. 36 runs — 6 tasks x 2 variants x 3 runs — executor and judge both claude / `claude-opus-5`, one stack start to finish. Skill vendored at `326ad4b`.

## Results

| task | no_skill | with_skill | failing check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 — Base swap venue + router address | **3/3** | **2/3** | expect_1 (Base-liquidity evidence) |
| quiz-002 — Uniswap v4 differs per chain | **3/3** | **3/3** | — |
| quiz-003 — vanity CREATE2 proves nothing cross-chain | **3/3** | **3/3** | — |
| quiz-004 — deprecated V1 VELO token | **3/3** | **3/3** | — |
| quiz-005 — per-chain Aave pools + native USDC | **3/3** | **2/3** | expect_4 (source attribution) |
| goal-001 — unprompted viem swap build | **2/3** | **3/3** | expect_6 (verify-before-funds) |
| **total** | **17/18** | **16/18** | |

## The finding

**The quiz half found no benefit; the goal half found the one the skill was written for.** Quizzes `13/15 vs 15/15`, goal-001 `3/3 vs 2/3`.

`no_skill` never guessed. Every unaided run probed the chain — `codesize` on candidate routers, `symbol()`/`name()` for token identity, `defaultFactory()`/`voter()` to prove a router belongs to the protocol claimed, quoter sims pinned to a block — or confirmed against an official deployment list. The stale-prior model the skill was written against does not survive tool access.

`with_skill` behaved identically on all five quizzes — consult, answer, stop — and that single behaviour produced four different outcomes, decided entirely by whether the skill's claim was true. True on quiz-002 and quiz-004: 3/3 each, 3-4x faster. False on quiz-001: fail. True-but-circularly-sourced on quiz-005: fail.

goal-001 is the exception and the argument for keeping the skill: nothing is asked, so the discipline has to surface on its own. All three `with_skill` runs told the developer to verify addresses before moving funds; one `no_skill` run did not.

## Skill defects found

Four mistake records under `mistakes/addresses/`. Two are content errors the runs caught rather than propagated:

- **L462 says Morpho isn't on Arbitrum.** It is, at `0x6c247b1F...`. All three `with_skill` runs checked anyway; one wrote the correction into its answer unprompted.
- **Slipstream appears nowhere in the file.** The Aerodrome section lists only the vAMM `Router`. A run quoting every candidate at real clip size measured that router at **-1,283 bps** against Slipstream's **-14 bps** on the exact trade the skill is consulted for. Nothing about the address is wrong — it just isn't the right router for the question the skill invites.
- **L353/L357's TVL claim is false** and its `~$500-600M` was copied verbatim into the failing quiz-001 answer. Aerodrome leads Base by routed volume, Uniswap by TVL.
- **The "Last Verified: March 3, 2026" stamp reads as a completed check** — 2/6 runs shipped addresses to live-funds config citing the skill itself as the source.

## Notes for review

- Every run carries `judge.self_judged: true`: same agent family for executor and judge, as AGENTS.md prescribes when one harness is available (`codex` is not installed here). The judge is still a separate blind process that never sees the variant, skill, or transcript.
- All six tasks are bare-workspace, so deliverables land in gitignored `output/`. The report quotes the graded evidence inline, and committed `transcript.md` files contain the file writes.
- Runs 1-31 were executed concurrently and exhausted a rate-limit window; five goal-001 runs died mid-flight and were **discarded, not graded** — their run ids were deleted and re-run from scratch. The final five ran serially in 57 minutes. Serial is the recommended default: goal-001 runs carry 1.8M-4.8M cache-read tokens each.
- Two runs independently flagged the `ethskills.com/feedback` instruction at the end of SKILL.md as a phone-home vector and declined to act on it. Ungraded, but the authors may want to know.

Report: `reports/addresses-2026-08-12.md`

65.title: eval: audit (claude)
65.body:
Results for `skills/audit` on the claude stack. 24 runs — 4 tasks × 2 variants × 3 — executor and judge both `claude-opus-5`, strictly serial, one sitting.

Report: `reports/audit-2026-08-12.md`.

## Headline

Every run passed every expect. **12/12 with_skill vs 12/12 no_skill.**

goal-001 read as a count per its notes rather than as a pass: **11/11 planted findings caught by both arms in all six runs**, with expect_12 (severity ranking) passing every time. Contrary to the spec's expectation of `pass: false` on both arms, all six recorded `pass: true`. There is no headroom on this model in which variant separation could appear.

## What the transcripts show

**The skill's headline mechanism never ran.** Phase 3 — one Opus sub-agent per routed domain, each writing `findings-<domain>.md` — produced **zero** Task-tool calls across all twelve with_skill runs. goal-001 run 1 fetched ten checklists and then worked every one inline in its own context. The question this eval was built to ask (does routing a domain sub-agent per area surface bugs a single careful read misses?) was never actually put to the test: the routing happened, the fan-out did not.

**The skill went unloaded in half its runs** — 6/12, including 3/3 on quiz-002 and one goal-001 run that listed the workspace, opened `SKILL.md`, read the routing table, and then audited without fetching anything. Those six are no_skill reruns wearing a with_skill label.

**The three mirrored claims are not stale priors on Opus 5.** no_skill named the Chainlink L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed and its grace period, got Arbitrum's `block.number` → L1 semantics right (including on goal-001, unprompted, where only flagging the clock was required), and prescribed both a signed nonce and deadline plus the constructor-cached domain separator — three times each, with no lookups.

**Cost went up, accuracy did not.** On goal-001, the runs that loaded the skill cost 27% more and took 36% longer for the same 11/11. No accuracy regression either way, and no false positives in any of the six audit reports.

Also worth noting: the two with_skill runs that loaded the skill never compiled anything, so the `forge build` lint warnings that were expected to hand three expects to both arms actually went only to the arm *without* the skill. Both arms still hit 11/11.

## Records

- `artifacts/audit-{quiz-001,quiz-002,quiz-003,goal-001}/` — 6 runs each, `result.yaml` + `transcript.md`
- `mistakes/audit/audit-subagent-phase-never-fires.yaml` — 6/6 of the runs that loaded the skill
- `mistakes/audit/audit-skill-not-invoked.yaml` — 6/12 with_skill runs

## Provenance and hygiene

- Checklist repo (`austintgriffith/evm-audit-skills`, unpinned) sha `ffe4b67` before the first run and after the last — unchanged, so every with_skill run read the same checklists. `skill_version` `2f0adb0` records the loader in `skills/audit`, not the checklists.
- No run attempted `gh issue create` (Phase 5 self-skipped as designed; the two grep hits were the skill's own text loading into context). No run modified `src/`. No run left a stray `findings-<domain>.md` — a side effect of the sub-agent phase not firing — so **all 24 gradings were blind**.
- `self_judged: true` on all 24 runs: `verify` sets it when judge agent equals executor agent, which is what a one-stack benchmark means. The judge was a fresh, blind process on `claude-opus-5` seeing only input, expects and the snapshotted workspace.
- One clean stop mid-run at 0.94 rate-limit utilization, aborted before `setup` so no partial run dir; resumed on the next window.

## Recommendation

The report answers the last row honestly: **the eval is the wrong artifact for this model, not the skill.** All four tasks are ceilinged. The 381-line fixture with eleven individually well-known bugs is within reach of one careful read, which is what happened six times out of six. Recovering discrimination needs a fixture where context, not knowledge, is the binding constraint — thousands of lines across a dozen contracts, bugs needing cross-contract reasoning, graded on coverage-under-budget — or a weaker executor. The quizzes are worth keeping as cheap regression canaries, but they document that these claims are no longer stale rather than measuring the skill.

Separately, the skill itself should either spawn the sub-agents Phase 3 describes or stop describing a mechanism it does not invoke.
