66.title: fix: isolate eval workspaces
66.body:
Trimmed to the #63 fix, as discussed in the thread. The rest is split out: #70 (transcript format), #71 (workspace cloning), #72 (moving workspaces out of the tree).

## What this fixes

Issue #63 recorded a run that had to be thrown away. Four of its symptoms have harness causes:

| Symptom in #63 | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runs graded before their executor finished | Nothing tied the executor process to `verify` — the spawn was the one loop step left to hand-written shell | `run-executor` owns the spawn and records when it finished; `verify` will not grade without that |
| Verification removed workspaces executors were still using | Same | Same gate |
| Parallel verification hit a git-index race | Workspaces had no repo of their own, so every git command resolved to *this* repo's index | Each workspace is its own git repo |
| quiz-003 executors committed their `/greetings` work to the local `main` | Same | Same |

One caveat on the last row. It is what #63 reports, but codex's `workspace-write` sandbox denies writes inside `.git`, and every run of a repo-shaped task in #67 said so outright — so how those commits reached `main` is unexplained. That run may have been configured differently, or the commits may not have come from the executor at all. The fix holds either way, and the `npm install` case below is confirmed independently.

## Root cause

Tooling resolves context by walking **up** the filesystem, and the workspace sat inside this repo. Being gitignored is not a boundary — measured:

```
$ cd <workspace> && git add .
The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: …
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.     # exit 1 — and an executor told to commit takes the hint

$ git add -A                 # exit 0, stages the orchestrator's tracked files, deletions included
$ git commit -am "done"      # exit 0, lands them on the checked-out branch

$ npm prefix
/…/ethskills-evals           # the framework's own manifest, two directories up
```

## What changed

**1. Executor lifecycle** (`scripts/run-executor.ts`, new)

- Builds the CLI invocation per executor, so the load-bearing flags cannot be forgotten: `--setting-sources project` for claude, `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true` for codex.
- Streams both output channels to disk as they arrive, and records `started` / `finished` / `exit` / `model` in `executor.yaml`.
- Refuses a second pass over a workspace that already ran.
- `verify` hard-fails until `finished` is set. A killed run stays ungradeable by design: it is a dead run, not a zero.

**2. A git repo per workspace** (`lib/workspace.ts`, `setup-workspace`)

`setup` git-inits each workspace and makes a baseline commit; the sha lands in `<run-dir>/baseline.sha`. Identity is set on the workspace repo so an executor's `git commit` works and is not attributed to the human. Installed dependencies stay out through `.git/info/exclude` — not a `.gitignore` the executor reads and the judge sees in the diff.

`verify` diffs against that baseline rather than the index: an executor that commits its own work leaves a clean worktree, and the old `git diff` called that an empty run.

**3. A stub `package.json`** for workspaces that have none, so npm's walk stops at the workspace. This is the fifth symptom, found on the way and reported independently in the standards eval: a bare workspace resolved to this repo as its npm project root, so `npm install` inside a run rewrote the framework's own manifest. The stub rides in the baseline commit, so it never appears in a diff, and the snapshot skips it by content match.

**4. Grading integrity** (`scripts/verify.ts`)

- `--judge-agent` is now required. The silent fallback to the run's own executor made a batch graded by a forgotten flag indistinguishable from one graded on purpose — which is exactly how #63 read.
- Evidence shape follows the task spec (`template:` → diff, bare → snapshot) rather than the presence of `.git`, which every workspace now has.
- `result.yaml` gains `executor_model` and `executor_exit`; AGENTS.md asked for the model to be recorded and nothing did.
- `output/` is no longer gitignored. It is the material the judge graded, and for 89 of 96 tasks it is the only copy — a few KB of `answer.md` per run. The old rule predates the shape-based split, when repo-shaped runs snapshotted a whole scaffold there.

## Verification

- Guard paths exercised: missing `--judge-agent`, missing `executor.yaml`, `finished: null`, a second `run-executor` pass, `git add -N` with a root `node_modules` present.
- Both task shapes end to end with a haiku executor and judge: bare → `output/answer.md` captured, `npm prefix` resolving to the workspace; repo-shaped with an executor that **commits** its change → non-empty `run.diff`, empty under the old code.
- The real thing: #67 ran 30 orchestration runs on codex `gpt-5.6-terra` on this harness, six executors in parallel at peak with no index contention.

## Limits

- Runs created by the previous harness cannot be graded by the new `verify` (no `executor.yaml`). Set them up again — none exist today, every committed run carries `pass:`.
- Long runs still have to be detached; `verify` blocks until `executor.yaml` shows `finished`.
- codex's `workspace-write` sandbox denies writes inside `.git`, so a codex executor cannot commit its work. Evidence is unaffected — the diff is taken against the baseline and covers the worktree — but a task whose prompt asks for committed code is asking for something the sandbox forbids.
- The two markers stop the tools that own them and nothing else; an executor can still read its way up the filesystem. That is what #72 is about.

Refs #63.

67.title: eval: orchestration (codex-gpt-5.6-terra)
67.body:
## What this is

Runs of `skills/orchestration` across four tasks, three per variant, executed and graded by Codex `gpt-5.6-terra` on the harness from #66. Thirty runs in all: quiz-003 has two sets, its first void — see below.

| Task | Shape | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 — explorer key for verification | question | **0/3** | **3/3** |
| quiz-002 — Phase 3 bug remediation loop | question | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| quiz-003 — scaffold hooks (deletion test) | repo | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| goal-001 — localhost → public URL runbook | question | 0/3 | 1/3 |

Read the per-check tables in `reports/`, not the aggregate: three of the four tasks turn on a single expect line.

## What the runs say about the skill

**Keep** the Phase 2 rule that verification needs no explorer key and runs immediately after deploy. quiz-001 is the cleanest result in the set — every no-skill answer preserved the ticket's false premise that a key must arrive from ops, every with-skill answer rejected it. The claim was revalidated against `create-eth@2.0.23` before the runs: the generated Foundry project still ships the default `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY`, copies the example env on postinstall, and exposes `yarn verify`.

**Add** explicit go/no-go gates at the phase transitions. goal-001's two with-skill failures are both expect 5: the plans had plenty of checks but never spelled out all three required transitions.

**Delete** the scaffold-hooks block. quiz-003 is the pre-registered deletion test and both arms pass all four checks — the SE2 workspace's own `AGENTS.md` already gets agents to scaffold reads, writes, event history and generated identity, and the skill's block adds nothing on top but about a quarter more tokens per run. That is the first row of the task's own decision rule.

Three mistake records mined: `orchestration-stale-verification-key`, `orchestration-transition-gates-implicit`, `orchestration-generated-registry-churn`.

## quiz-003 ran twice

The first set read `no_skill` 3/3 against `with_skill` 1/3. Both failures were the same check, expect_4, which asked that `deployedContracts.ts` "is not hand-edited" — and neither run had hand-edited it. The entries they added carry `inheritedFunctions` and `deployedOnBlock`, written by `generateTsAbis.js`, and their transcripts show `yarn deploy` and the generator running. The task's notes had already called that path the executor's call and ungraded.

The judge could not have got it right: it grades a diff, and a diff shows a file's text, not its origin. The check asked about something the evidence does not contain.

`3f2ee01` fixed the spec — expect_4 now grades only what a diff can answer, and the input no longer asks for committed code, which codex's `workspace-write` sandbox forbids. `982947c` is the re-run, and both fixes show in it: one run regenerated the registry and passed, the case that failed twice before, and the sandbox complaint about committing went from every run of the first set to none of the second. The first six runs stay in `artifacts/` — runs are append-only — and the report says which set counts.

## What is in the artifacts

Per run: `result.yaml`, `baseline.sha`, `workspace.path`, `executor.yaml`, `transcript.md`, and the evidence the judge graded — `output/answer.md` or `output/LAUNCH.md` for question-shaped tasks, `run.diff` against the workspace baseline for quiz-003.

## Caveats

- **Every verdict is `self_judged: true`.** One stack, start to finish: each grade ran in a fresh blind codex process that never saw the variant, the skill, or the transcript, but it is the same model that produced the run. Each report says so at the top.
- **The first 24 transcripts were re-rendered after the fact.** They were originally ~400 bytes each: `run-executor` took codex's stdout as the transcript, and codex puts only its final message there. Fixed in #66, and rebuilt from the raw session logs the harness kept beside them, by the function that writes them now. The quiz-003 re-run wrote its transcripts natively.
- **codex cannot commit inside its own sandbox.** `workspace-write` allows source edits but carves out `.git`, so `git add` / `git commit` fail on `index.lock: Operation not permitted`. Every run of the first quiz-003 set said so; the prompt now asks for finished code in the working tree instead. Worth knowing for any future repo-shaped task: on this stack, a prompt that asks for a commit is asking for something the sandbox denies.
- goal-001 `with_skill` 1/3 is not "the skill barely helps": all three no-skill runs failed, and all with-skill failures are the same single gate check.
- **quiz-003 is named a quiz but grades applies-unprompted in a repo.** Its result does not belong in the "quiz" column of the verdict matrix in #1, which reads quiz as knows-when-asked and goal as applies-unprompted. Read it as a second goal task.

## Base

Targets #66 (`fix/workspace-isolation`), which this branch merges — the harness changes have to land first. Merge #66, then this.

## Follow-ups

Not in this PR: it records runs, and changing the skill it was measured against would invalidate what it records. Each has evidence above or in `reports/`.

- [ ] Delete the scaffold-hooks block from `skills/orchestration`. Both arms of the deletion test pass without it. See `reports/orchestration-quiz-003-2026-08-13.md`.
- [ ] Optionally keep one line of it as a guard: frontend-only work does not deploy or regenerate `deployedContracts.ts` unless deployment was asked for. Mistake record: `orchestration-generated-registry-churn` (1/3 with_skill, 0/3 no_skill — extra work, not a failed check).
- [ ] Add explicit go/no-go gates to the phase transitions — local tests and deploy before Base, a small-real-money journey before the public frontend, a public-URL smoke test after deploy. Both goal-001 with-skill failures are this one check. Mistake record: `orchestration-transition-gates-implicit`.

68.title: skill: minimize tools from eval findings
68.body:
## Summary

- reduce the tools skill to the behavioral nudges supported by the PR #45 results

- correct the x402 2.x TypeScript guidance and Go module path, and warn against dependency-conflict fallback to the frozen v1 packages

  (18 of those runs are `with_skill` and carry a `skill_version`; the 15 `no_skill`
  records carry `null`)

The broader Hardhat, Scaffold-ETH, RPC, faucet, and command reference material was
removed because those claims were already saturated without the skill. This follows
the minimal-skill direction discussed in #1. The saturated tasks are otherwise
unchanged for one comparison rerun; they can then be retired or redesigned.

## Codex results

| Task | `no_skill` | `with_skill` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tools-quiz-001 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| tools-quiz-002 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| tools-quiz-003 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| tools-quiz-004 | 3/3 | 1/3 |

The two quiz-004 failures are grading false negatives — both runs verified live that
`create-eth@latest` resolves to `2.0.23` and gave the reproducible pin, which expect_2

`tools-eval-rejects-current-create-eth-pin`. Three `with_skill` reruns after the

reported separately from the 30-run headline.

Note that quiz-003 is 3/3 for both variants here, against 0/3 vs 3/3 on claude-opus-5
in #45. The Blockscout claim is retained on the #45 evidence.

## Post-review corrections

Two defects found reviewing this branch against the live npm and Go registries, after
the runs were graded:

- **x402 signature.** The skill asserted `wrapFetchWithPayment(fetch, account)` with a
  viem `LocalAccount`. That is the 1.x shape (`x402-fetch@1.2.0` takes `walletClient:
  Signer | MultiNetworkSigner`); every published 2.x — `@x402/fetch` 2.19 through 2.23
  — takes `client: x402Client | x402HTTPClient`, with `wrapFetchWithPaymentFromConfig`
  as the account-carrying convenience. The mistake record it came from had prescribed
  the wrong fix. All 12 goal transcripts across both stacks contradict it: every run
  built the client with `ExactEvmScheme`, none passed a bare account. The skill no
  longer pins a signature — it names the dead symbols and defers to the installed types.
- **`tools-goal-001` expect_3.** The tightened check listed `@coinbase/x402` as a
  deprecated package disqualifying a run. It is not deprecated: `@coinbase/x402@2.1.0`
  is the current Coinbase facilitator config, depends on `@x402/core ^2.0.0`, and is
  the ordinary way to settle on Base mainnet — which is what this task asks for. The
  rejection is now scoped to the v1 line. No run in this benchmark would have flipped.

`tools-skill-x402-example-api-nonexistent` is closed with the corrected pattern;
`tools-x402-v1-line-under-build-pressure` has its stale "not graded" note updated.

## Validation

- `loadTaskSpec` parses `tasks/tools-goal-001.yaml` (3 expects, `runs: 3`)
- all four `mistakes/tools/*.yaml` parse
- `git diff --check`
- package claims checked against the npm registry and the Go module proxy:
  `@x402/*` 2.23.0 (2026-08-18) vs unscoped `x402`/`x402-fetch`/`x402-express` frozen
  at 1.2.0 since 2026-04-16; `github.com/x402-foundation/x402/go/v2` at v2.23.0, while
  `github.com/coinbase/x402/go` returns HTTP 200 with the pseudo-version
  `v0.0.0-20260421184015-dd927a26cfef` (2026-04-21) — it does not error, it silently
  resolves to a stale pre-Foundation commit, which is a worse trap than an error and is
  now what SKILL.md says; `create-eth@latest` = 2.0.23

## Open decisions

- The `create-eth@latest` instruction is fitted to the quiz-004 check this PR files as
  broken. The alternative is to fix `tools-quiz-004` expect_2 per the mistake record
  and drop the instruction — SE-2 is 3/3 vs 3/3 on both stacks with no skill.
- Hardhat 3 was cut on pass rate, but quiz-002 carried the largest measured saving on
  claude-opus-5 (126s→77s, $0.55→$0.30) and this Codex benchmark records neither cost
  nor duration. Relevant to the cost-in-the-verdict-table question in #1.
- ~~The rewritten expect_3 has only run on codex.~~ Re-run on claude-opus-5, 3 per
  variant, `reports/tools-goal-001-2026-08-19.md`: **3/3 vs 3/3**, and 4 of the 6 runs
  shipped `@coinbase/x402@^2.1.0` inside a clean `@x402/*@^2.23.0` build — the ordinary
  Base-mainnet shape the pre-correction wording called deprecated. No run passed a bare
  viem account to `wrapFetchWithPayment`; all six used `ExactEvmScheme`.
  ~~The v1 regression did not recur.~~ **Corrected in review:** no run *shipped* the v1
  line, but 2 of 3 `no_skill` runs installed it into `package.json` first and migrated
  off after reading the installed types. Across both claude benchmarks the record now
  reads 3/6 reached / 1/6 shipped `no_skill`, 0/6 `with_skill` on either count — another
  instance of the graded-surface-saturated / ungraded-read-separates pattern below.
- New, from that rerun: the graded surface is saturated while the **ungraded** read still
  separates the arms — `with_skill` 3/3 Blockscout (two also wiring
  `mcp.blockscout.com/mcp`), `no_skill` split Etherscan / Blockscout / raw `eth_getLogs`.
  The run that hand-decoded logs — the thing the skill tells you not to do — passed 3/3,
  because the expects grade the payment mechanism, not the data path. Concrete instance of
  the resolution problem raised in #1. Cost on that task: 1277s/$6.76 `no_skill` vs
  808s/$4.66 `with_skill` (−37% / −31%).

Based on #45 and #1.

## Review round 2

rin-st's review is addressed in `cb7e82d`. Verified every claim in it against the
transcripts, the npm registry, and the Go module proxy before applying; all of it held.

- **The blocking item was right.** The report's "the v1 regression did not recur" was
  wrong; `tools-x402-v1-line-under-build-pressure` now counts reached (3/6) separately
  from shipped (1/6). One near-miss is excluded and said so: `2026-08-01T214602Z-claude-no-skill-1`
  installed the v1 packages into a throwaway `/tmp` probe dir to read their types, then
  built on `@x402/*@2.20.0`. Inspecting the frozen line is not standing on it.
- **expect_3 split into expect_3 + expect_4**, per the review, so a `fail` says which
  conjunct broke. It now names the frozen *package identities* at any version range —
  `"x402-fetch": "latest"` resolves to 1.2.0 too, and a blind judge cannot know that —
  and no longer hardcodes `2.x`. Existing records carry `expect_1..expect_3`; no run on
  either stack would flip under the new wording.
- **The `create-eth` tension is resolved rather than flagged.** `tools-quiz-004`
  expect_2 now accepts a live-verified pin, `tools-eval-rejects-current-create-eth-pin`
  is `status: fixed`, and the skill line no longer forbids a pin — which is what
  contradicted its own "treat versions as live data" opener. The two codex records that
  failed the old wording keep their grades. What that leaves genuinely open is narrower:
  the skill's `create-eth` instruction now has neither a broken check propping it up nor
  a measured uplift, so its place in a minimal skill is an issue #1 question.
- **Bookkeeping:** dead shas repointed (18 records, not 33 — the other 15 codex runs are
  `no_skill` with `skill_version: null`), `skill_section` anchors moved off line numbers,
  frontmatter narrowed to what the body still covers, `tools-quiz-002` and
  `tools-quiz-004` annotated as orphaned by the cut rather than retired.

One thing worth flagging in the other direction: the skill moved again in this commit
(frontmatter, x402 paragraph, `create-eth` line, Go trap), so the current revision has
not been benchmarked. The 2026-08-19 numbers are `090cf26`'s, and both reports now say
so explicitly.

69.title: eval: building-blocks (claude/opus-5)
69.body:
Five pre-crafted `building-blocks` tasks, 3 runs per variant, executor and judge both `claude` / `claude-opus-5`, content-only trigger. Report: `reports/building-blocks-2026-08-14.md`.

## Result

| Task | `no_skill` | `with_skill` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `quiz-001` — Base DEX pick | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `quiz-002` — Aerodrome fee model | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `quiz-003` — Aave V3 flash-loan fee | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `quiz-004` — Arbitrum yield stack | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `goal-001` — V4 dynamic-fee hook | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **Total** | **15/15** | **15/15** |

**The skill did not improve pass rate, because nothing was left to improve.** Every stale prior these tasks target failed to reproduce on Opus 5. No control run defaulted to Uniswap on Base, applied the Uniswap LP-earns-fees model to Aerodrome, quoted the 0.09% V2 flash-loan rate, reached for GLP over GM pools, or built the dynamic-fee hook on anything but V4. Controls reached for live data on their own — DefiLlama, Aerodrome source on GitHub, `FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TOTAL` read off the Aave Pool with `cast`, and in one case an anvil mainnet fork to measure gas empirically.

All six `goal-001` runs compiled and tested green (34, 23, 18, 16, 16 and 24 tests), verified from the transcripts since the judge cannot execute code.

## What the skill did change: cost

| Task | Duration | Tokens | Cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `quiz-001` | 720s → **374s** | 1.26M → **0.58M** | $2.36 → **$1.37** |
| `quiz-002` | 219s → **146s** | 156k → **125k** | $0.69 → **$0.47** |
| `quiz-003` | 393s → **266s** | 404k → **177k** | $1.15 → **$0.77** |
| `quiz-004` | 195s → **160s** | 104k → 116k | $0.57 → **$0.52** |
| `goal-001` | 793s → **753s** | 3.22M → **2.92M** | $3.85 → **$3.48** |

`with_skill` runs on the quiz tasks often answer from the skill with no web or RPC calls at all — `Skill → Read → Write` in ~155s against controls spending 190–255s reading Aerodrome source to reach the same answer.

## Mistakes filed

That shortcut is also how the skill's own stale facts reach the output. Neither is caught by any expect line.

- **`building-blocks-aero-merger-tense`** (`with_skill` 3/6, `no_skill` 2/6) — SKILL.md L16/L169 state the Aerodrome/Velodrome merger into Aero as completed; it was announced Nov 2025 and is still unlaunched, targeting Sep 2026. One run repeats it *inside* a "verify every address onchain before deploy" warning. Two controls hold the same belief unaided, so the skill confirms an existing error rather than creating one. Predicted by quiz-001's notes and already flagged from the addresses side.
- **`building-blocks-base-dominance-asserted`** (`with_skill` 1/3, `no_skill` 0/3) — one run picked its venue in 162s with no lookup, asserted "Aerodrome is the dominant DEX" from L169, and declined on principle to quote any depth figure. `expect_1` says a dominance claim asserted rather than shown fails; the judge passed it. A judge false-pass, not a scoring artifact.

## Recommended follow-ups

**Skill:** re-tense the merger at L16/L169 (same fix needed in `skills/l2s` and `skills/addresses`); replace "~$500-600M TVL / dominant" with the actual split — Aerodrome leads Base routed volume, Uniswap leads Base TVL — plus an instruction to check DefiLlama for the specific pair. The fee model, the 0.05% fee, and the V4 material are correct and carried runs to full passes faster than controls.

**Eval:** `quiz-001` `expect_1` needs a dated-figure requirement the judge cannot read past; add a merger-tense expect somewhere; all five tasks are now saturated on this stack and need harder targets to stay informative.

## Notes

All runs are recorded `self_judged: true` — the harness sets that flag whenever `judge.agent == executor`, which is unavoidable for a single-stack claude benchmark run as AGENTS.md prescribes. Each judgment still ran blind in a fresh `claude -p` process that never saw the variant, the skill, or the transcript.

`skill_version: ff8a521` in the records is a commit on `fix/minimal-gas-skill`, the branch checked out while the runs executed. `skills/building-blocks/` and `tasks/building-blocks-*` are byte-identical between that commit and `origin/main`, so the sha identifies the same skill content; this branch is cut from `origin/main`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

70.title: harness: one transcript format across stacks
70.body:
Stacked on #66.

`codex exec` is the mirror of claude: the session log — reasoning, every exec and its output, patches, token count — goes to stderr, and stdout carries only the final message. `run-executor` took stdout as the transcript, so a codex run committed a ~400 byte `transcript.md` that reads as if the agent did nothing, while its 60–170 KB session log sat in `executor.stderr`, a file named for errors. Measured across one 24-run benchmark: 68 KB of committed transcripts against 1.4 MB of session logs that were not committed at all.

That matters because AGENTS.md asks for transcripts to be mined — which pointers the skill actually surfaced, whether it was opened at all — and the mining would silently read the wrong file for half the stacks.

Rendering moves to `lib/transcript.ts` and takes both streams; the executor decides which one is the session. Both raw captures are streamed to disk as they arrive (a killed run keeps what it had) and both are gitignored, the rule claude's stream-json already had.

Verified on both stacks: a codex run assembles the full session, a claude run renders as before.

71.title: harness: clone template workspaces instead of copying them
71.body:
Stacked on #66.

A repo-shaped template with its dependencies installed is 1.9 GB across 237k files, and every run gets a copy. The system `cp` can clone instead — copy-on-write shares the data blocks, so a workspace only pays for what the executor changes.

Measured on `templates/se-2-foundry` with `node_modules` installed, macOS/APFS:

| | time | disk per workspace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fs.cp` (before) | 91s | 1.9 GB |
| `cp -Rc` (after) | 48s | 830 MB |

The clone is not free: every file still needs its own inode and directory entry, and at this file count that metadata is most of the 830 MB. Node's own `COPYFILE_FICLONE` is no help at all — measured 3.5 GB copied and 3.5 GB of disk gone — hence shelling out.

The disk column is the APFS figure, and it does not carry to every host. The two flags disagree about a filesystem that cannot clone: macOS `-c` fails and lands on the portable `fs.cp` path, while `--reflink=auto` never fails — it degrades to a plain copy, so an ext4 host (most CI runners) gets the speed but still pays the full 1.9 GB. `--reflink=always` would surface that, at the cost of dropping those hosts onto `fs.cp`, the slowest of the three; the degraded copy is the deliberate trade.

On a six-run benchmark of a template that size this is ~4 minutes, and on a CoW filesystem ~6 GB of peak disk.

Not pure performance after all — review on this PR turned up four things in the `fs.cp` fallback, all fixed in `harness: make the fs.cp fallback a real fallback`. It now clears the destination first (it was merging into whatever partial tree a failed `cp` left behind), passes `verbatimSymlinks` (it was rewriting every relative `node_modules/.bin` link into an absolute path back into the shared template, undoing the isolation #66 establishes), aborts rather than restarting the copy when `cp` is killed by a signal, and reports `cp`'s stderr when it does fall back.

72.title: harness: move workspaces out of the repo tree
72.body:
Stacked on #66. This is the part of the original PR worth arguing separately — see the thread in #66.

#66 gives each workspace its own git repo and a stub `package.json`, which stops git and npm at the workspace. Both are markers, and a marker stops the tool that owns it and nothing else. What neither touches:

- **the neighbourhood.** The workspace sits inside its run dir, so `ls ../..` from it reaches sibling runs of the same task — their `answer.md`, `run.diff` and `result.yaml`, now committed and therefore on every machine — and `tasks/` with every expect line is two directories further up. No marker stops an `ls`.
- **tools without a marker in the workspace.** `tsc` keeps walking for a `tsconfig.json`, forge for a `foundry.toml`. Planting a stub per tool is a race that cannot be won.

So workspaces move to `~/.cache/ethskills-evals/<task-id>/<run-id>/` (`EVAL_WORKSPACE_ROOT` to relocate), where nothing above them is worth finding, and the run dir keeps a `workspace.path` pointer.

Costs, stated plainly:

- one extra file per run (`workspace.path`);
- `verify` now removes the workspace once it has graded — nothing cleans them up with the run dir anymore, and an SE2 workspace is ~2 GB while live. `--keep-workspace` opts out;
- runs made by an older harness cannot be graded after this, having no pointer. None exist: all 546 committed runs across every eval branch carry `pass:`, and `verify` refuses to regrade regardless.

A cheaper middle option, if the pointer and `verify` owning deletion are the sticking point: keep workspaces in the repo but outside `artifacts/` (`.workspaces/`, gitignored). That removes the adjacency without either cost, and leaves `tasks/` up the tree.

73.title: eval: noir (claude/opus-5)
73.body:
24 runs — 4 tasks × 2 variants × 3. Executor and judge both `claude` on
`claude-opus-5`; `self_judged: true` on every run, as expected on a single-stack
benchmark. Skill vendored at `skills/noir` (upstream `191dcc1`).

Toolchain: nargo 1.0.0-beta.26, bb 5.1.0, forge 1.4.4-stable, node v22.18.0.

## Result

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| noir-quiz-001 — build pipeline | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| noir-quiz-002 — Poseidon as external dep | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| noir-quiz-003 — msg.sender linkability | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **noir-goal-001 — anonymous DAO voting** | **1/3** | **3/3** |

Three of four tasks are at ceiling on both variants. Three failures across 168
judged checks, all in `no_skill`, all on goal-001, concentrated in two checks:
e4 (NoirJS stack) and e7 (tree mirror).

## The prior this skill corrects is mostly gone on opus-5

`nargo prove` / `nargo verify` never appeared as commands in any of the six
quiz-001 scripts. More significantly, goal-001 e1 and e2 pass 3/3 *without* the
skill on a task that never mentions linkability — all six runs routed the vote
through a relayer and scoped the nullifier to the proposal id unprompted. That
claim was the eval's centrepiece and the model now applies it on its own.

What the skill still buys is toolchain currency:

| Axis | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NoirJS in-process vs `bb` CLI shell-out | 1/3 | 3/3 |
| Files replaying insert events into a tree mirror | 0, 1, 0 | 3, 3, 2 |
| In-circuit hash | keccak256 ×2, Poseidon2 ×1 | `poseidon::bn254::hash_2` ×3 |

The keccak result is worth flagging: 2/3 `no_skill` runs hashed commitments and
nullifiers in-circuit with keccak256 — ~30k gates against ~600 — on a circuit
meant to prove in a browser. **No expect in the suite grades it**, because
goal-001 defers the hash to quiz-002 and quiz-002 is at ceiling. The skill's
largest content win is invisible in every pass count above.

## Negative delta

The skill pins poseidon at `v0.2.6` (SKILL.md L189), which does not compile on
beta.26. 6/6 `with_skill` runs across quiz-002 and goal-001 hit
`error: Expected type [Field], found type &[_; 0]`, diagnosed it, and re-pinned
to `v0.3.0`. 0/6 `no_skill` runs paid that cost — they went straight to v0.3.0.
It cost no expect, because every run recovered, but the skill made runs slower
at the thing it exists to speed up.

The predicted `claude mcp add noir-mcp` + `/reload-plugins` burn **did not
occur** — 0 occurrences in all 24 transcripts.

## Skill edits this supports

1. Re-pin poseidon to `v0.3.0` (L189), with the nargo version it was validated against.
2. Replace `[u1; N]` with `[bool; N]` (L235, L256, L285, L411) and restate the `binary_merkle_root` signature (L420) — all three `with_skill` circuits silently rewrote it to `bool` and compiled.
3. `bbup -v <version>` instead of bare `bbup` (L54); bare 404s on nargo ≥ beta.23, and the installer link points at `master` while the version map lives on `next`.
4. Leave the `UltraHonkBackend(bytecode, bb)` example alone — the skill is right and the upstream docs are wrong.

Two items previously listed as known rot **do not hold** on this pin and should
be dropped from the task notes: the generated verifier's floor is `>=0.8.21`
(matching the skill), and zk-kit's `binary_merkle_root` takes `[bool; N]` and
compiles fine.

## Eval changes this supports

- **quiz-002 expect_1 does not discriminate.** All three `no_skill` runs used Poseidon2 from the external `poseidon` dependency; the notes say that should fail as skill-conformance, and the judge passed it 3/3. Rewrite the line or accept Poseidon2 in the notes.
- **Add a hash-family expect to goal-001**, so the keccak-in-circuit result is graded somewhere.
- **quiz-001 and quiz-003 are exhausted on this model** — 5/5 and 4/4 in all six runs each. 12 runs to learn nothing.
- Exclude `out/` verifiers from the 256KB evidence drop. It bit once: `no-skill-1`'s 354KB generated verifier was dropped and its 974-byte `MockVerifier.sol` was what reached the judge, on a task whose e3 fails any MockVerifier in the deploy path. The judge got e3 right from the deploy script anyway.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The runs were produced on a local `harness/run-lifecycle` branch (`ec831b8`, `5aef6cb`) that is **not on origin**. This PR carries the results only; the scripts that generated the evidence are not in `main` yet.
- Six goal-001 runs were killed mid-flight by an orchestrator session restart (`nohup` does not survive a process-group teardown). Per AGENTS.md they were deleted as dead runs rather than graded as zeros, and both variants were re-run whole with fresh run ids — no table mixes pre- and post-restart runs.
- `--setting-sources project` governs settings, not `CLAUDE.md` discovery: 4 of 6 quiz-001 executors read the machine's user-level `RTK.md` on their first turn. It appears in both variants and does not bias the comparison, but the isolation is weaker than the flag suggests.

Full report: `reports/noir-2026-08-18.md`. Six mistake records under `mistakes/noir/`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

74.title: fix: reduce building-blocks to a live-verification trigger
74.body:
## Why

Follow-up to #69 using the keep-vs-wiki rule in #1. The original five-task Opus 5 benchmark saturated at 15/15 in both variants, showing that the protocol facts themselves belong in a wiki/reference layer. The remaining question was whether a skill trigger makes the model apply current venue verification while building.

## Changes

- reduces `skills/building-blocks/SKILL.md` from 1,475 words to a 128-word trigger
- removes static protocol rankings, addresses, examples, and time-sensitive protocol facts
- keeps only live deployment/pair/gauge/incentive/reward verification and composition guardrails
- strengthens `building-blocks-quiz-001` so dated pair evidence and merger tense are actually graded
- adds the unprompted `building-blocks-goal-002` Base vault task
- includes six valid Opus 5 run records, transcripts, mistake record, and report

## Goal-002 result

| Variant | Full passes |
| --- | ---: |
| `no_skill` | **1/3** |
| `with_skill` | **3/3** |

All six runs selected Aerodrome and implemented its gauge-emission reward model correctly. The only repeated control failure was omitting dated, sourced, pair-specific Base evidence: 2/3 controls asserted dominance or comparable depth from memory, while 3/3 skilled runs measured current pools, liquidity/volume or incentives, and gauge status.

That is the quiz-pass / goal-split outcome from #1: retain a small trigger because a passive wiki cannot reliably make the verification happen mid-build, while moving the protocol knowledge out of the skill.

Full analysis: `reports/building-blocks-goal-002-2026-08-18.md`.

## Validation caveat

The benchmark tested the 467-word candidate at `06e154a`. The final 128-word skill is a post-eval attribution-driven reduction: only its opening live-verification instruction produced the measured delta. It should be rerun against `building-blocks-goal-002` before merge; this PR does not transfer the 3/3 score to the shorter text without evidence.

75.title: skills: minimal addresses from the #62 eval findings
75.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the addresses eval in #62, taking the minimal-skill direction from issue #1 ([step 4](https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/issues/1#issuecomment-5237465043)) and stacked on the eval branch.

`skills/addresses` goes from **547 lines / 2,840 words** of address tables to **39 lines / 706 words** of the discipline the eval showed the skill actually buys. Two task rubrics are tightened where #62's report found them ambiguous.

## What #62 measured

| | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 quizzes | **15/15** | 13/15 |
| goal-001 | 2/3 | **3/3** |

That is issue #1's second verdict row — *the model knows the facts when asked, but doesn't think to apply them mid-build* → **keep as skill, move the knowledge out**. The tables changed no answer the model could not reach by looking it up, and they supplied both `with_skill` failures:

- quiz-001 run 1 wrote *"dominant DEX on Base by TVL (~$500-600M)"* — copied verbatim from L357, roughly double the pinned ground truth, with Uniswap actually ahead on TVL. Tool sequence: `ls` → `Skill` → `Write`.
- quiz-005 run 3 got all eight addresses right and attributed every one to *"verified address reference"* — the skill it had just read — then wired them to a live `supply()` call without looking at a chain.

Both are the same root cause: a five-month-old snapshot labelled "verified onchain" with a ✅ on every row reads as a completed check. `mistakes/addresses/addresses-verified-stamp-substitutes-for-check.yaml`.

## The skill

Kept — the one behaviour with a real delta, plus the four traps the runs proved are invisible to `eth_getCode`:

- **Verify on the chain you are wiring it for, before the address reaches anything that moves funds.** Code + identity call, settled against the protocol's deployment list, and a named instruction in the deliverable for whoever runs it. Stated explicitly: *a dated table — this document included — does not discharge the check.*
- **Same protocol, different chain.** CREATE2/vanity proves nothing cross-chain (the quiz-002 v4 claim). And the converse the old file got backwards: nothing at an address is not absence from the chain — check the deployment list before saying a chain is unsupported.
- **Same protocol, older deployment.** Deprecated contracts stay live and keep answering `symbol()`; a read that returns 0 without reverting is the tell (the V1 VELO case).
- **Right protocol, wrong contract.** Aerodrome's v2-style `Router` cannot reach Slipstream, where the major Base pairs trade — measured 2026-08-12 on one 500k USDC→WETH clip: −14 bps through Slipstream, **−1,283 bps** through the vAMM Router, both addresses genuine, neither call reverting.
- **Bridged vs native.**
- **Venue choice** keeps the steer and drops the metric error: the deepest L2 venue is often not the mainnet one, no venue leads on every metric, so name the metric — routed volume for the pair decides execution, aggregate TVL does not — and back it with a live quote.

Removed: every address table, the `Last Verified: March 3, 2026` stamp and the per-row ✅, the false Base TVL claim, the Morpho-not-on-Arbitrum line, the Aero merger tense error, the dated Chainlink prices, and the `ethskills.com/feedback` instruction — two #62 runs declined that one unprompted as an outbound-network vector, and per [rin-st's comment](https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/issues/1#issuecomment-5257872886) addresses was one of the three files still carrying it.

## What the cut costs

The tables' one measured benefit was speed where their facts held: quiz-004 **4x** faster (52s/$0.35 vs 220s/$0.71), quiz-002 **3x**. This PR gives that back — a `with_skill` run now has to look every address up. quiz-004 is where it will show, and its notes say so, so the re-run measures the cost rather than hiding it. The trade is deliberate: the same tables produced 2/2 of the negative deltas, and `no_skill` was 15/15 on the quizzes because this model measures rather than guesses.

## Eval changes

Only where #62's report says the rubric, not the skill, was at fault:

- **quiz-001** — expects 1 and 2 overlapped (an asserted dominance claim arguably failed both, and the blind judge split them). Now: expect_1 grades whether Base-specific evidence is present, expect_2 grades whether what the answer asserts is true. expect_3 pins the Slipstream SwapRouter and grades **which** router inside the venue was handed over — the gap that let the −1,283 bps error pass every rubric while runs caught it unprompted.
- **goal-001** — expect_6 now states that runtime assertions in `swap.ts` do not substitute for a written verify-before-funds instruction; that ambiguity is exactly what the one failing `no_skill` run turned on. New **expect_7** grades router-within-venue. Slipstream router + CLFactory added to expect_3's pinned list.
- All six tasks: line-number references into the old file replaced, pre/post-reduction provenance recorded, #62 per-task baselines noted for whoever runs it next.

Deliberately **not** changed: the quizzes are otherwise untouched so they stay a usable baseline. Because expect_7 is new, goal-001 aggregate counts are not comparable with #62 — per-expect results for 1–6 still are, and the notes say so.

Slipstream addresses verified on Base before pinning: `0xBE6D8f0d05cC4be24d5167a3eF062215bE6D18a5` → `factory()` = CLFactory `0x5e7BB104d84c7CB9B682AaC2F3d509f5F406809A`, `WETH9()` = `0x4200…0006`. Morpho on Arbitrum re-confirmed live (`0x6c247b1F…`, 31,167 bytes of code).

## Status of the mistake records

All five stay `status: open` with a "fix proposed" note — they close when a re-run confirms, not when this merges. `addresses-aero-merger-tense` also flags that `skills/l2s` (L22, L97-98) and `skills/building-blocks` (L16, L169) still carry the same stale tense.

## Validation — re-run, 24 runs

The benchmark **has** now been re-run against the reduced skill (`a461aa8`), same stack as #62,
serial, one judge throughout. Full report: `reports/addresses-minimal-2026-08-19.md`.

| task | no_skill | with_skill | #62 with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 | 3/3 | **3/3** | 2/3 |
| quiz-002 | 3/3 † | **3/3** | 3/3 |
| quiz-003 | 3/3 † | **3/3** | 3/3 |
| quiz-004 | 3/3 † | **3/3** | 3/3 |
| quiz-005 | 3/3 † | **3/3** | 2/3 |
| goal-001 | **1/3** | **3/3** | 3/3 |
| total | | **18/18** | 16/18 |

† carried from #62: identical inputs, identical expects, same judge model, so re-running the
unaided variant would have re-measured a constant. goal-001 and quiz-001 were re-run in both
variants because their expects moved in this PR.

**The cut is safe, and both #62 negative deltas closed.**

- **quiz-001 2/3 → 3/3.** The copied `~$500-600M` TVL claim is gone with the section that supplied
  it. All three runs argue the venue from measured Base evidence; run 1 hands over the Slipstream
  SwapRouter `0xBE6D8f0d…` with its QuoterV2, CLFactory and the ts=100 USDC/WETH pool.
- **quiz-005 2/3 → 3/3.** With no table to cite, runs source their addresses to
  `aave-address-book`, Circle's contract list, and live `getMarketId()` / `getReserveAToken()`
  calls. **No output in any of the 18 `with_skill` runs cites the skill as an address source** —
  that was the entire mechanism of `addresses-verified-stamp-substitutes-for-check`.
- **Every skilled run verified on-chain**: minimum 8 Bash calls, median 18, goal-001 runs 38–64
  (they fork Base on anvil and execute against fork state). #62's two failing runs ran
  `ls → Skill → Write` with zero verification.

**goal-001, the task the skill is kept for: `with_skill 3/3` vs `no_skill 1/3`** (#62: 3/3 vs 2/3).
Both unaided failures are precise rather than sloppy — they verified heavily and wrote long
"before real funds" sections, but neither told the developer to confirm the addresses against an
explorer or the protocol's deployment list. Part of the widened gap is this PR's reworded expect_6
stating that distinction outright, not worse unaided behaviour; the report says so.

**What the cut costs.** Real, smaller than #62 implied. quiz-004 — the sharpest case — goes
52s/$0.35 with the table to 171s/$0.57 without, against 220s/$0.71 unaided: deleting the V1/V2 VELO
row cost ~2 minutes, not a full regression, because the "older deployment" rule still says what to
suspect. On goal-001 skilled runs are *cheaper* than unaided ones ($3.70 vs $4.53) while running
longer.

**Honest caveat on expect_7.** The new router-within-venue check passed in all six goal-001 runs,
both variants — unaided runs find Slipstream by quoting too. Keep it as a guard against the
specific −1,283 bps error; do not read it as evidence for the skill.

**Where this leaves the eval.** The five quizzes are now saturated in both variants and can no
longer detect a regression in this skill. goal-001 is the only discriminating task, and one expect
carries the whole delta. The next skill change needs a second goal-shaped task, not this set — the
report's final row spells that out.

Four mistake records are marked `fixed` with their confirming evidence; `addresses-aero-merger-tense`
stays `open` because the same stale tense still sits in `skills/l2s` and `skills/building-blocks`.

Also checked before running: quiz-004's blocking run-day gate (VELO V2 still the live Optimism
token, Aero still unlaunched per aero.xyz, audit contest to Sep 11) and the pinned rubric addresses,
including the Slipstream router this PR adds.

Based on #62 and issue #1.

76.title: fix: minimize the indexing skill to its nudges
76.body:
Stacked on #64 (the indexing eval), so the diff carries that PR's eval records until it merges. The skill and task changes came in `017094b`; everything after it is the re-run against the minimized skill.

## What #64 measured

codex `gpt-5.6-terra`, 3 runs/variant, per-check:

| Task | no_skill | with_skill | Failing check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 (scan vs index) | 3/3 | 3/3 | — |
| quiz-002 (Graph go-live + cost) | 3/3 | 3/3 | — |
| quiz-003 (don't over-index) | 3/3 | 3/3 | — |
| goal-001 (Streak build) | 0/3 | 3/3 | expect_5 only |

One delta in the whole benchmark: the README naming a production deploy path for the read side. Event-first design, index-over-events, rankings offchain and a stated read architecture all passed 3/3 **without** the skill, so only the deploy nudge was carrying anything and the rest was a candidate for the wiki.

## Skill: 318 lines -> 24

Following the minimal pass agreed in #1.

- **Cut**: the subgraph schema/mapping/query samples, the Dune SQL block, the Alchemy and viem snippets, the event-gas arithmetic, the WebSocket example, and both solution tables.
- **Kept**: one nudge per claim the tasks grade — index don't scan, event-first contracts, rankings offchain, current state is a direct/Multicall read — plus the measured win promoted to its own paragraph: the read side is not designed until its production home is named.
- **Sharper `description`**: names the trigger moments (feeds/leaderboards/analytics, event design, deploying an indexer or subgraph).
- **Stale content fixed**, re-read from the live docs on 2026-08-18:
  - `graph init --studio` / `graph deploy --studio` are gone; current CLI is `graph init <slug>` / `graph auth <deploy-key>` / `graph deploy <slug>`
  - the free hosted service was sunset June 2024, and deploying to Studio is not publishing to the network
  - production queries are metered — ~100K free/month, then ~$2 per 100K (thegraph.com/studio-pricing), with a re-check-the-page nudge rather than a number to recite

No feedback footer in this skill, so nothing to remove there.

## Eval changes

- **goal-001: expect_5 split in two.** It was carrying two claims and it was the benchmark's only delta, so as written we could not tell "the skill makes the run decide production" from "the skill points at The Graph, whose deploy target and command are pre-named". The no_skill READMEs all describe *running* the indexer (supervised processes, persistent volume, Postgres to scale) but never name **where**. New expect_5 = is there a production run story at all; expect_6 = is the target named.
- **quiz-001: chain height refreshed.** Its notes require the input and expect_2's worked example to agree; mainnet is 25,783,129 as of the rewrite, so both now read ~25.8M / ≈12,900 paginated calls.
- **quiz-002: ground truth re-validated** (100K free, $2/100K, sunset, current CLI) and failure semantics recorded as flipped — the minimal skill now states this path itself, so a with_skill miss is wrong content, not a gap. Also captured the report's own suggestion: every transcript shows a web fetch, so isolating retained knowledge means one network-disabled pair, reported as its own benchmark.
- **quiz-003: unchanged**, documented as negative-delta insurance now that the skill leads with "index, don't scan".
- **Mistake record**: `skill_section` repointed at the surviving paragraph.

## Step 5: the re-run, on two stacks

Both rounds were driven by a fresh orchestrator that had not read the expect lines.

**claude `claude-opus-5`, all four tasks, 2026-08-19** (`reports/indexing-minimal-2026-08-19.md`) — 24 runs. Cutting 294 lines lost no check: quizzes 3/3 vs 3/3 across the board, goal-001 2/3 vs 3/3. The skill self-invoked in 11 of 12 with_skill runs on its `description` alone.

**codex `gpt-5.6-terra`, goal-001, 2026-08-20** (`reports/indexing-goal-001-2026-08-20.md`) — 3/3 vs 0/3, the #64 delta reproduced exactly on 24 lines instead of 318, every no_skill run failing both expect_5 and expect_6.

**Verdict: keep the minimal skill, and the wiki move is closed.** The 08-19 report proposed retiring it if codex converged; codex did not converge. The two rounds together say the same 24 lines are worth nothing on claude and the entire task on codex — identical content, identical checks — so a verdict cell in the #1 table only means something with a stack attached. That reading is recorded as an addendum on the 08-19 report.

On the expect_5/expect_6 split: it earns its keep on claude, where the single no_skill failure names a full run story and no host (`2026-08-19T061503Z-claude-no-skill-3`). On codex the two moved together, so the 08-20 sample alone would not have shown it.

## Follow-ups from review (@rin-st)

- `.gitignore` no longer ignores `artifacts/**/transcript.md` — that line arrived in #64 and survived the merge in `8bc553d` as a resolution, not a decision, and it contradicts #46. The three duplicate `transcript.jsonl` rules on main are collapsed to one.
- **All 30 transcripts for this PR's runs are now committed.** They were never lost, just untracked in the clones the rounds ran in: the 24 claude runs in the 08-19 working copy, the 6 codex runs in the 08-20 worktree. Variant integrity checks out on all 30 — every `with_skill` transcript carries the skill, no `no_skill` one does.
- Task notes for quiz-002 now carry the same pre-/post-rewrite annotation as quiz-001 and quiz-003.
- The 8-cell table in `reports/indexing-goal-001-2026-08-20.md` had a 9-cell delimiter and did not render; fixed.
- `frequency` in the mistake record now has a stack key per measurement instead of one field holding two stacks in a comment, with the schema slot documented in `AGENTS.md`.

### What the restored transcripts changed

Re-checking the transcript-derived findings against the files found one wrong number, now fixed:

- **The trigger fired 12 of 12, not 11 of 12.** `reports/indexing-quiz-002-2026-08-19.md` recorded `2026-08-19T033814Z-claude-with-skill-3` as never invoking the skill; its transcript opens on `Skill(indexing)` with an args string, before any web call. Corrected there and in the summary — in all twelve with_skill runs the Skill call is the *first* tool call, which is a stronger result for the rewritten `description` than what was written down.
- The rest reconcile exactly: quiz-001 shows zero web calls in all six runs; quiz-002 shows with_skill 10/18/16 against no_skill 19/20/20, matching the 14.7 vs 19.7 averages in that report.

**Still open, and not this PR's:** the 25 codex runs from 2026-08-12 that #64 carries have no transcripts anywhere — never committed, and not on this machine. Their reports' transcript-derived lines stay uncheckable until #64 resolves it. Separately, the codex transcripts are raw CLI stdout while claude's are structured markdown, which is the divergence #70 fixes.

77.title: eval: concepts (claude/opus-5)
77.body:
18 runs, 3 per variant per task. Executor and judge both `claude`/`claude-opus-5`, one stack start to finish. Skill `skills/concepts` @ `2f0adb0`.

## Results

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| concepts-quiz-001 (randomness) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| concepts-quiz-002 (fee vs caller gas) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| concepts-goal-001 (billing build) | 1/3 | 2/3 |

**The stale prior this skill corrects did not reproduce on this stack.** goal-001 expects 2–4 grade "Nothing Is Automatic" — who pokes it, why would they, is it enough — and both variants passed them 3/3. All six runs independently chose per-second read-time accrual with a permissionless `settle()`, so no periodic transaction exists to fund at all. Nobody shipped "charged monthly" with nothing to run it.

What did fail is the habit layer. `expect_7` (forkability) failed 3 of 6 runs across both variants: runs stop at Etherscan verification and never say what a third party could run if the provider walked — the weather API and the per-request subscription check go unmentioned. Two mistake records filed.

Both quizzes are at ceiling on both variants, as `concepts-quiz-002`'s own notes anticipated. quiz-001's per-path expects (256-block window, EIP-2935, commit-reveal) were never exercised — all six runs chose VRF.

## Pre-run price check

ETH $1,880.26, mainnet gas 0.1065 gwei → 250k gas = $0.050/call against a $0.0088/day fee, break-even ≈ 5.7 days. Inside the band the task notes assume, so the $8,000 deposit figure did not need to come down.

## Caveats, all detailed in the report

- **Every run records `self_judged: true`** — one stack means executor and judge are both claude/opus-5. Each grading still ran blind in a fresh process.
- **Three runs produced and not counted**: one discarded for variant contamination (it ran repo-root `git status` and could see it was the with_skill arm), one killed by a memory-pressure reaper, one killed by the orchestrator's own foreground timeout. Plus an Opus 5 availability window that aborted three launches.
- **Executors mutated this repo three times.** `forge install` without `--no-git` registers workspace dependencies as submodules at the repo root, and one executor ran `rm -rf <repo>/lib`, deleting `judge.ts`/`task.ts`/`types.ts`. All reverted; no committed state damaged, no graded result affected. Worth fixing properly — workspaces sit inside the repo tree.
- **The prescribed canary probes `claude-haiku-4-5` while executors run `claude-opus-5`**, so it reported `allowed` moments before Opus 5 returned `529 Overloaded`.

## Recommendation

No skill content change — SKILL.md:25 states the open-source claim correctly. The gap is reach: it is one bullet in a four-item CROPS list that a run must carry unprompted through ~40 minutes of build work. The eval side needs more runs on goal-001 (the whole finding rests on a 2/3-vs-1/3 split on one expect) and the two quizzes retired or rewritten.

Checklist sha `ffe4b670e78e1945bcf275f79d4b7b0481bcff35`, unchanged before and after.

80.title: eval: noir minimal skill (claude/opus-5)
80.body:
Fresh benchmark of the compressed `skills/noir` (3939 → 732 words, 81%, ~5100 → ~950 tokens) per issue #1 step 4. Reported separately from #73 and never blended into one table — #73 appears only as the bar to clear.

12 runs: `noir-goal-001` and `noir-quiz-002`, both variants, n=3. Executor and judge both `claude` / `claude-opus-5`, so every run is `self_judged: true` — expected on a single-stack benchmark, same as #73.

**Verdict: keep `skills/noir` as a minimal skill.** The 81% cut cost nothing this benchmark can see.

## Did the 81% cut cost anything?

**No, on every axis this benchmark can see.** `with_skill` went **3/3 on goal-001 and 3/3 on quiz-002**, exactly #73's bar, and all three rot items fixed inside the minimal skill landed. The headline is the poseidon pin: in #73 every run burned a compile-fail-and-re-pin cycle on the stale v0.2.6 pin, and across all 12 runs here that error appears **zero** times. `[bool; DEPTH]` replaced `[u1; N]` (which `no_skill` still reaches for), the skill's `bbup -v <version>` line reached the install docs of 3/3 `with_skill` deliverables and 0/3 `no_skill` — documented, not invoked; no run ran `bbup`, the toolchain is pre-installed per the task's pre-flight — and the deleted MCP section cost **0 turns in all 12 runs**.

The complication is on the other side: **`no_skill` improved sharply** — 2/3 and 3/3, against #73's 1/3 on goal-001 — so the pass column barely separates the variants any more. What still separates them is ungraded and only visible by reading circuits:

| ungraded read (goal-001) | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Poseidon over BN254 in-circuit | 1/3 | **3/3** |
| skill's `poseidon::poseidon::bn254` import path | 0/3 | **3/3** |
| member note written to disk by the tool | 0/3 | **3/3** |

The third row is weaker than the other two — no `no_skill` run actually loses the note. See "Corrections after review".

Two of three `no_skill` runs put a ~30,000-gate bit-oriented hash where ~600 would do, in a circuit whose members prove in a browser — one hand-rolled truncated SHA-256, one pulled in `keccak256` — and both wrote a confident rationale for it. **`no-skill-2` passed 7/7 anyway**: no expect grades in-circuit hash choice.

## Environment drift did not fire

`@aztec/bb.js` 5.2.0 is live and `npm install` resolves to it against this machine's 5.1.0 CLI. **All six goal-001 runs pinned 5.1.0 deliberately; none took npm latest** (verified in `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and resolved `node_modules` — all three agree). expect_4 passed 6/6, so there was no failure to attribute to either cause: no run shelled out to the `bb` CLI *to prove* (`no-skill-1` did, for `write_vk` and `write_solidity_verifier`), and no run proved on a mismatched pair.

## Comparability

`with_skill` is directly comparable and clears the bar. **The `no_skill` baseline is not strictly comparable to #73** — it improved on three independent axes (pass rate, in-process proving 3/3 vs 1/3, unprompted v0.3.0 pin), none of it drift. The model's prior moved. This benchmark therefore has less power to detect a compression cost than #73 did; the ungraded reads carry the signal, and they favour the compressed skill.

## Also in here

- **2 mistake records** — `noir-bit-oriented-hash-in-circuit` (2/3 no_skill), `noir-tree-mirror-from-view-call` (1/3, the only graded failure in 12 runs). Both 0/3 with_skill. A third, `noir-note-not-persisted`, was filed at 3/3 and is withdrawn — below.
- **4 skill edits, applied in this PR** rather than filed against the skill it introduces — all inherited from the pre-cut text, none of them followed by any run. Below.
- **Harness finding:** the `lib` exclusion matches by directory name at any depth and silently dropped authored source from the judge's evidence in two runs (`scripts/lib/prover.mjs`, `js/lib/{prove,note}.mjs`). I read the dropped files directly — they support the verdicts, and it hit one run per variant, so the comparison is unbiased. The 256KB cap also dropped two >320KB generated verifiers, again one per variant. Narrowing `lib` to the workspace root is the immediate fix; the root cause is `verify.ts` routing template-less tasks to the `output/` path, and it is a follow-up.
- **noir-quiz-001 and noir-quiz-003 were deliberately skipped** — 5/5 and 4/4 in every run of both variants in #73, so they discriminate nothing. Stated in the report rather than left un-run silently.
- **quiz-002 expect_1 did not discriminate**, for the second benchmark running: all three `no_skill` runs passed it with Poseidon2 from the external dep. The `with_skill` pass there is not evidence the import path landed — the actual imports are tabulated in the report.
- **Merge order:** `5aef6cb` and `ec831b8` are byte-identical to #66's two commits. Merge #66 first and this lands as skill + runs; merging #80 first puts the harness on main unreviewed and empties #66.

## Corrections after review (@damianmarti)

Three claims in the original description did not hold as stated when re-derived from the artifacts. Fixed in `5dc830a`, and in the report.

**1. The four wrong lines in the skill are fixed here.** `{ keccak: true }` → `{ verifierTarget: "evm" }` (deprecated, and means `evm-no-zk`, whose proofs an `evm` verifier rejects); the Solidity floor `>=0.8.21` → `>=0.8.27` with the `solc_version = '0.8.27'` remedy the cut dropped; the `npm install @noir-lang/noir_js "@aztec/bb.js@$(bb --version)"` command restored; and `--oracle_hash keccak` → `--verifier_target evm`, on the grounds that it names the transcript hash and the ZK setting together where `--oracle_hash` names the hash alone — **not** because the old flag is gone. It is not gone: it works on bb 5.1.0, and 6/6 quiz-002 runs used it — `no_skill` 3/3 as well as `with_skill` 3/3, so that is convergence on a live flag rather than skill-following. That correction is in `874a0fe`.

The benchmark stays valid on the count that carries it: **0/6 goal-001 runs copied the `{ keccak: true }` example** — the one goal-001 occurrence is `with-skill-2` calling it wrong — and all six wrote `verifierTarget: 'evm'`, five of them verifiable from the committed evidence (`no-skill-1`'s prover is one of the two files the `lib` exclusion dropped, read from the workspace).

It is not latent, though: on quiz-002 the example propagated into 2/3 `with_skill` deliverables as advice for a frontend nobody wrote (`with-skill-3`'s `output/src/main.nr:56-60` copies the snippet and adds *"`{ keccak: true }` is required"*; `with-skill-1`'s `:53` recommends the same). Both runs proved through the `bb` CLI, so nothing executed it and no expect graded it. Two of the four inherited lines reached run output, not one — a better argument for fixing them than "latent" was. Corrected in `983bb75`.

The committed skill is now 802 words against the 732 benchmarked at `840dde0`; that delta is on record in the report.

**2. `noir-note-not-persisted` is withdrawn** (3/3 → 0/3). Re-reading the three `no_skill` clients, none of them loses the note: no-skill-1 and no-skill-3 derive the secret from a wallet signature over a fixed message, so there is nothing to back up; no-skill-2 prints a random secret at registration and re-imports it via `--secret`/`--passphrase`, deliberately not derived from the ETH key so the voting key can rotate. All three recover the leaf index by locating the commitment in the tree. That is a key-management design difference, not a lost note. The eval finding stands: the split expect_7 must grade **recoverability** — persisted by the tool, handed to the member, or deterministically re-derivable, leaf index recoverable — not "writes a note file", which would fail all three sound `no_skill` designs.

**3. `bbup` was documented, not invoked.** No run ran `bbup` at all. What is actually in the artifacts is the skill's line propagating into each `with_skill` deliverable's `README.md` — `with-skill-1` copied the `bbup -v <version>` placeholder verbatim, `-2` and `-3` wrote `bbup -v 5.1.0` — against 0/3 `no_skill`, whose only `bbup` string is a `ls ~/.bb/` listing. Still a 3/3 vs 0/3 effect, on documentation.

Left as follow-ups: an explicit `evidence: diff|output` field in the task spec (root cause of both evidence losses) and the `GENERATED_DIRS` mirror in `.git/info/exclude`; the `run-executor.ts` / AGENTS.md notes, which belong to #66's commits; and the eval edits themselves — split expect_7, a hash-choice expect on goal-001, quiz-002 expect_1, and the stale `tag = "v0.2.6"` in quiz-002's ground-truth block.

Full report: `reports/noir-minimal-2026-08-19.md`.

81.title: skills: minimal qa (alternative to #48)
81.body:
## Summary

Cuts `skills/qa` from 2821 to 811 words (19.5KB → 5.5KB, roughly 3650 → 1050 tokens) — issue #1 step 4, "minimal and thoughtful, remove the why stuff, just have the nudge".

One file, nothing else. **The task specs are deliberately untouched**: this PR exists to answer one question — is the cut safe — and that answer comes from re-running both goals. Change the grading surface in the same PR and a moved result can't be attributed to either cause. The expects stay exactly as #29 measured them.

Alternative to #48 for `SKILL.md` — that PR sharpens the existing structure, this one removes most of it. They conflict on the file, which is the point: it forces an explicit choice rather than letting two versions stack silently.

Draft until #29 lands — the mistake records this rests on are there.

## What the cut is based on

Per-expect pass rates read from the raw `result.yaml` files in #29 (3 runs per variant). goal-001 measures whether the model *sees* an issue in review; goal-002 whether it *fixes* it unprompted. They disagree often enough that the pair, not either alone, decides what stays.

| Check | g1 no_skill | g2 no_skill | Read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Connect button not text | **0/3** | **0/3** | skill carries entirely |
| `externalContracts` registration | **0/3** | 1/3 | skill carries |
| Address display / contract shown | **0/3** | **0/3** | skill carries entirely |
| `--radius-field` pill inputs | **0/3** | **0/3** | skill carries entirely |
| Branding (title, README, footer, favicon) | **0/3, 0/3** | 1/3, **0/3** | skill carries entirely |
| Mobile deep link · Phantom | **0/3, 0/3** | n/a | skill carries entirely |
| DaisyUI `loading` class · dark wrapper | 1/3, 1/3 | 1/3, 1/3 | skill carries most |
| `AddressInput` | 3/3 | **0/3** | sees, does not apply |
| Wrong-network gating | 3/3 | **0/3** | sees, does not apply |
| `pollingInterval` | 3/3 | 1/3 | sees, mostly does not apply |
| One-action-at-a-time, scaffold write hook, button locking, error surfacing, RPC posture | 3/3 | 3/3 | model already carries these |

The cleanest evidence for "nudge, not knowledge" is `AddressInput`: goal-001 flags it **3/3 without the skill** and goal-002 fixes it **0/3 without it**. Knowledge present, application missing. Same shape for wrong-network gating. That is what the shorter file is built to preserve.

That also makes the parts of the old skill that explain *how* pure context cost: the quizzes went 3/3 in both variants on externalContracts, the `loading` class and `--radius-field`, so the model derives that code cold once the claim is in front of it.

## What changed

**Kept, with the specificity that makes them actionable** — the checks the skill carries. Concreteness is the nudge: "`--radius-field: 9999rem` renders pill-shaped inputs, fix in both theme blocks" changes behavior where "check your border radii" does not.

**Kept because the pair splits** — `AddressInput` and wrong-network gating, on the 3/3-then-0/3 evidence above.

**Compressed to one line each** — one-action-at-a-time, the scaffold write hook, button locking, error surfacing, RPC posture. All 3/3 in both variants and both modes, so model-carried on this stack; compressed rather than deleted as cheap insurance for codex/gpt-5.6, per #58's precedent.

**Dropped** — the "What You Probably Got Wrong" preamble, both duplicate checklists (the top-of-file flow list and the bottom-of-file audit summary restated the rules between them), the two-cooldown approve recipe, the `openWallet` scheme-matching block, and every remaining code sample except one. The `externalContracts` migration stays because goal-002 e5 is the single residual `with_skill` gap (**1/3 → 1/3**): the skill makes the model see the misplaced USDC entry and not migrate it. The rest are wiki candidates rather than deletions.

**Dropped with no evidence either way, flagging it explicitly** — USD context on amounts and the absolute-OG-image rule. Both are listed in `qa-goal-001`'s notes as deliberately ungraded weak signals, so nothing supports keeping them and nothing condemns it. This is real content loss, not compression, and should be a conscious call rather than something that slips through.

## Rot fixed while cutting

Two claims in the old text were false, in sections the cut rewrites anyway:

- **`isPending` → `isMining`.** The old text ties the `disabled` prop to "`isPending` from `useScaffoldWriteContract`". The hook sets `isMining` before the write and holds it across `waitForTransactionReceipt` (`useScaffoldWriteContract.ts:109-144`); the `isPending` it passes through from wagmi drops when the wallet returns the hash — precisely the double-approve window the section exists to close.
- **"SE-2 defaults `--radius-field` to `9999rem`".** `templates/se-2/…/globals.css` ships `0rem`. `templates/qa-target` seeds `9999rem`, so the check stays valid; its stated premise was not.

## Deliberately not carried over from #48

#48 makes contract-address display, Phantom, and deep-link handling conditional on product policy. That rewrites what those checks assert, and it would land in the same re-run as the cut — leaving a moved goal-001 number with two candidate causes. It is a real question, but it belongs in its own change with its own measurement.

Side effect worth noting: because the cut *drops* the mobile-linking prescription rather than replacing it with a counter-prescription, it does not collide with `qa-quiz-004`'s `e2`/`e3` the way #48 does. The short text says nothing about timing or storage internals, so quiz-004 keeps measuring base-model knowledge (1/3 vs 0/3 in #29 — noise) instead of the skill's disagreement with its own grader.

## How to test

Coverage first — every graded expect still has a home in the shorter text. All 32 across both goals map:

- goal-001 e1–e5 → the five "Wallet and action flow" bullets · e6–e8 → "Contracts and addresses" · e9 → error bullet · e10–e12 → "Theme and loading states" · e13–e14 → "Config" · e15–e16 → "Branding" · e17–e18 → "Mobile"
- goal-002 e1–e4 → "Wallet and action flow" · e5–e7 → "Contracts and addresses" · e8 → error bullet · e9–e11 → "Theme and loading states" · e12 → "Config" · e13–e14 → "Branding"
- quiz mirrors: quiz-001 → `externalContracts` bullet · quiz-002 → `loading` bullet · quiz-003 → `--radius-field` bullet · quiz-004 → deep-link bullet · quiz-005 → the `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` clause in "Config"

Then the actual test, which is issue #1 step 5 — a fresh benchmark of both goals against this revision, landed on this branch (artifacts + report) before it leaves draft: 3 × `no_skill` + 3 × `with_skill` per goal, one stack start to finish (claude / opus-5, fresh blind judge on the same model), reported separately from #29. `no_skill` re-runs too — #29 ran on `claude-opus-4-8`, and comparing a fresh `with_skill` against that baseline would blend stacks and judges, which AGENTS.md forbids ("never blend them in one table").

Quizzes are skipped as non-discriminating: 001/002/003/005 went 3/3 in both variants in #29 and their claims are covered by the mapping above; 004 is excluded as broken on the merits, not merely noisy — see #29's review notes.

Twelve runs total. Any expect that drops from #29's `with_skill` 3/3 marks where the compression went too far — that is the signal this PR exists to produce.

Also verified locally: `git diff --check` clean, frontmatter parses (`name`, `description`), and `setup-workspace.ts` only copies the skill directory and records the repo sha, so nothing structural depends on the removed sections.

## Worth a reviewer's attention

- **The re-run has a prerequisite this branch does not carry.** `main` has no `scripts/run-executor.ts` and no `lib/workspace.ts` — `package.json` on `main` exposes only `setup` and `verify`, while `AGENTS.md` step 2 already documents `yarn run-executor`. The harness lives on the `fix/workspace-isolation` stack (#66, #70–#72). The benchmark has to run from a tree that has it.
- The `description:` frontmatter is now a large part of the trigger surface, and #29 measured **~0/15 skill invocations in quiz framing vs 6/6 on goals**. It names every checked surface by name for that reason. If it is too narrow the skill never loads and the eval measures nothing.
- `qa` is a skill the evidence **keeps** — goal-001 went 0/3 → 3/3 overall, an 18/18 sweep in every `with_skill` run. It just does not need 2821 words to do it.
- It overlaps `frontend-ux` (#58) and `frontend-playbook` on theme, loading states and address components — a candidate for the combining pass in step 7, not now.

82.title: skills: date the Aero merger by state in l2s
82.body:
## Summary

Closes the last open thread from the addresses eval (#62 / #75): the Aero merger is described in the past tense in three vendored skills. This fixes `skills/l2s`; `skills/addresses` is handled in #75, and `skills/building-blocks` needs no separate fix because #74 drops every Aero mention with the rest of that skill's prose.

`skills/l2s` L22 said the two protocols **"merged into Aero"** in November 2025, **"Same contracts, new brand"**, and its dominant-DEX table listed both Base and Optimism under the Aero name.

## Ground truth, re-checked 2026-08-19

- The merger was **announced** in Nov 2025, not completed. Per the protocol's own [schedule post](https://aero.xyz/articles/aero-is-on-the-horizon/): codebase public 3 Aug, final audits through 21 Aug, **public audit contest 24 Aug – 11 Sep 2026**, launch targeted September with no date pinned, token consolidation expected at launch.
- Confirmed on-chain the same day: VELO `0x9560e827aF36c94D2Ac33a39bCE1Fe78631088Db` is still the live Optimism token — `symbol()` returns `VELO`, supply 2.575e27 and growing against V1's static 1.99e27.
- **"Same contracts, new brand" is wrong twice over**: Aero is a new codebase currently under audit, not a rebrand of the deployed contracts.

A skill whose job is telling builders which protocol is live on which chain cannot describe an in-flight migration in the past tense. An agent trusting this treats Aero as the settled brand and VELO as historical, which is backwards on Optimism today.

## What changed

- The paragraph dates the merger **by state, not by announcement**, names Aerodrome and Velodrome as the live protocols with their own live tokens, and keeps the steer the paragraph exists for — don't default to Uniswap on every chain.
- Table rows return to the live names. The Base row now **names the metric** — Aerodrome leads by routed volume, Uniswap leads by TVL, check depth for your pair — rather than asserting bare dominance, per `addresses-base-dominance-metric`, which caught a run copying the old skill's TVL claim into a failing answer.
- A one-line note that Aero is the brand these two will ship under once it launches.

Net: +10 −5 in the skill. Nothing else in `skills/l2s` is touched.

## Evidence status

**No eval evidence behind this one, and I'd rather say so than imply otherwise.** The l2s benchmark has not run yet (#60), so this is a factual correction verified against the protocol's own schedule and the chain, not a measured improvement. No l2s task grades the merger claim, so the pending eval is unaffected and will simply measure the corrected skill.

`mistakes/l2s/l2s-aero-merger-tense.yaml` → `fixed`. `mistakes/addresses/addresses-aero-merger-tense.yaml` stays `open` until this and #74 land, with the cross-skill status recorded there.

**If Aero launches before #60 runs, this paragraph needs the opposite edit.** `addresses-quiz-004` carries a blocking run-day gate that catches it first.
