83.title: eval: l2s (claude/claude-opus-5)
83.body:
30 runs, 5 tasks, 3 per variant. Executor and judge both claude / `claude-opus-5`; judge is a fresh blind process per run via `yarn verify`. Report: `reports/l2s-2026-08-20.md`.

## Headline

| Task | with_skill | no_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| l2s-quiz-001 (Celo sweep runbook) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| l2s-quiz-002 (Polygon zkEVM stuck dashboard) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **l2s-quiz-003 (Base ↔ OP game token)** | **3/3** | **0/3** |
| l2s-quiz-004 (Rust onchain, no chain named) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| l2s-goal-001 (Celo payout/sweep build) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **Total** | **15/15** | **12/15** |

The whole delta is quiz-003, and inside it a single expect line. All three no_skill runs failed only expect_2 — the answer never names Base's departure from the OP Stack — while passing the other four checks. Two of them asserted the opposite as a *stability assumption*, in the section the prompt reserved for exactly that question:

> **Both chains track the same OP Stack hardfork schedule.** Today they upgrade together under the Superchain schedule, which is what makes one bytecode at one address on both chains safe.

That is false as of mid-2026 and load-bearing for the design. All three with_skill runs named the departure, sourced from the skill's Superchain paragraph. Live search did not rescue no_skill: they had network access and used it correctly for interop status, but nothing in the prompt flags the membership premise as questionable, so they never checked it.

## Run-day gate fired

quiz-003's blocking gate was re-checked before the first run:

- **Interop unchanged** — still not mainnet-live on Base or OP Mainnet (`docs.optimism.io/interop` now 404s; explainer says "in active development"; optimism#18939 says devnets only). Task ran as written.
- **Base's separation has landed** — `base/node` v0.16.0 (2026-05-22) dropped every client except `base-reth-node`/`base-consensus` for the Azul mainnet deadline; Base's blog says Azul "established the Base Stack as a new foundation for the chain"; **Beryl**, Base's second independent upgrade with its own B20 standard and its own 7d→5d withdrawal change, activated 2026-06-25/26. Per the gate, expect_4's "already left"/"separation is already complete" clauses were dropped so a run stating that fact isn't failed for it; the overcorrection guards are unchanged. Committed as `4f93522` before any run started.

## Both verdict-flipping expects passed

quiz-001 expect_2 and goal-001 expect_4 grade prove/finalize, which the skill's text does not contain — a with_skill failure there would have been a skill gap. **No failure: 12/12 across both variants.** The best evidence came from a no_skill run that read the parameters off Celo's contracts rather than trusting a remembered number (`maxChallengeDuration` 302,400 = 3.5d), priced the \$2M sweep against real Mento liquidity (40% haircut), and disproved a search result claiming Celo CCTP support by checking that `TokenMessengerV2` has no code on chain 42220.

## Efficiency

On quiz-001 the skill roughly halved cost and wall time for the same 3/3 — \$1.25 vs \$2.24, 329s vs 663s. The model stops researching what the skill already told it.

## Mistakes

Filed: `l2s-base-departure-model-blindspot` (3/3 no_skill), `l2s-base-departure-tense` (2/3 with_skill inherit the skill's now-stale "finalized in a future hardfork"), `l2s-stylus-multiplier-conflation` (1/3 with_skill **and** 1/3 no_skill — a model prior the skill echoes rather than causes, which is why no expect graded a number).

Updated with run evidence: `l2s-base-superchain-contradiction` (predicted it might mislead with_skill; it did not, 0/3 — latent defect, not active), `l2s-celo-bridging-gap`, `l2s-celo-fee-abstraction-gap`, `l2s-polygon-zkevm-tense`.

## Recommended skill edits

1. Re-tense the Base departure to "live on mainnet since Azul (May 2026)", keeping "Base is still an Ethereum L2, chain id and addresses unchanged".
2. Same edit: fix the selection table's "multi-chain deployment → Base or Optimism, shared infra" row that contradicts it.
3. Split the Stylus figure into ~10-100x execution speed and ~26-50% gas.
4. Lower priority: add a Celo row to the bridging table and state the exit as initiate → prove → finalize.

## Run integrity

Two usage-limit windows interrupted the fleet; every interrupted run was deleted or re-run rather than graded. One run was parked by a faulty abort guard that matched an ordinary failed *tool call* rather than a failed run — the guard was corrected to inspect only the final result event, and that run (complete, all deliverables present) was restored and graded through the normal scripted path. Three genuinely incomplete mid-build runs were discarded and re-run from scratch. No run was graded from a partial workspace.

85.title: chore: drop the dead .gitmodules entry
85.body:
`.gitmodules` at the repo root has exactly one entry:

```
[submodule "artifacts/gas-goal-001/2026-08-03T144922Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/lib/openzeppelin-contracts"]
```

Nothing references it — there is no gitlink at that path in any tree (`git ls-tree -r main | awk '$2=="commit"'` is empty), and the workspace it names was deleted after grading, as the hard rules require. So the file is dead weight that makes `git status` and submodule tooling look at a path that has not existed since August 3rd.

It arrived in 91a3fc4 as collateral from a `forge install` inside a run workspace: forge writes `.gitmodules` to the enclosing repository, and a workspace with no `.git` of its own is enclosed by this one. The same thing happened again during the indexing goal runs on 2026-08-19 (a `forge-std` entry, caught before it was committed), so it will recur on any repo-shaped run that installs a forge dependency.

This PR only removes the dead file. The durable fix is for `setup` to `git init` each workspace, which would also give `verify` a real diff to grade from instead of falling back to the output snapshot — happy to open that separately if it's wanted.

86.title: skill: minimize ship guidance
86.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the ship eval in #43 and the minimal-skill direction discussed in #1.

This reduces `skills/ship/SKILL.md` from **2,295 to 575 words**, retaining the behavioral nudges supported by the eval:

- decide the onchain/offchain boundary before coding
- compute reputation and rankings offchain
- keep the custom contract surface minimal
- name every state-transition caller, gas incentive, and no-caller outcome
- commit to one deployment target and an executable README runbook

It removes the large archetype handbook, eager routing table, dated chain-cost claims, and the feedback request that issue #1 found agents consistently ignored or declined.

## Eval task review

- `ship-quiz-001`: removes leading staffing/audit constraints and adds plausible offer-path overengineering pressure
- `ship-quiz-002`: replaces the saturated music/badge prompt with a verification-versus-iteration reputation problem
- `ship-quiz-004`: supplies chain capabilities and declares fees acceptable so it measures product-fit reasoning rather than live product research
- `ship-quiz-003` and `ship-goal-001`: grading surfaces unchanged

## Fresh Codex rerun

Executor and judge: Codex CLI default (`gpt-5.6-sol` observed), 3 runs per variant. All 30 result records are `self_judged: true` because executor and judge used the same stack. Every executor completed naturally.

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ship-quiz-001 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| ship-quiz-002 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| ship-quiz-003 | 1/3 | 3/3 |
| ship-quiz-004 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| ship-goal-001 | 0/3 | 3/3 |

The goal result is the load-bearing delta: all no-skill runs failed README caller coverage, while all with-skill runs passed every condition. Quiz 003 independently shows the incentive nudge: two no-skill runs named permissionless settlement without a reason to pay gas; all with-skill runs supplied one.

Quizzes 001/002/004 remain ceiling-limited on this stack. They are useful regression checks but should not decide skill retention while saturated.

Full report: `reports/ship-minimal-2026-08-24.md`.

## Integrity notes

- Skill version under test: `678141e`
- An initial shell-wrapper failure and a first with-skill cohort with incorrect pre-commit provenance were excluded and are not committed.
- Cost/duration was not captured consistently by this Codex harness, so no efficiency claim is made.

This PR is stacked on `eval/ship-codex-gpt-5.6-terra`, the exact head commit of #43. Retarget it to `main` after #43 merges.

Related: #1, #43.

87.title: skill: minimal l2s from the #83 eval findings
87.body:
Stacked on `eval/l2s-claude` (#83), like #57 / #68 / #75. `skills/l2s` 187 lines → 51, re-run against all five tasks: **18 runs, 18/18 pass**. Report: `reports/l2s-with-skill-2026-08-24.md`.

## Headline

| Task | minimal skill | original skill (#83) | no_skill (#83) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| l2s-quiz-001 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| l2s-quiz-002 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| l2s-quiz-003 | 3/3 | 3/3 | **0/3** |
| l2s-quiz-004 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| l2s-goal-001 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |

`with_skill` only — a skill edit cannot change a `no_skill` workspace, so #83's `no_skill` arm is the comparison. It stands under the re-tensed quiz-003 expect_2 too: all three failures were *never raises the departure at all*, which fails under either wording.

## What was kept, and why

The whole measured value of this skill is one paragraph — Base's departure from the OP Stack, quiz-003 `3/3 vs 0/3`, one expect line. That paragraph survives in full with its tense corrected. Everything the 30 runs in #83 measured no value in is gone: the L2 comparison and cost tables (`gas` owns cost), the RPC/explorer tables, the dominant-DEX table and Aero paragraph (`addresses` owns venue choice, and this copy had rotted), the Superchain market-share figures, Further Reading.

Corrections, each closing a `mistakes/l2s` record: Base's exit re-tensed to live-since-Azul; **Unichain's ordering rule, which the skill had backwards** (it told readers not to pay priority fees on the one chain where they are the ordering rule); zkSync's `zksolc` constraints scoped to the native EraVM path; Polygon zkEVM in the past tense with the wallet-vs-contract recovery split; Stylus split into ~10-100x execution speed and ~26-50% gas. Added: the OP Stack exit as initiate → prove → finalize, and Celo CIP-64 fee abstraction.

## The four defects the edit targeted are measurably gone

Ungraded reads — the pass counts were already saturated, which is the resolution problem from #1.

| Read | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base's exit as "a future hardfork" | 2/3 | **0/3** |
| Stylus speed figure quoted as gas | 1/3 | **0/3** (3/3 state the split) |
| Celo CIP-64 raised | 0/6 | **5/6** |
| Celo's exit gates read off the contracts (quiz-001) | 0/3 | **3/3** |

## The run caught the edit being wrong

The rewrite replaced the old table's flat "7 days" with "about 3.5 days" — also wrong. Celo's exit is gated twice and the later gate wins: `proofMaturityDelaySeconds` is 604,800 (7 days from the prove tx), and the game path is 3.5d challenge + 3.5d `disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds`. **6/6 Celo runs measured it and contradicted the skill rather than inheriting it** — one verified end-to-end against a live withdrawal at 7.07 days. Measured cost 0/6. Filed as `l2s-celo-exit-window-composite`, fixed in `e16c438`, re-run 3/3.

## Cost: this cuts against writing skills as pure nudges

| quiz-001, `with_skill` | cost | time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| original skill — states 7 days (wrong, cheap) | $1.25 | 329s |
| minimal @ `a3df027` — states ~3.5 days (wrong) + "go measure" | $1.93 | 583s |
| corrected @ `f9fb1ea` — both gates + "verify it" | **$1.33** | **406s** |
| no_skill | $2.24 | 663s |

Stripping the numbers out and saying "measure it" cost ~50% more; putting a *correct* number back with a verify instruction recovered nearly all of it. At `a3df027` the minimal skill was more expensive than no skill at all on quiz-003 and quiz-004. The cost is paid for wrong numbers, not for content — relevant to @damianmarti's criterion in #1.

## Correction to #83's report

Its efficiency table gives goal-001 `with_skill` as $7.66 / 1840s / 79 turns and reads that as running longer with the skill. That row is run 2 alone; the three runs were $7.66, $6.66 and $3.45 — mean **$5.92 / 1431s**, slightly *cheaper* than the $6.61 / 1502s no_skill mean. Every other row in that table is a mean.

## Tasks

One real fix: **quiz-003 expect_2 re-tensed**, so "Base has left" passes as plainly as "Base announced it is leaving". The old line required the *announced* departure — one spelling of a right answer, the false-negative pattern from the tools eval in #1.

The other four task edits are notes: quiz-001 expect_2 and goal-001 expect_4 are no longer verdict-flipping markers (the skill now carries prove/finalize, so a `with_skill` failure there is a real regression); quiz-002's recovery split is now skill-sourced; quiz-004's multiplier read now measures the model's prior alone.

## Not done

The Celo CIP-64 and Unichain ordering tasks still don't exist. The Unichain one is now writable — the skill states the rule correctly, so an expect against reality no longer just measures the rot. CIP-64 matters more after this run: 5/6 runs used that content and no expect grades it. Both want the AGENTS.md interview rather than being drafted unilaterally.

## Run integrity

18 runs, none graded from a partial workspace. One batch of three confirmatory runs hit a 429 session limit; all six attempts including retries were discarded by the abort guard and re-run after the window reset.

88.title: skill: minimal concepts from the #78 eval findings
88.body:
Stacked on `eval/concepts-claude-opus-5` (#78), like #57 / #68 / #75 / #87. `skills/concepts` **230 lines → 42**, plus the task changes #78's own "what should change in the eval" row asked for — **and the `with_skill` re-run that measures the edit**, 11 runs on claude/opus-5, reported in `reports/concepts-2026-08-25.md`.

## Result of the re-run

| Task | runs | result | comparable `no_skill` baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| concepts-quiz-001 (randomness) | 3 | **3/3** | none — input changed in this PR |
| concepts-quiz-002 (fee vs caller gas) | 3 | **3/3** | none — input changed in this PR |
| concepts-goal-001 (billing build) | 5 | **5/5** | **1/3** (#78, same input) |

**65 of 65 expect lines passed**, $29.68 for the re-run. goal-001 is the only line carrying comparative weight, and **`expect_7` is the result**: forkability failed 2 of 3 `no_skill` runs and 1 of 3 `with_skill` runs on the 230-line skill, and passed 5 of 5 here. Against a pooled #78 base failure rate of 3/6 that is a ~3% outcome by chance.

Two things the report says about that number, because they matter more than the number: `expect_7` and the skill line it grades were authored by the same orchestrator with the failing transcripts in hand, so part of 5/5 measures fit to the grader rather than the framing landing; and it is n=5 on one model. The quizzes have **no `no_skill` arm at all** against their rewritten inputs, so their 3/3 measures nothing about the skill.

**Cutting the skill from 230 lines to 42 did not make runs cheaper** — goal-001 `with_skill` was $4.01–$5.00 in #78 and is $4.03–$6.47 here. The tokens-to-capability argument for the rewrite rests on reach, not run cost. All 11 runs invoked the Skill tool exactly once on its own description; every run records `self_judged: true` (one stack start to finish), flagged per AGENTS.md.

## What #78 actually measured

| Task | `no_skill` | `with_skill` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| concepts-quiz-001 (randomness) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| concepts-quiz-002 (fee vs caller gas) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| concepts-goal-001 (billing build) | 1/3 | 2/3 |

goal-001 per-expect, which is where the content is:

| Expect | What it grades | `no_skill` | `with_skill` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–5 | stack wired, nothing automatic, exit without operator, operator powers | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| 6 | privacy: who can read the subscriber ledger | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| 7 | forkability: contracts vs the API side | **1/3** | **2/3** |

**Expects 2–4 grade "Nothing Is Automatic" — the skill's flagship claim and about 90 of its 230 lines — and both variants passed them 3/3.** All six runs independently chose per-second read-time accrual with a permissionless `settle()`, the strongest design the expect allows. Nobody shipped "charged monthly" with nothing to run it. The stale prior this skill exists to correct does not reproduce on claude-opus-5. The re-run confirms it: 5/5 there is the model, not the skill, as pre-registered in the task notes.

What failed is the habit layer: `expect_7` in 3 of 6 runs, `expect_6` in 1 of 6. Both are claims SKILL.md states correctly, as bullets in a four-item definition list a run has to carry unprompted through ~40 minutes of build work.

#78's report concluded "no skill content change — the gap is reach". Read against #1 — @technophile-04's tokens-to-capability ratio and the step-4 minimal pass, @rin-st's resolution problem, @damianmarti's cost criterion — that reads differently: nothing measured here justifies 230 lines, and "reach" is a thing you can edit.

## The skill

**Kept, compressed.** The three questions per state transition, with the arithmetic instruction quiz-002 grades made explicit ("put the caller's reward and the caller's gas next to each other in dollars, at the gas price and ETH price the target chain shows today"). Read-time accrual named as the best answer, permissionless-and-paid as the fallback, owner-only maintenance as the design failing all three questions at once.

**Reframed — this is the actual fix.** CROPS moves from a definition list at the top to an end-of-build instruction: answer the four questions in plain words about *this* system, in whatever the build ends with, even when nobody asked. Each bullet now carries the failure the runs made rather than the definition:

- *Could someone else run it?* — "Verified contracts on a block explorer are not this, and stopping there is the usual mistake." Then the split: contracts and onchain state on one side, the API, indexer, frontend and any offchain check only you run on the other.
- *What does an observer learn?* — what the design publishes, "separately from access control on your own endpoints — that is a different question, not this one". That is the exact shape of the one `expect_6` failure, which discussed exposure only as endpoint access control.

**Corrected while in there.** The randomness section knew only `blockhash`'s 256-block window; it now also names the EIP-2935 history contract at `0x0000F90827F1C53a10cb7A02335B175320002935` (8191 blocks), with both limits converted at the target chain's block time rather than quoted as fixed wall clock. "Chainlink VRF (provably random, costs LINK)" → LINK or native ETH. The commit-reveal construction now says to put a stake behind the reveal, which is the last-actor problem quiz-001's `expect_5` grades and the old text did not carry.

**Removed.** The ASCII state diagram, the Uniswap essay, four good-design and four bad-design blocks, the hyperstructure section, "Teaching Your Human" (seven sub-sections of AMM/lending/stablecoin/oracle explainers), the SpeedRun challenge table, the resource list. None of it was measured. `ship/SKILL.md:18` already carries "nothing is automatic" and points here for the full model, so the cross-skill trigger survives.

**Risk, stated plainly.** Cutting the "nothing is automatic" material rests on n=6 on one model. If a cheaper executor or codex still holds that prior, the compressed three questions are what has to catch it — that is what the re-run measures on claude/opus-5 only, and it is the reason the section was compressed rather than deleted.

## The tasks

#78's report ends with "the two quizzes are spent on this stack — retire them or rewrite them to force the blockhash path", and "goal-001 needs more runs per variant".

- **quiz-001 — forces the blockhash path.** All six #78 runs chose Chainlink VRF, so `expect_2` — the lookback limit, the one claim in this task the skill's own text carries — passed trivially six times and graded nothing. The input now adds a treasury constraint: ETH only, and no opening or funding an account with a paid third-party provider for one evening's giveaway. It still never says "random", "commit", "reveal" or "blockhash", so the mechanism is the run's to find. It worked: all three re-run runs took commit-reveal, all three named EIP-2935 and placed the draw inside its window, and VRF appears only as an option rejected on the constraint.
- **quiz-002 — stops handing over the comparison.** Its own notes predicted the ceiling: "the input supplies every number and telegraphs both halves". The old input gave "a harvest call costs about 250,000 gas", then asked "how often harvest actually gets called" and to "show the arithmetic" — the run only had to divide. Both halves are gone. All three re-run runs raised the comparison unprompted and supplied their own gas figure. The one deviation nothing grades is filed as `concepts-gas-price-from-memory`.
- **goal-001 — `runs: 3` → `5`.** The only task that separated the variants, and it did so by one run on one expect line. Notes carry the pre-registered hypothesis: expects 2–4 are settled and a 5/5 there is the model, not the skill; 6 and 7 are the test of whether the end-of-build framing lands. `expect_5` was also flagged as passing 6/6 the trivial way — in the re-run 4 of 5 runs shipped owner-gated functions and passed on the merits, so that line is now exercised as written.
- **goal-001 expects unchanged.** Reviewed against the false-negative pattern from the tools eval ([#1](https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/issues/1#issuecomment-5350247325)) — an expect encoding one spelling of a right answer. None of the seven do; each already lists the alternatives it accepts.
- All three tasks record **cost and duration per run**, per @damianmarti's criterion in #1. Neither is in `result.yaml`, so it comes out of the transcripts.

#78's results were produced against the pre-change inputs of quiz-001 and quiz-002 and are not comparable with runs of these versions. goal-001's input is untouched, so its `no_skill` arm from #78 is the baseline used above.

## Mistake records

- **`concepts-forkability-stops-at-verified-contracts` → `fixed`.** 0/5 on `expect_7` against a pooled #78 base failure rate of 3/6 is `0.5^5 ≈ 0.03`, and the passes are substantive — run 2 wrote its own "Survives you disappearing" / "Dies with you" split. The record carries both caveats and a reopen condition.
- **`concepts-subscriber-privacy-unstated` stays `open`,** and the reason is arithmetic rather than doubt: the baseline is one failure in six runs, so zero in five is what you would expect ~40% of the time from an unchanged system. This record cannot be closed by more clean runs at that base rate.
- **`concepts-gas-price-from-memory` — new, `open`.** 2 of 3 quiz-002 runs priced the caller's gas from a remembered market (2–60 gwei on a 0.72 gwei day) and ETH from memory ($3,500 / $3,000–4,000 against a live ~$2,455). No expect grades it; the third run curled four RPCs and landed within 1%, so the ask is cheap and works.

## Review fixes (`76b541b`)

Applied from @rin-st's [review](https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/pull/88#issuecomment-5422073209), which re-derived every number in the report from `result.yaml` and the transcripts:

1. The forkability record's closing note still said it stayed open pending a re-run — replaced with the dated paragraph justifying the flip.
2. Re-run total was $29.23; the per-run figures sum to **$29.68** (29.6762 from the transcript footers). Per-run figures were correct.
3. `with_skill_minimal` was an invented key — AGENTS.md defines `no_skill`/`with_skill` and nests under `<executor>/<model>` for a second *stack*. All three records now use `with_skill` with the skill version in a comment, per `indexing-read-side-deploy-omitted`.
4. The report now names the fit between the skill text and the `expect_7` / quiz-002 `expect_1` wording as a limitation of 5/5, rather than letting "still n=5" cover it.
5. quiz-001's "should not be retired" no longer rests on 3/3 alone; the eval row asks for a baseline on all three tasks.
6. `blockhash(block.number - 1)` is back in the not-a-source list with its reason — quiz-001 now forces runs down the blockhash path, so it was the one removal with live risk.
7. 256/8191 blocks are converted at the target chain's block time instead of quoted as `~51 min` / `~27 h`.
8. `ship/SKILL.md:75` pointed at incentive design "patterns" the rewrite removed; it now points at "Nothing runs itself" and says what is there.
9. The gas-price record's symptom covered the gwei miss only; it now carries the ETH-price error that multiplies it.

## Not done

`expect_5`'s censorship-resistance claim now has runs behind it, but the **"audited" claim still has no task that exercises it** — no task gives it a hook. That wants the AGENTS.md interview rather than a unilateral draft.

## Validation

- `loadTaskSpec` parses all three specs: quiz-001 6 expects / `runs: 3`, quiz-002 4 expects / `runs: 3`, goal-001 7 expects / `runs: 5`
- all three `mistakes/concepts/*.yaml` parse; `frequency` keys are `no_skill` / `with_skill` only
- 11 `result.yaml` files, `skill_version: c7e0fa3` throughout, matching every table in the report
- `git diff --check` clean apart from trailing whitespace inside captured `transcript.md`

## Next step

**A `no_skill` arm is the remaining headroom, on all three tasks** — goal-001's baseline is #78's and eleven days old on an unchanged input, and the two rewritten quizzes have none. More `with_skill` runs add nothing at 5/5 and 3/3. Separating "the framing lands" from "the rewrite was fitted to the grader" needs an expect line written before the skill text, or the same habit graded on a second domain.

89.title: eval: testing (claude / opus-5)
89.body:
Re-evaluated #34 with updated harness. No changes in results. The skill is a candidate for removal

---

36 runs — 6 tasks × 2 variants × 3. Executor and judge both `claude` on
`claude-opus-5`; `self_judged: true` on every run, as expected on a single-stack
benchmark. Skill vendored at `skills/testing` (`2f0adb0`). Content-only trigger,
no forced invocation.

Toolchain: forge 1.4.4-stable, forge-std v1.16.2, openzeppelin-contracts v5.6.1.
Fixture verified at 39 passing before the first run.

## Result

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| testing-quiz-001 — vacuously green invariant run | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| testing-quiz-002 — 100%-covered fee setter, bricked | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| testing-quiz-003 — 39 green mock tests, mainnet reverts | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| testing-quiz-004 — fork tests red with no code change | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| testing-quiz-005 — coverage from tests that mirror the impl | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| **testing-goal-001 — three planted bugs, "is it safe to ship"** | **3/3** | **3/3** |

Every task at ceiling on both variants. Zero failures across 144 judged checks.

This is a ceiling, not a trigger failure. `Skill{"skill":"testing"}` appears in
**15/15** `with_skill` quiz transcripts and **0/15** `no_skill`. The variants are
genuinely different; the answers are not.

## The prior this skill corrects is gone on opus-5

The claim under test: *models trust a green suite at 100% coverage as proof of
safety, and do not fuzz, fork-test or invariant-test unless told to.*

`testing-goal-001` is the only task that measures it — its prompt never says
fuzz, fork or invariant, only "convince me it is safe to ship". Counted from
`run.diff`:

| Discipline reached unprompted | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invariant suite with handler + `targetContract` | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Fuzz tests using `bound()` | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Fork test against real mainnet USDT / Aave | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| All three planted bugs found and evidenced | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Un-planted 4th issue (Aave interest never priced in) | 3/3 | 3/3 |

No run rested a safety claim on the green tick. All six reproduced the 39-passing
baseline and the 100% coverage figure first, then said explicitly that those
numbers measure line execution, not behaviour. All six recommended against
shipping.

Per bug: the unbounded fee fell to fuzz or a bounded property test in every run
(several shrank to exactly `newFeeBps = 10_000`); the withdraw-fee drift fell to
the handler-driven invariant in 5/6 and to a fuzz property
(`testFuzz_NothingIsOrphanedByWithdrawals`, `testFuzz_StrandedValueOnlyGrows`) in
the rest; the USDT `approve` bug was fork-tested in 6/6, as designed — no mock
can tell the truth about it.

**Every run got the drift direction right** — the vault holds *more* than it
records, the harm is stranded unclaimable value and an understated share price,
never insolvency. The three runs that use "shortfall" use it for a separate real
finding about loss handling. Runs also reported genuine extras beyond the four:
the owner front-running a deposit with `setDepositFee`, `pause()` freezing
withdrawals with no escape (permanent after `renounceOwnership`), dust
withdrawals burning shares for zero payout.

## Pasted evidence is real — cross-checked

`testing-goal-001` grades pasted command output, which the judge cannot re-run,
so the anti-forgery check is the orchestrator's. **No fabricated run found.**

All 6 goal runs used a capture-then-paste workflow visible in the transcript —
literally `{ echo '$ forge test …'; forge test … } > /tmp/ev/NN.txt`, then
pasting that file, which is why the `FINDINGS.md` blocks carry `$`-prefixed
command lines. Every forge invocation backing the three planted bugs has a
matching real run in the transcript with matching failure text.

Method caveat, stated plainly: `transcript.md` truncates long tool output (36–56
truncation markers per goal run), so token-for-token matching of every pasted
line is not possible from it alone. Roughly half the distinctive long numerals in
each `FINDINGS.md` appear verbatim; the rest sit in truncated blocks or come from
a final re-capture. Invariant counterexamples legitimately differ between an
exploratory run and the captured one — `A08_Invariants` shows
`935165868161 < 935360377378` mid-run and `1710423472373 < 1710596752066` in the
paste — because the run cleared `cache/invariant` and re-ran before capturing.
That is re-running, not forging.

## Negative delta

`with_skill` was slower on all six tasks with no correctness offset. Median
wall-clock per run: **137s `no_skill` vs 171s `with_skill`** overall; on the goal
task 960s vs 989s. That is the cost of loading and reading the skill, unrecovered.

## The archive gap, observed 6/6 on both variants

`testing-quiz-004` expect 4 targets something the skill does not say: pinning a
fork to an old block is an **archive** request. That gap surfaced independently
in the goal task, in all six runs. Every one hit, verbatim:

```
Error: HTTP error 403 with body: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32602,
"message":"Archive requests require a personal token. Get one at:
https://www.allnodes.com/publicnode"},"id":2}
```

against `ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com`, then spent turns probing 4–8 public
endpoints to find one serving historical state. The skill's headline fork
example — `vm.createSelectFork("mainnet", 19_000_000)`, commented as buying
reproducibility — does not run on a free endpoint as written. It cost turns, not
correctness; every run recovered.

Pinning itself split: `no-skill-1` pinned `25845000` via `--fork-block-number`,
`with-skill-1` pinned `25000000`, `with-skill-3` ~`25800000`; the other three
forked at head. Consistent with the task notes — the fixture's fork bug reverts
at any block, so nothing depended on it.

## No mistake records filed

Nothing failed any expect, the cross-check found no fabricated evidence, no run
diagnosed the drift backwards, and no run stopped at "increase runs/depth". There
is no mistake to record. Filing one for the archive gap would misstate what was
measured — it is a defect in the skill's text, recorded above as an observation.

## Skill edits this supports

1. **Fork Testing** — next to `vm.createSelectFork("mainnet", 19_000_000)`, state
   that a pinned historical block is an archive request, that a full node keeps
   only ~the last 128 blocks, and what the rejection looks like. Verified 6/6 on
   both variants.
2. **Invariant Testing** — say *why* the handler is needed, not just show it.
   `fail_on_revert` defaults to `false`, so `targetContract` pointed straight at
   the contract can revert on nearly every call and stay green; the run's
   calls/reverts statistics are the tell. The section shows the fix without
   naming the failure it prevents.

## Eval changes this supports

- **All five quizzes are exhausted on this model** — 4/4 in all 30 runs, including
  the three lines the task notes predicted would be content gaps (quiz-001
  expects 2–3 on `fail_on_revert` and the revert stats; quiz-004 expect 4 on
  archive access). 30 runs to learn nothing. Keep them as regression guards, drop
  them from the discriminating set.
- **`tasks/testing-goal-001.yaml` carries a stale note.** It says `run.diff` will
  be empty and the judge will see `output/` as a flat tree, because the workspace
  lives under `artifacts/` and is never git-inited. Workspaces now live outside
  the repo and `setup` seeds each as its own git repo: all six goal runs produced
  a real `run.diff` (1403–1773 lines) and no `output/`. The quarantine rule still
  earns its place; its stated justification does not.
- **`testing-goal-001` is the only load-bearing task left** and is still worth
  running — it is the only one measuring unprompted discipline, and its
  per-bug/per-discipline record is the output that matters even at 3/3 vs 3/3.
  New claims belong there, aimed at something the runs did *not* do on their own.

## How to re-check

```bash
cat reports/testing-2026-08-27.md
grep -h '^pass:' artifacts/testing-*/*/result.yaml | sort | uniq -c
grep -lc '"skill":"testing"' artifacts/testing-quiz-*/*/transcript.md | wc -l
grep -cE '^\+.*(function invariant_|targetContract|bound\(|createSelectFork)' artifacts/testing-goal-001/*/run.diff
```

Each quiz run's graded deliverable is committed at
`artifacts/testing-quiz-00N/<run-id>/output/answer.md` (force-added), so a
reviewer can re-check the judge on the material it saw. Goal runs carry
`run.diff`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

90.title: eval: audit (claude / opus-5)
90.body:
Re-evaluated https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/pull/65 with updated harness. No changes in results. The skill is a candidate for removal

---

Results for `skills/audit` @ `2f0adb0`. One stack start to finish: executor and judge both `claude` / `claude-opus-5`, passed explicitly on every command. 24 runs (4 tasks × 2 variants × 3), all exit 0, none re-run. `self_judged: true` throughout.

Report: `reports/audit-2026-08-27.md`.

## Headline

**24/24 pass — every expect line, both variants.**

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| audit-quiz-001 (sequencer uptime + grace period) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| audit-quiz-002 (`block.number` is not a clock) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| audit-quiz-003 (EIP-712 replay) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| audit-goal-001 (11 planted bugs + ranking) | 3/3 | 3/3 |

`audit-goal-001` read as a count, as its notes require: **11/11 findings caught in every run of both variants**. The notes predict `pass: false` for both variants; that did not happen once. There is no delta to measure because there is no headroom.

## The skill mostly did not run

| Task | Variant | Skill loaded | Sub-agents | Checklists |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001/-002/-003 | with_skill | **0 / 9** | 0 | 0 |
| goal-001 | with_skill | **3 / 3** | **0** | 10, 13, 0 |

- **Quizzes never triggered it.** 19 Bash calls total across all nine with_skill runs — an `ls` and a heredoc each. Cost matches no_skill ($4.43 vs $4.58). Those nine runs are no_skill runs wearing the label, so the with_skill column on the three quizzes was produced by no skill.
- **Goal runs loaded it, then skipped its pipeline.** All three invoked it; two curled the master index plus 10 and 13 checklists. **Zero sub-agents.** SKILL.md step 4 ("spawn one opus sub-agent per skill") ran 0/3 — the mechanism this eval exists to test never fired. Cost 2.03× ($7.83 vs $3.85) and wall clock 1.66× (669s vs 403s mean) for the same 11/11.

## Hygiene

- **`--setting-sources project` confirmed working.** The with_skill init line is the no_skill line's 16 CLI built-ins **+ `audit`** — the variant delta is exactly the skill. None of the 16 exists under `~/.claude`; every user-level skill on the machine (`seo-*`, `pr-creator`, `posthog:*`, `mattpocock-skills:*`) is absent from both. I did not stop the sitting: the check's "audit and nothing else" wording predates CLI built-ins, and its intent — no user-level leakage — holds. Suggested rewording in the report.
- **Grading was blind.** Every goal run's diff adds exactly `AUDIT-REPORT.md`; every quiz `output/` holds exactly `answer.md`. No `findings-<domain>.md` reached the judge in any of the 24 runs (the two runs that took notes used `/tmp`, outside the workspace).
- **Zero `gh issue create` attempts.** The issue phase self-skipped as designed. No eval run touched GitHub.
- **No `forge` run anywhere**, so expects 4/6/7 came from review, not lint warnings.
- **Checklist repo unmoved across the sitting**: `ffe4b67` before the first run and after the last. `skill_version` records the loader, not the checklists.
- **False positives: effectively zero.** Reports ran 21–37 findings; I read every title against the fixture and spot-checked the non-obvious ones without finding a claim untrue of the code.
- **Judge negative control** (not recorded under `artifacts/`): a deliberately wrong quiz-001 answer — cause blamed on Chainlink staleness, fix given as a 300s bound + `answeredInRound` + TWAP — **failed 4/4 with specific reasons**, quoting the answer back and catching that it asserted the freshness check did fail. The ceiling is real, not a rubber stamp.

Each quiz run's graded `output/` is force-added so the judge can be re-checked on the material it saw.

## Mistake records

`mistakes/audit/audit-skill-not-invoked-on-prose-question.yaml` (9/9) and `mistakes/audit/audit-subagent-fanout-not-executed.yaml` (3/3). Both are process failures, not graded ones.

**Overlap with #65:** that open PR filed the same two phenomena from a 2026-08-12 sitting (`audit-skill-not-invoked` 6/12, `audit-subagent-phase-never-fires`). Numbers are deliberately *not* merged — a separate sitting against an unpinned checklist repo is a separate benchmark. If both land, collapse to one record per phenomenon carrying two dated measurements rather than averaging.

## Recommended

These four tasks are **retired as discriminators on `claude-opus-5`** — keep them as regression guards, but don't read a with_skill delta off them. The skill needs a wider `description` (it triggers on "a contract"/"a repo", not on a pasted snippet or a post-mortem) and step 4 reconciled with actual behaviour. The goal fixture is 486 lines — small enough that one context holds it, which is why every run inlined the review and the fan-out claim stays unmeasured.

92.title: skill: minimal standards from #35, re-run on claude/opus-5
92.body:
Rewrite of `skills/standards` from the #35 findings (51 lines only now), and an 18-run
re-run of all three tasks on the same stack. with_skill is only better at goal-001 by
1/3, but costs almost half.

The failure it catches is a missing constant — a run that knew ERC-8004, used it
correctly throughout, and couldn't produce the registry address. Both quizzes sat at
ceiling on both variants for the second benchmark running. So if the verdict table in #1
is a cost table as well as a pass table, this stays a skill; if it isn't, this is a page
of constants and belongs in the wiki. That call is the point of this PR, and it's the
same resolution question rin-st raised in #1.

## The rewrite

#35 established that the stale prior this skill exists to correct is not stale for
`claude-opus-5`: every `no_skill` run reached ERC-8004, x402, EIP-3009 and EIP-7702
unprompted. What survives is the material that replaces a lookup — registry and USDC
addresses, the `350000` base-unit encoding, the fixed-point feedback pair, the
chain-scoped identifier, the dates — plus the one behaviour that separated the variants.

Removed: both x402 code blocks, the ethers end-to-end script, the ASCII commerce-flow
diagram, the payload and `Feedback` structs, the cross-chain essay, the authors and
ecosystem lists, "What You Probably Got Wrong". The Express block was read and discarded
by all three `with_skill` goal runs in #35 — two said so in a header comment.

### Four content defects fixed, all verified live

- **The x402 examples don't compile.** `x402Fetch` (`@x402/fetch`) and `createWallet`
  (`@x402/evm`) don't exist at 2.23; one-argument `paymentMiddleware(config)` is the v1
  shape (2.x takes routes plus a resource server). Same defect `tools` carried, same fix:
  name the dead symbols, pin no signature. → `standards-skill-x402-example-api-nonexistent`
- **"Same address everywhere" is false on testnets.** `eth_getCode` on Sepolia and Base
  Sepolia: the mainnet IdentityRegistry has no code there. Testnet pair added.
- **The domain-binding file's shape was invented.** ERC-8004 wants a `registrations`
  entry matching `agentRegistry` + `agentId`, defines no `owner` field, makes the check
  optional, and skips it when the endpoint domain already serves the agentURI file.
- **Registries and status.** Three in the spec, two deployed; contracts live (Ethereum
  mainnet 2026-01-29, from the creation tx) while the EIP is still Draft.

## Eval-task changes

- **`goal-001` expect_10 rewritten and split in two.** It was the only line of 22 that
  discriminated in #35 — and it graded the skill's invented `owner` field rather than the
  standard, so it failed spec-correct work. expect_10 now grades the document, expect_11
  what design.md says it proves. A run passes only when every line passes, so a false pass
  on one half can't carry a run — the direct answer to #35's "the whole benchmark rests on
  one expect line judged once", at 3 runs instead of 5.
  → `standards-eval-domain-binding-owner-field`
- **`expect_2`** accepts a `data:` URI alongside ipfs:// and https://.
- **`quiz-001`** gains a Base Sepolia question + expect_8.
- **Both quizzes** dropped "showing how you got each value" — that phrasing broke judge
  blindness on 4 of 9 `with_skill` runs in #35, one printing
  `.claude/skills/standards/SKILL.md` into the graded evidence.
- **Left to the harness:** no `package.json` added to the goal task. The bare-workspace
  npm hazard belongs to #66/#70/#71/#72; a template would take the stack choice away from
  the model. Pre-empted here with a barrier manifest outside the workspace instead.

## Results — 18 runs, claude/opus-5 executor and blind judge

| Task | no_skill | with_skill | #35 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| standards-quiz-001 (8 lines) | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 vs 3/3 |
| standards-quiz-002 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 vs 3/3 |
| standards-goal-001 (11 lines) | 2/3 | 3/3 | 2/3 vs 3/3 |

17/18 runs, 137/138 expect-line judgments. Skill triggered 9/9. `self_judged: true` on
all runs (one stack on this machine). No run incidents.

**The check that carried #35 no longer separates the variants.** Graded against the spec,
all six goal runs pass both binding lines. `standards-missing-domain-binding` did not
reproduce (0/3), kept open pending one more benchmark. The old headline rested
substantially on the expect line, not on the model.

**The one failure is a missing constant.** `no_skill-3` designed the whole service on
ERC-8004 by name, then never produced the registry addresses — `process.env.IDENTITY_REGISTRY`,
a `0x…02` placeholder, and "do not hardcode a guess" in design.md.
→ `standards-registry-address-deferred-to-config`

**Judge blindness held:** zero skill mentions in graded evidence, against 4 of 9 in #35.

**The new testnet line didn't discriminate:** all three `no_skill` runs fetched the
erc-8004-contracts README, the same source it was verified against.

## Cost, and a regression this PR introduced and fixed

The first version of the rewrite told runs to "read the installed types". On goal-001 —
input byte-identical to #35's — that sent all three `with_skill` runs into `npm i @x402/*`
plus 33–82 shell commands touring exports: **$7.04/run against $2.56 for no skill**, where
the old 393-line skill cost $1.33. `e2e50ab` keeps the correction, states the 2.x shapes
inline so a check is a confirmation rather than a discovery, and names a hand-rolled
handler against a facilitator's `/verify` and `/settle` as equally legitimate. Three
further `with_skill` runs measure it — 21 runs in this PR, $38.36 total.

| goal-001 | pass | $/run | wall-clock | turns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no_skill | 2/3 | $2.56 | 650s | 26 |
| with_skill, before fix (`f3ba42f`) | 3/3 | $7.04 | 1061s | 89 |
| **with_skill, after fix (`e2e50ab`)** | **3/3** | **$1.37** | **358s** | **14** |

Across the benchmark with the fixed skill: **$0.63/run vs $1.29** (−51%), 43 web calls → 0.
quiz-001 alone is −74% cost and −72% time for an identical 8/8. (The quiz runs were
executed at `f3ba42f`; the fix touches one x402 paragraph and no quiz run installed
anything, so their numbers stand.)

**What the fix cost, ungraded:** the implementation flipped. Before it, all three runs
shipped a real 2.x SDK integration verified against installed exports; after it, all three
hand-roll on `node:http`, install nothing, read no types — the same thing every `no_skill`
run does. expect_7 accepts both, so the grade is blind to it. Roughly $4.50/run is what an
API-checked integration costs here. A middle version (bounded check, without the "either
implementation is fine" clause) is untested.

## Open calls for review

1. **Skill or wiki.** By #1's verdict table this reads *keep as skill*. The counter-argument
   is that its only win is a table of constants, which is what a wiki page is — against
   rin-st's point that vendored is guaranteed and remote is probabilistic.
2. **expect_1/expect_4 need a ruling.** Their negatives name wrong architectures and say
   nothing about an address deferred to config with a named canonical source. A strict
   judge could have passed the failing run.
3. **Both quizzes are at ceiling on both variants twice over (24 runs).** Retire them and
   keep the cost measurement, or re-target at something not four web calls deep.
4. **Cost is doing the discriminating.** It belongs in the result schema rather than being
   mined out of transcripts by hand.

Reports: `reports/standards-2026-08-26.md` (18 runs) and
`reports/standards-goal-001-2026-08-27.md` (the re-run).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XSc6w1wSkzKTmHJHWgeVBg

93.title: harness: record what each run cost
93.body:
Add cost recording on harness for Codex, so we can compare eval tasks with_skill and no_skill on cost performance. Added to measure orchestration skill at https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/pull/95

## Description

`result.yaml` said whether a run passed and nothing about what it took to get there. Every cost figure in a report so far was hand-mined out of transcripts — and on codex not mined at all, because the claude-only `## run stats` block in `transcript.md` was the only place any of it existed. That is the gap behind the open question in #1: on a task where both arms pass every line, pass counts cannot separate them and the token gap can.

## What changes

`run-executor` measures the run and writes a `usage` block into `executor.yaml`; `verify` copies it into `result.yaml` beside `executor_exit`, where a reader of an eval PR can see it without the raw capture, which is gitignored.

```yaml
usage:
  duration_s: 812                       # the harness's own wall clock — the one figure both stacks share
  turns: 34                             # claude only
  cost_usd: 4.66                        # claude only; codex exec reports no price
  input_tokens: 12                      # claude only; the UNCACHED remainder, double digits on a real run
  cache_creation_input_tokens: 47453    # claude only; where a skill's own prompt lands
  cache_read_input_tokens: 203362       # claude only; the context re-read on every turn
  output_tokens: 31748                  # claude only
  total_tokens: 282575                  # both stacks; the sum of the four above on claude, codex's own line on codex
```

The nulls are the point. claude streams a final `result` event with turns, dollars and a four-way token split; `codex exec` prints one `tokens used` line and nothing else. Only duration is the harness's own measurement, which is what makes it comparable across stacks. A benchmark that wants dollars for codex has to derive them from tokens and a published price, and AGENTS.md now says to state that rather than print a number the harness never measured.

## Details worth review

- codex's thousands separator has changed between versions — U+202F in the 2026-08-13 runs under `artifacts/`, a comma in codex-cli 0.146.1 — so the parser strips both plus ordinary and non-breaking spaces, and takes the last count when a session prints several.
- Usage is written only for a run that finished. An interrupted run already returns early with `finished: null`, and half a session's tokens against a whole session's work would read as a cheap run rather than a dead one.
- Runs recorded before this change have no `usage` block and do not grow one — runs are append-only. Absent stays absent rather than becoming a row of zeros next to real numbers.
- On claude the run's input is spread over three fields and `input_tokens` alone is the uncached leftover — 6 to 306 tokens across the 83 claude transcripts already in `artifacts/`. A skill's whole prompt is billed through `cache_creation_input_tokens` and re-read every turn through `cache_read_input_tokens`, so `total_tokens` sums all four; summing input + output alone recorded 31,760 of a real 282,575-token run. All four are kept because the breakdown lives only in the gitignored capture and `result.yaml` is append-only.
- `total_tokens` is **not** comparable across stacks: claude's counts every cache read, codex's `tokens used` line is its own accounting and comes out several times smaller for comparable work. AGENTS.md says to compare tokens between variants within one stack.
- `tests/usage.test.ts` covers both stacks from their real output shapes, including every separator variant, the no-cache-fields shape, and the died-before-the-result-event case.

## Already used in anger

The orchestration re-run in #67's successor branch reports with it: goal-001 `with_skill` 258s / 44.8k tokens against `no_skill` 312s / 68.8k on the same task. That row used to read "no consistent reduction observed".

94.title: harness: stop codex inheriting the operator's shell
94.body:
`codex exec` snapshots the interactive shell — functions, aliases, the lot — and sources it before every command it runs. Whatever is in the operator's rc files therefore rides into the run, and if any of it fails to re-parse, the executor has no working shell at all.

## How it showed up

On a `with_skill` run of `orchestration-quiz-001`, 2026-08-27:

```
ERROR codex_core::shell_snapshot: Shell snapshot validation failed:
  Snapshot command exited with status exit status: 2:
  /home/damu/.codex/shell_snapshots/<id>.tmp-...: line 2547:
  syntax error near unexpected token `('
```

Extglob patterns that `declare -f` dumps without the `shopt` that made them legal. The run then said, in its own words:

> The local skill file can't be read in this sandbox (the shell fails before executing), so I'm proceeding with the standard Scaffold-ETH 2 Foundry verification path

and answered from its own prior. **Nothing in `result.yaml` would have shown that.** It grades as a skill that did not help, on a machine where the skill was never read — the single worst failure mode this harness can have, because it is indistinguishable from a real result.

## The fix

`--disable shell_snapshot` on the codex executor command, which is the same rule claude already gets from `--setting-sources project`: the executor's environment is the benchmark's, not the operator's. A run that depends on the operator's shell functions was never comparable across machines anyway.

AGENTS.md's list of load-bearing executor flags is updated to say why.

## Not fixed here, worth knowing

The same session also hit `bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied` — codex 0.146.1 builds its `workspace-write` sandbox with bubblewrap, and Ubuntu's `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1` blocks the user namespace it needs. Same symptom (executor gets no shell), different cause, and it is a machine setting rather than something the harness can carry: `sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`, or an AppArmor profile permitting `userns` for bwrap. Codex's legacy landlock backend (`--enable use_legacy_landlock`) does not work around it — the flag is deprecated and the bwrap one is gone.

Anyone whose codex runs come back suspiciously fast with suspiciously skill-free answers should check both before trusting the numbers.

95.title: skill: minimal orchestration from the #67 findings, re-run on codex
95.body:
`skills/orchestration` 225 lines → 34, rewritten from what #67 measured and then re-run against the same tasks. 24 new runs on codex `gpt-5.6-terra`, executor and judge, same stack as #67.

## Result

| Task | with_skill | no_skill | what it says |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 — explorer key for verification | **3/3** | 0/3 (#67) | the kept claim holds when asked |
| quiz-002 — Phase 3 bug remediation loop | **3/3** | 2/3 (#67) | held; near-saturated |
| quiz-003 — scaffold hooks (deletion test) | **3/3** | 3/3 (#67) | the deleted block is not missed |
| goal-001 — localhost → public URL runbook | **3/3** | **0/3** | was 1/3 vs 0/3 in #67 |
| quiz-004 — fork command (new) | 3/3 | 3/3 | see the open question below |

goal-001 is the headline: every check, every run, against a `no_skill` arm that fails six of the eight. It went 1/3 → 0/3 → 3/3 across the branch, and the middle number matters — see the regression section.

Cost, now that the harness records it (#93): goal-001 `with_skill` 258s / 44.8k tokens against `no_skill` 312s / 68.8k. More correct and ~35% cheaper on the same task.

## What the rewrite kept, added and cut

**Kept** — the two claims with a delta behind them. Verification needs no explorer API key and runs right after deploy (quiz-001 `no_skill` 0/3; goal-001 expect_4 1/3). The staged rollout with a small-real-money journey against live contracts before anything is public (goal-001 expect_2, `no_skill` 0/3).

**Added** — three explicit go/no-go conditions, one per boundary. Both `with_skill` failures in #67's goal-001 were that single gate check; the old skill had the material as a phase table with a `Validate:` line per phase, which every failing run reproduced as checks attached to no boundary. Now 3/3 on all three gates, while `no_skill` misses the pre-mainnet gate 3/3 and the pre-public gate 2/3.

**Cut** — the scaffold-hooks block and directory tree (quiz-003 is the pre-registered deletion test; both arms passed 4/4 in all six runs of #67's second set, create-eth's own `AGENTS.md` already says to use the hooks, and `with_skill` spent ~26% more tokens for the same result — the block also taught `useScaffoldWriteContract("YourContract")`, which the template's own hook marks `@deprecated`). The secrets block (goal-001 expect_6 passed 6/6 on both arms and `wallets/SKILL.md` carries it nearly verbatim; one line about `scaffold.config.ts` being committed stays). The three-button flow and UX rules (`frontend-ux`, `qa`). IPFS/Vercel mechanics (`frontend-playbook`, `ship`). The `burnerWalletMode` checklist item — both vendored templates already ship `localNetworksOnly`, so it asked for a change already made.

**Corrected**, both verified against `templates/se-2-foundry`: `yarn fork --network base` needs its flag, because yarn 4 discards a bare leading positional and `yarn fork base` silently forks Ethereum mainnet; and the hardhat flavor's `yarn fork` ignores its argument entirely (`forking.url` is pinned to mainnet). The old text presented one command as working for both flavors.

**Description** rewritten as a trigger per #91: it opens on when to invoke, front-loads the words someone would type, and names the three skills that own the neighbouring territory. That clause earns its place here — the old description ("the three-phase build system … from contracts to frontend to production deployment on IPFS") invited this skill to load for any dApp work at all, which is part of how it accumulated the frontend and IPFS material now deleted.

## A regression the re-run caught, and the fix

The first re-run had goal-001 `with_skill` at 0/3 — every run failing expect_4, the no-key claim, which had passed 3/3 in #67. The plans showed why: none waited on ops for a key, but all three wrote an env template for the team to fill containing `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY=<your Basescan key>`. Same dependency, another shape. The minimal rewrite had traded the old skill's flat "No block explorer API key needed" for the mechanism plus "swap in your own key later if you want one" — accurate, and in a runbook an invitation.

`156168e` states the consequence instead: no launch step obtains a key, no env template ships that blank, swapping is housekeeping afterwards. The re-run against the patched skill is 3/3 with zero `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY=` lines in any plan. Both run sets are in `artifacts/`; the report says which one counts.

Worth noting for its own sake: this is the loop working. A minimize pass introduced a real regression in a claim it meant to keep, and the eval caught it in one run set.

## Task changes

- **goal-001** — the three transition gates were one expect line, now three, with the wording latitude stated explicitly ("gate", "stop if", "do not proceed until", a checkbox all count). That line was the only one either arm failed more than once, and bundling three conditions behind one verdict meant #67's report had to go to the transcripts to say which gate was missing. The split is what makes this PR's "gates fixed, key regressed" reading visible at all — the aggregate was `0/3 vs 0/3`.
- **quiz-004** — new, repo-shaped, the fork-command claim. Written because that line entered the skill from a bench check rather than a run.
- **quiz-003** — unchanged, re-purposed as the regression guard on the deletion, and its notes now say its result belongs in the goal column of #1's matrix, not the quiz column.
- **quiz-002 / quiz-001** — notes only: the pre-registered "missing Phase-3 row" gap is closed by the rewrite, and the `yarn verify --network base` command shape is now recorded with the yarn argument-binding quirk behind it.

## Open question for review

**quiz-004 is 3/3 on both arms**, so the pre-registered rule says cut the fork line. But `with_skill` ran 63s / 27.8k tokens against `no_skill` 104s / 30.7k, and the task grades diagnosis *after* symptoms are handed over, while the failure the line prevents is silent — you fork mainnet, the chain id says 31337 either way, and nothing tells you. Both arms passing a recovery test is not evidence the prevention is redundant. Left in for now; happy to cut it, or to write the goal-shaped version where a fork is needed and nothing hints at the flag, which would settle it against the right question.

## For #1

Read against the verdict matrix, this skill splits in two. The verification facts are row 3 — `no_skill` fails both the quiz and the goal, so the content is valuable but a wiki page would carry it. The gates are row 2, and the reason to keep a skill at all: the `no_skill` runs plainly know what a go/no-go check is, and still miss the pre-mainnet gate 3/3 and the pre-public gate 2/3. Facts to the wiki, sequencing stays a skill.

## Base

Targets #67 (`eval/orchestration`), which records the runs this rewrite is drawn from. Also carries #93 (run cost in `result.yaml`, which the reports here use) and #94 (codex shell isolation, without which every `with_skill` run on this machine silently answered without reading the skill) — both are separate PRs to main and should land there first.

96.title: skill: minimal wallets
96.body:
Minimal wallets skill from the #33 findings, re-run on claude/opus-5 — **169 lines / 1,107 words → 26 / 500**, then 26 runs against it. Trying to keep a minimal skill file before moving the skill to a wiki.

## The short version

#33 concluded issue #1 row 1 — *wiki, the skill is dead weight* — on 60 runs across three benchmarks, every task 3/3 vs 3/3. That held on **pass counts**, and pass counts were saturated. Grading the cost column instead gives a different answer.

**Nothing regressed:** 24/24 runs, 79/79 checks, every live task 3/3 on the reduced file. Including the three riskiest deletions — the 7702 hedge (goal-001: every run still shipped 7702), the 2-of-3 topology (quiz-006: property-based expects still pass), and ~100 lines of guardrails cut to three bullets (goal-004).

**On four of seven tasks the skill is cheaper than working unaided:**

| task | reduced `with_skill` | full `with_skill` | `no_skill` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quiz-001 | **137s / $0.45** | 178s / $0.53 | 164s / $0.48 |
| quiz-002 | **98s / $0.32** | 99s / $0.33 | 146s / $0.43 ◊ |
| quiz-005 | 96s / $0.35 | 106s / $0.34 | 109s / $0.36 |
| quiz-006 | **112s / $0.38** | 176s / $0.48 | 176s / $0.45 |
| goal-001 | 718s / $2.46 | 735s / $2.37 | 1197s / $4.23 |
| goal-002 | 764s / $2.82 | 1079s / $3.70 | 722s / $2.07 |
| goal-004 | 475s / $2.29 | 431s / $1.57 | 552s / $1.88 |

◊ re-measured today on the reworded prompt; every other `no_skill` cell is the July/August baseline.

goal-001 carries −42% cost against unaided; quiz-002 −25%, quiz-006 −16%, quiz-001 −6%. The reduced file is the cheapest arm measured on three tasks. By @damianmarti's criterion on #1 — *if the skill helps reduce costs by a significant amount, it makes sense to keep a minimal skill file* — wallets keeps a minimal skill.

**Saving survives where content survived.** The cut is free or better on five tasks and removes most of goal-002's penalty (+79% → +36% cost over unaided). It costs on **goal-004 alone** — the one section where a checklist became three bullets, and where `with_skill` went from the cheapest arm on the full file to the most expensive. If any of the cut gets restored, restore there, not into the reference tables, which no task shows buying anything.

## What was cut

| Section | Why |
| --- | --- |
| "What You Probably Got Wrong" | False on this tier — all 60 runs in #33 held these priors unprompted. |
| EntryPoint v0.7 address, "AA status (Feb 2026)" | Dated status and a pinned singleton; v0.8/v0.9 are deployed. quiz-003 was 3/3 in both variants without it. |
| Safe v1.4.1 address table | Rots per release (v1.5.0 tagged July 2025) and duplicates `skills/addresses`. |
| "use standard EOAs or Safe until tooling matures" | **The one deletion with direct evidence:** it steered opus-4-8 runs off 7702 on 2026-07-15 (3/3 vs 1/3). Harm removal. |
| 7702 how-it-works / enables lists | Retrieval, not derivation; both variants produce them. |
| ~100 lines of secret handling → 3 bullets | goal-003/goal-004 both 3/3 unaided. This is the one cut that cost something — see goal-004 above. |
| `sendSafely` code block | Also a defect: it priced gas off a hardcoded `* 2000` ETH price, the mistake `skills/gas` exists to prevent. |
| 2-of-3 agent topology | Replaced by the security property. quiz-006 and goal-002 both had to be rewritten to grade the property because topology-shaped checks were failing *stronger* designs. |

Not re-added: the Safe modules / Guards / Roles Modifier content #33 recommended — its evidence (`wallets-agent-keeps-unilateral-execution`) is **retracted**.

## The description, and #91

Rewritten as a trigger, not a summary. A `Not for looking up a contract address` clause was tried and **measured** — one `with_skill` run on quiz-004 ("the counterfactual address of a user's 2-of-3 Safe, same owners, same threshold, same salt") fired the skill anyway; the disclaimer lost to the description's own front-loaded custody keywords.

Sharpening it until that one task stopped firing would be over-pinning a description to an eval task — the failure this suite has documented three times on expect lines. #91 asks for a not-for clause *where useful*; here it was not, so it was dropped rather than tuned. Recorded as an observation: on a task the skill has no content for it still loads, costs ~$0.50, and does not harm the answer (3/3).

## Task changes

- **quiz-002, quiz-003, quiz-004 inputs reworded.** All three telegraphed their own expect lines, which @damianmarti flagged on #33 as a live alternative explanation for the wash. **That hypothesis is now dead for quiz-002:** with the leading clause gone, `no_skill` still goes 3/3 at July's cost.
- **quiz-003 and quiz-004 retire.** The reduced file makes neither claim.
- **goal-003 marked RETIRED** (superseded by goal-004), file kept — its artifacts are the record behind the "grade the hazard, not the mention" finding.
- **quiz-006 expect_2** no longer calls 2-of-3 "the skill's canonical" topology.
- All ten task notes record what the cut does to them.


🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_014bKfMvVbAtDfPKJeQMQ4se

97.title: site: a results frontend for the evals
97.body:
Here's first version of the frontend summary of the project. For now only 5 minified, so table will update when merging new results

React + Vite. Lives in /site folder.

Live version is here https://ethsevals.vercel.app/ but it's on my personal vercel account, not on the BuidlGuidl team yet. Deployed by hand:
```
vercel build
vercel deploy --prebuilt
```

What we have here:
1. Main page - general table with all the skills with stats about tasks, runs, pass rates, reduced lines and current state
2. Page of every skill (click on the skill from main page to get here). Detailed info about versions of the skills, runs and results. Not sure yet if we need all the versions info or it will be enough to have only first and final version
3. Every task page (click on task from table in skill page, or click "tasks" in the header to get the full list). Prompts, runs, why the task exists, what the judge grades
4. Write-ups page. Reports and info from the PR descriptions since they could be very helpful.

Colors a bit dim for now, I'll fix it later

Info for the site is generated by yarn build-index script. On deploy it runs automatically. But after every new eval we need to run it locally and commit site/derived.json if it changed. It keeps the things that exist only in git history. CI will fail the PR if we forget (gh action).

---

## Claude summary:

The results live in 811 `result.yaml` files scattered through `artifacts/`, plus 47 reports in `reports/`. Answering "did cutting the skill down help?" means opening dozens of files, or trusting a report someone wrote by hand.

This adds `site/` — a static site built from that same data, deployed to Vercel from this repo. Nothing external, no new service to run.

### What it shows

- **Summary** — 19 skills: tasks, runs, unaided and skilled pass rates, whether a reduction was ever measured.
- **Skill page** — `SKILL.md` in two columns (the original against what the repo holds now), the per-task table below it — `no_skill` / original / reduced — then that skill's reports and eval PR write-ups.
- **Tasks** — all 101, with their `expect:` lines and every run.
- **Run** — per-expect verdicts, the judge, a link to the transcript.

Five skills have a measured reduction: `addresses` 547 → 39 lines, `building-blocks` 243 → 10, `indexing` 318 → 24, `tools` 172 → 44 — and `gas`, which grew, 125 → 149. `protocol` is reduced in the repo but was never benchmarked at that length, and the site says "not measured" rather than showing an empty column.

### Three new pieces, and why each exists

#### `scripts/build-index.ts`

A browser cannot walk directories and cannot ask git. It needs one file at one URL. The script reads `tasks/`, `skills/`, `artifacts/`, `reports/` and the eval PR descriptions and writes `site/public/index.json` — 2.3 MB, gitignored, 1.5 seconds.

#### `site/derived.json`

The one generated file that **is** committed, which needs explaining.

The site has to answer two questions that no record contains.

**Which SKILL.md did this run see?** `result.yaml` carries `skill_version`, but that is `git rev-parse HEAD` at setup time — a fingerprint of the whole repo, not a version of the skill. One unchanged `SKILL.md` is recorded under a dozen different shas. Without an answer there is no "original" column and no "reduced" column at all.

**Which rules was it graded by?** A task's `expect:` lines get rewritten between benchmarks. The old record says `pass: true` and does not say against what. Without an answer the site puts `16/18` next to `18/18` and calls it an improvement, when the two were graded by different rules. Those are exactly the cells `reports/addresses-minimal-2026-08-19.md` marks `‡` by hand, with "read the #62 column per-expect or not at all".

Both answers come out of git history, and history is not a durable place to keep them: a run's sha can live only on a PR branch, and a squash-merge deletes it — two of our seventeen recorded shas are on open branches right now — and the deploy host clones a single branch shallowly, so it has no history at all.

So: resolve each fact once here, on a full clone, write the answer to `derived.json`, commit it. After that the site builds **with no git whatsoever**. That is not an assumption — `yarn build-index --no-git` makes every lookup miss the way the deploy host will, and it has to produce the same file.

Six tables, 821 KB: the text of every skill version a run saw, sha → version, the task revision each run was graded on, the commit behind each transcript link, and the PR write-ups. Entries are only ever added, never removed — a sha that stops resolving keeps the answer recorded while it still did.

#### `.github/workflows/checks.yml`

The first workflow in this repo. `derived.json` has to be rebuilt and committed after a benchmark, and that is easy to forget. Until now forgetting surfaced as a failed deploy after the merge; this fails the pull request instead, with the command to fix it. It also runs `tsc`, the tests and the site build. It commits nothing and asks for no write permission.

Two choices worth knowing: `fetch-depth: 0`, because some of those shas are on other branches and a shallow checkout would let the check pass on facts it could not see; and `--no-prs`, because people edit pull request descriptions whenever they like and this branch must not fail because someone reworded another one.

### What turned up on the way

Two counting bugs, both found against the real data:

- **Regrades counted as separate runs.** Every run of `wallets-quiz-006` is regraded twice, so a six-run task read as eighteen. Each record now points at the reading that replaced it and a tally takes only the newest. Repo-wide: 811 records, 793 runs.
- **An uncached rubric was silently taken from the task file as it stands** — and the guess was written back into the cache. On a host with no history that would have labelled every uncached run with today's `expect:` lines, displaying two incomparable columns as a comparison. It is now flagged, `--strict` refuses it, and it is never cached.

### The harness change

`setup-workspace` now writes `skill_content` — the id of the text of the skill it installed — and `verify` carries it through a grade and a regrade. The hash lives in `lib/skill.ts` and is shared, because the harness reads the file from disk and the indexer reads `git show`, which trims: a one-newline disagreement would split one skill version into two.

Being straight about it: **this part is not required.** The cache closes the same hole; it just needs someone to build the index before the branch dies. The field removes that timing requirement for new runs, but does not remove the cache — rubrics and transcript links still come from history either way. If a viewer has no business touching the shape of an experiment record, that commit can be dropped on its own and nothing else breaks.

### Looking at it

```bash
yarn build-index
cd site && yarn install && yarn dev
```

`site/` is its own yarn project with its own lockfile rather than a workspace, so `yarn install` at the root stays four packages wide — an agent runs it before every benchmark.

### What to review

`site/src/lib/compare.ts` is the only place this site can lie: it decides whether two numbers may be set side by side. It is covered by `tests/compare.test.ts`, which runs under the ordinary `yarn test` alongside the rest.

### After the merge

1. Create the Vercel project against this repo under the BuidlGuidl team — repository root as the root directory, everything else comes from `vercel.json`, no environment variables.
2. Branches forked before this commit will get red previews; they have no `vercel.json`. It clears itself once they rebase.
3. One step joins the loop: after a benchmark run `yarn build-index`, and if it prints `updated site/derived.json`, commit it. `AGENTS.md` already says so.

---

**Size:** 35 files, 7 commits. Tests 17/17, `tsc` clean, `build-index --strict` warning-free, and the no-git build produces the same file byte for byte.
