98.title: eval: wallets goal-004 at n=7 — with_skill 6/7 vs no_skill 1/7 (p=0.029)
98.body:
Follow-up to #96, which merged while these runs were in flight. It answers the one question #96
left open, and the answer is the first significant result this suite has produced. Goal-004 `with_skill` 6/7 vs `no_skill` 1/7. Claude suggested raising goal-002 to n=7 too, but I'm not sure if this worths. I think the current minimized wallet skill makes sense and helps the agents.

## Result

**wallets-goal-004, n=7 per variant: `with_skill` 6/7 vs `no_skill` 1/7. Fisher exact two-tailed
p = 0.029.**

| | pass | fail | failing check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `with_skill` | **6** | 1 | expect_2 (`.gitignore` / pushable tree) |
| `no_skill` | **1** | 6 | **expect_3 ×6** |

The failure modes do not overlap, which matters more than the counts. All six unaided failures are
expect_3 and *nothing else* — each of those runs passed the other three checks. The single aided
failure is a different check. The arms are not differing in rate on a shared failure; they fail for
unrelated reasons.

**What expect_3 grades, read from the runs.** The guardrails report warned this check reads as
borderline, so the runs were read before the counts. It is not borderline — the difference is
behavioural:

- Aided runs derive the brief's key to `0x6Ed090E7EBd28B191810eaBc9b2c31B9660A2402`, put that
  address on a deny list (`BURNED_ACCOUNTS`, `config.ts`) so the delivered scripts **refuse to sign
  with it**, and keep `sweep` able to drain it as the rescue path.
- Failing unaided runs state the rule — *"if a key is exposed, it is burned"* — and never point at
  this key. Nothing in their code knows about it.

## The caveat to cite alongside the p-value

The n=7 cell **mixes designs**: 3 runs per variant batched (2026-08-27/28, from #96) with 4
interleaved (2026-08-29). The interleaving argument strictly covers only runs 4–7, which on their own
are `with_skill` 3/4 vs `no_skill` 0/4 — **p = 0.14, not significant**. The significance comes from
pooling. Pooling is legitimate here — same skill file by md5, same judge, same model, same expects,
no limit-killed runs — but it is a step a reader should be able to check without re-deriving it, so
both numbers are in the report and in the commit message.

Second caveat, also in the report: an earlier benchmark of this same task ran the **other** way —
2026-08-06, full skill file, `no_skill` 3/3 vs `with_skill` 2/3
(`reports/wallets-guardrails-2026-08-06.md`). Those six runs are deliberately **not** counted in the
frequency above, which covers only the 14 runs against the reduced file.

## Why the runs are interleaved

Both prior n=3 results on this task were collected as a **batch per variant in a single session**,
and they pointed in opposite directions three weeks apart on identical expects and the same codex
judge. That leaves a session-level effect confounded with the variant. Runs 4–7 alternate
`no_skill` / `with_skill` inside one session, one run start to finish before the next is set up.
Free to do, and it is what makes this result readable. Recommended for every future benchmark.

## Cost — the skill costs ~21% more here, and is worth it

| variant | n | turns | duration | cost | range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `no_skill` | 7 | 36 | 521s | $1.63 | $1.24–$2.43 |
| `with_skill` | 7 | 43 | 464s | $1.97 | $1.61–$2.63 |

This inverts the framing #96 ran on. On this task the skill is not buying a discount — it is buying
a pass, and the extra $0.34 per run buys 6/7 against 1/7. (Duration is not comparable across the two
dates: runs 1–3 were 6-concurrent, runs 4–7 ran alone. Cost and turns are.)

`run-stats` prints the aided row at **n=8** — 44 / 470s / $2.12 — because it counts the excluded
`2750ecf` run. The row above is the counted n=7; the report carries the seven per-run values so the
median is checkable. An earlier revision of this PR printed the n=8 row, which had that run out of
the pass count and in the cost median at the same time.

## Context from #96, for anyone picking this up cold

#96 reduced `skills/wallets` from 169 lines / 1,107 words to **26 / 500** and re-ran the suite.
@rin-st's review there found the comparison basis was unsound: of 78 prior wallets runs, none carried
a run-stats footer, the guardrails report recorded no cost at all, and one cost cell was the
2026-07-25 *benchmark-wide* medians carrying the other variant's column. Re-measuring all six stale
unaided arms same-day changed the conclusion twice — the cost deltas moved, and the pass column
turned out not to be saturated. That is what produced goal-004 3/3 vs 1/3 at n=3, and this PR is the
follow-up it asked for.

#96 also added the harness pieces this PR leans on: `yarn run-stats` (cost tables derived from
committed transcript footers, never assembled by hand), `status: live | retired` on task specs, and
`input_sha` with a `--regrade` guard.

## What this does not establish

- **One task.** goal-002 stays at n=3 (3/3 vs 2/3) and is unresolved. The five quiz tasks are 3/3 vs
  3/3 and saturated.
- **One model tier.** Everything is `claude-opus-5`.
- **One guardrail.** expect_3 is the only check that has ever discriminated here. The four guardrails
  the cut deleted still have nothing grading them.
- **Nothing about the description.** No task in the suite could catch the narrowed description
  failing to fire.
- **Half the aided arm is unauditable.** Runs 1–3 (2026-08-27, from #96) committed neither `output/`
  nor `run.diff`, so `verify --regrade` refuses them. Runs 4–7 and all seven `no_skill` runs carry
  11–16 output files each. The unauditable half is the non-interleaved half — the half the pooled
  significance rests on — so the reasons pooling is legitimate cannot yet include "same, checkable
  evidence".
- **The control arm moved on its own.** `no_skill` was 3/3 on 2026-08-06 and is 1/7 on 2026-08-28/29,
  same expects and same judge: Fisher two-tailed **p = 0.033** on that pair alone. A `no_skill` run
  reads no skill file, so full-vs-reduced cannot explain it. Read against the aided arm going 2/3 →
  6/7, most of the separation is the control collapsing rather than the skill improving, which makes
  *whatever else changed between those dates* the leading alternative explanation for p = 0.029.

## Contents

- 8 runs (`artifacts/wallets-goal-004/2026-08-29T*`), `output/` force-added so the judge can be
  re-checked on the material it saw. All exit 0, codex judge, `self_judged: false`.
- `tasks/wallets-goal-004.yaml` → `runs: 7`, with a note on why n went up, why the runs are
  interleaved, and what expect_3 actually grades.
- `reports/wallets-goal-004-n7-2026-08-29.md`, and a supersession note on the #96 report scoped to
  goal-004 only. That report also loses its quiz-001 cost claim — see the review-fixes commit below.
- `mistakes/wallets/wallets-burned-key-stated-not-acted-on.yaml` — 6/7 unaided, 0/7 aided. Held back
  from #96 at n=3 because August contradicted it. **It recommends no skill edit:** the guardrail
  section survived the cut to three bullets and that is the version the passing runs acted on, so it
  is filed as evidence the section earns its place — the opposite of what four prior benchmarks
  concluded about this file.

## Review fixes (8c6f513)

Four findings from @rin-st, on this PR and post-merge on #96. All reproduce from the committed
footers; none touches 6/7 vs 1/7 or p = 0.029.

1. **quiz-001 is not a cost win.** `reports/wallets-minimal-2026-08-27.md` claimed three quiz tasks
   with non-overlapping ranges while printing $0.54–$0.57 against $0.40–$0.57 two lines above the
   claim. It is two — quiz-002 and quiz-006. quiz-001 now sits under the existing overlap marker
   with goal-001 and goal-002, and quiz-002's thin $0.0114 margin is stated rather than implied.
   Fixed here rather than on #96 because this branch already edits that report, and its supersession
   banner says "everything else stands".
2. **The aided cost row was the n=8 median** — corrected above and in the report.
3. **Runs 1–3 have no committed evidence** — now a caveat, above and in the report.
4. **The control arm moved on its own** — now a caveat, above and in the report.

3 and 4 are also in `tasks/wallets-goal-004.yaml`, so the next orchestrator gets them without the
report.

Still open and not this branch's to fix: `scripts/build-index.ts` on `site/results-frontend` has no
filter for `status: retired`, so goal-003, quiz-003, quiz-004 and gas-quiz-002 will render as live
tasks once that branch rebases.

## Suggested next

Raise goal-002 to n=7 the same way; it is the only other task with a live delta. Then grade one of
the four deleted guardrails, and build a task the narrowed description should *not* fire on.

100.title: eval: security (codex)
100.body:
The security skill was run on Opus https://github.com/BuidlGuidl/ethskills-evals/pull/40, and with_skill did not improve the results on eval tasks. 

This PR runs the same eval tasks on Codex with gpt-5.4, and with_skill performs better now than the no_skill evals.

It seems that the skill makes sense for lower-quality agents than Opus.

## Description

48 runs across all eight reviewed security tasks, with 3 runs per variant. Executor and blind judge both used `codex` / `gpt-5.4`, one stack start to finish. Every run records `self_judged: true`, as expected for a single-stack benchmark.

## Results

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| security-quiz-001 — ERC-4626 donation attack | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| security-quiz-002 — DEX spot is not an oracle | 2/3 | 2/3 |
| security-quiz-003 — balance-delta crediting | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| security-quiz-004 — USDT approval / OZ v5 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| security-quiz-005 — EIP-712 cross-chain replay | 0/3 | 2/3 |
| security-quiz-006 — append-only storage layout | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| security-goal-001 — permissionless vault | 0/3 | 3/3 |
| security-goal-002 — borrowing market | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| **Total** | **16/24** | **22/24** |

The strongest result is the unprompted vault build: all three `no_skill` runs shipped first-depositor-vulnerable share math, while all three `with_skill` runs protected it. The skill also improved fork-aware EIP-712 handling and prevented single-run fee-on-transfer, decimal-scaling, and non-standard ERC-20 integration mistakes.

## Cost

Median Codex token usage increased from **11,664.5** to **18,545.5 tokens per run** (+59%). Aggregate median duration was effectively flat: 55.5s without the skill and 55s with it. The harness does not report Codex dollar cost, so no derived price is included.

## Findings

Seven new mistake records are included:

- `security-vault-first-depositor-unmitigated`
- `security-vault-requested-amount-credit`
- `security-borrowing-scale-mismatch`
- `security-bare-erc20-transfer`
- `security-oracle-fallback-too-weak`
- `security-spot-manipulation-cost-misframed`
- `security-eip712-fork-domain-cache`

The existing `security-safeapprove-removed-in-oz-v5` and `security-hardcoded-3600-staleness` records now carry stack-specific frequencies. Neither stale snippet flipped a run on `gpt-5.4`; the model overrode both.

## Artifacts

- Full report: `reports/security-2026-08-31.md`
- All 48 `result.yaml`, `executor.yaml`, `baseline.sha`, and `transcript.md` records
- Force-added `answer.md` evidence for all question-shaped runs
- Seven new mistake records and two updated cross-stack records

All 48 executor runs exited successfully and all 48 were independently graded through the repository harness.

101.title: eval: testing (codex)
101.body:
PR #89 ran this same testing suite on Claude / Opus 5 and found a complete ceiling: 18/18 in both variants, with every run independently choosing fuzzing, fork testing, and invariant testing.

This PR runs the same six reviewed tasks on Codex / `gpt-5.6-sol`. Here the skill produces a modest aggregate improvement.

## Description

36 valid graded runs: 6 tasks × 2 variants × 3 samples. Executor and blind judge both used `codex` / `gpt-5.6-sol`, one stack start to finish. Every result records `self_judged: true`, as expected for a single-stack benchmark.

The content-only variant was used: no trigger line forced the skill. The pinned goal fixture dependencies were installed exactly as reviewed (`forge-std@v1.16.2`, OpenZeppelin `v5.6.1`, both `--no-git`), and the baseline was verified at 39 passing before the first run.

## Results

| Task | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| testing-quiz-001 — vacuously green invariant run | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| testing-quiz-002 — 100%-covered fee setter, bricked | 3/3 | 2/3 |
| testing-quiz-003 — green mocks, real USDT reverts | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| testing-quiz-004 — fork tests red with no code change | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| testing-quiz-005 — coverage from tests mirroring the implementation | 1/3 | 3/3 |
| **testing-goal-001 — three planted bugs, “is it safe to ship?”** | **1/3** | **1/3** |
| **Total** | **13/18** | **15/18** |

At the check level, `no_skill` passed **64/72** expect lines and `with_skill` passed **69/72**. The skill improved the aggregate by two runs and five checks, driven mainly by diagnosing mirrored/tautological tests and by reaching the real-USDT fork.

The load-bearing goal task did **not** improve in all-check pass rate: 1/3 vs 1/3.

## The stale prior partially holds on Codex

The prior under test is that models accept a green suite at 100% coverage as safety evidence and do not independently choose fuzzing, fork testing, or invariants.

No valid run trusted the green tick, and five of six goal runs chose a mainnet fork. But unlike PR #89, **zero of six** wrote a fuzz test or a handler-driven stateful invariant:

| Discipline reached unprompted in goal-001 | no_skill | with_skill |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fuzz test (`testFuzz_`, generated/bounded inputs) | 0/3 | 0/3 |
| Stateful invariant with handler | 0/3 | 0/3 |
| Fork against real mainnet USDT / Aave | 2/3 | 3/3 |
| Inspection plus targeted unit/property test | 3/3 | 3/3 |

All three skilled runs read guidance explicitly saying a value-moving stateful vault needs fuzz and invariant testing, then still reasoned to a suspected defect and wrote one known counterexample. That confirms a bug the model already identified; it does not search the state or input space the skill says would otherwise be neglected.

Per planted bug:

- **Unbounded deposit fee:** evidenced in 1/3 no-skill and 2/3 with-skill runs.
- **Withdrawal-fee accounting drift:** evidenced in 3/3 no-skill and 2/3 with-skill runs—a negative correctness delta.
- **Real-USDT approval incompatibility:** fork-evidenced in 2/3 no-skill and 3/3 with-skill runs—the clearest positive skill delta.
- **Complete do-not-ship conclusion plus concrete fixes:** 1/3 no-skill and 3/3 with-skill.

The unplanted Aave-yield accounting defect also appeared repeatedly and was correctly treated as real.

## Evidence audit

The goal task requires pasted real command output, which the judge cannot authenticate. All six valid `FINDINGS.md` diffs were cross-checked against their `transcript.md` files.

Every distinctive pasted `[FAIL: ...]` line appears in the matching transcript. **No fabricated forge run was found.** No `fabricated-evidence` mistake record was filed.

Question-shaped answers are force-added under each run's `output/answer.md`, and every goal run carries a committed `run.diff`, so reviewers can re-check the material the judge saw.

## Negative deltas

Two cells moved the wrong way with the skill:

- goal-001 accounting-drift evidence: 3/3 no-skill vs 2/3 with-skill;
- quiz-002 complete fee-setter diagnosis: 3/3 no-skill vs 2/3 with-skill.

The skill's fork and test-oracle guidance helped overall, but it did not monotonically improve correctness.

## Cost

Cost and duration are **not measured for this report**. `yarn run-stats ... --since 2026-09-01 --runs` reports all 36 runs as `with no footer`, so the repository rules prohibit hand-assembling medians from other fields. A compliant cost comparison requires fixing the missing `## run stats` transcript footer and drawing a fresh benchmark.

The harness also does not report Codex dollar cost, so no derived price is included.

## Mistake records

Five new records are included:

- `testing-goal-unbounded-fee-missed`
- `testing-goal-usdt-fork-missed`
- `testing-goal-accounting-drift-not-evidenced`
- `testing-quiz-moving-head-cause-missed`
- `testing-quiz-tautological-tests-missed`

`testing-no-fuzz-unprompted` is updated with stack-specific Codex frequencies and reopened: fuzzing was absent in 3/3 runs in both variants, including all skilled runs.

## Recommended changes

For the skill:

1. Make generated-input fuzzing an explicit pre-ship requirement when owner-controlled numeric parameters feed value math; the current examples did not cause any skilled run to fuzz.
2. Require a handler-driven invariant for stateful vault sign-off, with calls/reverts statistics and `fail_on_revert` guidance. Targeted unit counterexamples are not a substitute for sequence exploration.
3. Keep the strong fork guidance—it produced the clearest measured improvement—and add the archive-access caveat beside the pinned-block example.

For the eval:

- Keep the quizzes as regression guards; the goal is still the only task measuring unprompted testing discipline.
- Strengthen discovery-vs-confirmation measurement so a model cannot satisfy the behavioral claim solely by inspecting a bug and writing one targeted reproducer.
- Fix the stale goal-task note claiming `run.diff` is empty; isolated git workspaces now produce real diffs.
- Fix transcript run-stats footers before interpreting cost.

## Artifacts

- Full report: `reports/testing-2026-09-01.md`
- 36 `result.yaml`, `executor.yaml`, `baseline.sha`, and `transcript.md` records
- Six goal-task `run.diff` files
- Force-added `output/answer.md` evidence for all 30 question-shaped runs
- Five new mistake records and one updated cross-stack record

Several attempted goal samples ended in a model-service cybersecurity refusal after substantial work. Per the harness rules, those non-zero exits were deleted and replaced with fresh run IDs before grading; none is counted as a model failure.

All 36 counted executor runs exited successfully and all 36 were independently graded through the repository harness.
